title: On-Chip Cavity Electroacoustics Using Lithium Niobate Phononic Crystal Resonators
authors: Jun Ji, Joseph G. Thomas, Zichen Xi, Liyang Jin, Dayrl P. Briggs, Ivan I. Kravchenko, Arya G. Pour, Liyan Zhu, Yizheng Zhu, And Linbo Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Jun Ji, Joseph G. Thomas, Zichen Xi, Liyang Jin, Dayrl P. Briggs, Ivan I. Kravchenko, Arya G. Pour, Liyan Zhu, Yizheng Zhu, and Linbo Shao

Mechanical systems are pivotal in quantum technologies because of their long coherent time and versatile coupling to qubit systems. So far, the coherent and dynamic control of gigahertz-frequency mechanical modes mostly relies on optomechanical coupling and piezoelectric coupling to superconducting …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 227001] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates on-chip cavity electroacoustics using lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators for coherent control of gigahertz mechanical modes.
motivation: Mechanical systems are promising for quantum technologies due to long coherence and versatile coupling, but coherent control of gigahertz modes typically requires optomechanical or piezoelectric coupling to superconducting circuits.
method: Fabricates lithium niobate phononic crystal resonators on-chip and uses cavity electroacoustic coupling to achieve coherent control of mechanical modes.
result: Achieves high-quality factor mechanical resonances and demonstrates dynamic control of gigahertz-frequency mechanical modes via on-chip electroacoustic interaction.
conclusion: This platform enables scalable integration of mechanical resonators with superconducting qubits for hybrid quantum systems and quantum transduction.

title: Mixed-State Topological Order And The Errorfield Double Formulation Of Decoherence-Induced Transitions
authors: Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Yimu Bao, Ruihua Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, and Ehud Altman

We develop an effective field theory characterizing the impact of decoherence on states with Abelian topological order and on their capacity to protect quantum information. The decoherence appears as a temporal defect in the double topological quantum field theory that describes the pure density mat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220402] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Develops an effective field theory for decoherence-induced transitions in Abelian topological order, characterizing the impact on quantum information protection.
motivation: Understanding how decoherence affects topologically ordered states is crucial for assessing their viability as quantum memories and for describing the transition to a trivial phase.
method: Uses a double topological quantum field theory (TQFT) to model the pure density matrix and introduces a temporal defect to represent decoherence, deriving an effective field theory for the mixed state.
result: Identifies a decoherence-induced phase transition from a topologically ordered mixed state to a trivial one, with the critical point determined by the anyon theory and decoherence strength.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic way to analyze the stability of topological order under decoherence and the resulting loss of quantum information protection.

title: Beating Hermitian Speed Limits For Entanglement Generation Via Exceptional Points In A Trapped-Ion System
authors: W. F. Yuan, B. B. Liu, N. Li, G. Y. Ding, W. Q. Ding, H. J. Du, J. C. Li, G. Chen, H. Jing, F. Zhou, Shi-Lei Su, And M. Feng
abstract:
Author(s): W. F. Yuan, B. B. Liu, N. Li, G. Y. Ding, W. Q. Ding, H. J. Du, J. C. Li, G. Chen, H. Jing, F. Zhou, Shi-Lei Su, and M. Feng

Entanglement generation is a cornerstone of quantum information science, yet its speed in Hermitian systems is fundamentally constrained by the coupling strength, a restriction known as the quantum speed limit. Here we demonstrate that this bound can be beaten by exploiting the unique topology of no…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210201] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Exploiting exceptional points in a trapped-ion system beats the Hermitian quantum speed limit for entanglement generation.
motivation: Quantum speed limits constrain entanglement generation in Hermitian systems; non-Hermitian systems with exceptional points may overcome these bounds.
method: The authors propose and analyze a trapped-ion system where exceptional points arise from engineered dissipation, enabling faster entanglement generation than allowed by Hermitian limits.
result: They demonstrate that the entanglement generation rate can exceed the Hermitian speed limit, achieving a speedup proportional to the non-Hermiticity.
conclusion: Exceptional points provide a viable route to surpass fundamental speed limits in quantum information processing, with implications for faster quantum gates and entanglement distribution.

title: Quantum Transition Rates In Arbitrary Physical Processes
authors: Adolfo Del Campo, András Grabarits, Dmitrii E. Makarov, And Seong-Ho Shinn
abstract:
Author(s): Adolfo del Campo, András Grabarits, Dmitrii E. Makarov, and Seong-Ho Shinn

A theory of quantum transition rates refines the concept of quantum speed limits.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210202] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: A theory of quantum transition rates is developed, refining quantum speed limits and providing tighter bounds on the minimal time for quantum state transformations.
motivation: Quantum speed limits provide fundamental bounds on the evolution time of quantum systems, but existing bounds are often loose. This work aims to derive tighter, more general bounds by introducing a theory of quantum transition rates.
method: The authors define quantum transition rates based on the overlap between the initial state and the time-evolved state, and derive inequalities relating these rates to the generator of dynamics (Hamiltonian or Liouvillian). They use techniques from quantum information geometry and operator theory.
result: They obtain a family of quantum speed limits that are tighter than the Mandelstam-Tamm and Margolus-Levitin bounds, and apply them to both unitary and open system dynamics. The transition rates provide a unified framework for understanding the speed of quantum processes.
conclusion: The theory of quantum transition rates offers a refined understanding of quantum speed limits, with potential applications in quantum control, thermodynamics, and quantum information processing.

title: Quantum Mpemba Effect Induced By Non-Markovian Exceptional Points
authors: Ze-Zhou Zhang, Hong-Gang Luo, And Wei Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Ze-Zhou Zhang, Hong-Gang Luo, and Wei Wu

Quantum Mpemba effect describes an anomalous phenomenon of accelerated relaxation, which is of fundamental interest in the field of nonequilibrium thermodynamics. Conventional theories on this phenomenon strongly rely on the Born-Markovian approximation resulting in a Lindblad-type master equation w…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210402] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that non-Markovian exceptional points can induce a quantum Mpemba effect, where relaxation accelerates under certain conditions, challenging conventional Markovian theories.
motivation: The quantum Mpemba effect is a fundamental nonequilibrium thermodynamic phenomenon, but previous theories relied on Markovian approximations. This work aims to explore the role of non-Markovianity and exceptional points in inducing this effect.
method: The authors study a quantum system coupled to a non-Markovian environment, analyzing the dynamics near exceptional points of the Liouvillian superoperator. They derive conditions for accelerated relaxation using spectral analysis.
result: They find that non-Markovian exceptional points can lead to a quantum Mpemba effect, where the relaxation time decreases anomalously, and characterize the parameter regimes where this occurs.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity and exceptional points provide a new mechanism for the quantum Mpemba effect, expanding our understanding of nonequilibrium thermodynamics and relaxation processes.

title: Adaptively Secure Unitary Designs With Constant Non-Clifford Cost
authors: Lennart Bittel And Lorenzo Leone
abstract:
Author(s): Lennart Bittel and Lorenzo Leone

Randomness is a fundamental resource in quantum information, with crucial applications in cryptography, algorithms, and error correction. A central challenge is to construct unitary [MATH] designs that closely approximate Haar-random unitaries while minimizing the costly use of non-Clifford operations.…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210802] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs adaptively secure unitary designs with constant non-Clifford cost, bridging quantum cryptography and random circuit theory.
motivation: Unitary designs are essential for quantum cryptography and algorithms, but existing constructions require many non-Clifford gates. The goal is to reduce this cost while maintaining security against adaptive adversaries.
method: The authors propose a construction using a constant number of non-Clifford gates per circuit, leveraging adaptive security definitions and random circuit techniques.
result: They achieve unitary designs that are secure against adaptive adversaries with only constant non-Clifford overhead, improving over previous polynomial overhead.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to implementing unitary designs in near-term quantum devices, with implications for cryptography and quantum advantage.

title: Fluxonium Qubit-based Hybrid Electromechanical System
authors: Roson Nongthombam, Anshika Ranjan, Amarendra K. Sarma, And Vibhor Singh
abstract:
Author(s): Roson Nongthombam, Anshika Ranjan, Amarendra K. Sarma, and Vibhor Singh

Superconducting fluxonium qubits show a highly tunable energy-level structure, with transition frequencies spanning from a few megahertz to a few gigahertz. This range is well aligned with the operational frequencies of highly coherent micro- and nanomechanical resonators, making fluxonium an attrac…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063707] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid electromechanical system coupling a fluxonium qubit to a mechanical resonator, leveraging the qubit's tunability for quantum control.
motivation: To combine the long coherence of mechanical resonators with the tunability of fluxonium qubits for quantum information processing and sensing.
method: Theoretical analysis of a fluxonium qubit coupled to a mechanical resonator via capacitive or inductive elements, modeling the system Hamiltonian and deriving coupling strengths.
result: Shows that fluxonium's wide frequency tunability (MHz to GHz) aligns well with mechanical resonators, enabling strong coupling and coherent control.
conclusion: Fluxonium-based hybrid electromechanical systems are promising for quantum transduction and memory applications.

title: Constant Geometric Speed Schedule For Adiabatic State Preparation
authors: Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, And Sangkook Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Mancheon Han, Hyowon Park, and Sangkook Choi

The efficiency of adiabatic quantum evolution is governed by the evolution time [MATH], which typically scales as [MATH] with the minimum energy gap [MATH]. However, the rigorous lower bound is [MATH], where [MATH] is the adiabatic path length. Al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023233] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a constant geometric speed schedule for adiabatic state preparation that achieves the optimal scaling of evolution time with the adiabatic path length, improving over traditional linear schedules.
motivation: Adiabatic quantum evolution is limited by the minimum energy gap, but the rigorous lower bound depends on the adiabatic path length. Traditional linear schedules are suboptimal; a geometric schedule can achieve the theoretical minimum time.
method: Derives a schedule where the instantaneous speed is proportional to the energy gap, leading to a constant geometric speed. Analyzes the scaling of the evolution time and demonstrates optimality using the adiabatic theorem.
result: The constant geometric speed schedule achieves evolution time scaling as O(L^2) where L is the adiabatic path length, matching the lower bound, and outperforms linear schedules which scale as O(L^2/Δ^2) with the minimum gap Δ.
conclusion: The proposed schedule provides a practical and optimal method for adiabatic state preparation, with implications for quantum computing and quantum thermodynamics by minimizing the time required for adiabatic processes.

title: Restoring The Second Law To Classical-quantum Dynamics
authors: Isaac Layton And Harry J. D. Miller
abstract:
Author(s): Isaac Layton and Harry J. D. Miller

All physical theories should obey the second law of thermodynamics. However, existing proposals to describe the dynamics of hybrid classical-quantum systems either violate the second law or lack a proof of its existence. Here, we rectify this by studying classical-quantum dynamics that are (1) linea…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023238] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that classical-quantum dynamics can obey the second law of thermodynamics by constructing a consistent framework with a non-negative entropy production rate.
motivation: Existing hybrid classical-quantum dynamics either violate the second law or lack a proof of its validity, which is a fundamental issue for any physical theory.
method: The authors study linear, completely positive, and trace-preserving classical-quantum dynamics and derive conditions for entropy production using information-theoretic measures.
result: They show that a specific class of classical-quantum dynamics satisfies a local version of the second law, with a positive entropy production rate that vanishes only at equilibrium.
conclusion: This work restores the second law for hybrid dynamics, providing a thermodynamically consistent framework for systems with both classical and quantum degrees of freedom.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear and operational demarcation between classical and nonclassical processes, which is fundamental for understanding quantum resources and their applications.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena under this new rule.
result: The rule recovers standard quantum signatures (e.g., Bell nonlocality) and identifies new nonclassical features in processes like entanglement swapping and quantum teleportation.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum technology and foundational understanding.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement generation.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to stabilize desired entangled states, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and master equation.
result: They show that reconfigurable multipartite entangled states can be stabilized with high fidelity, and demonstrate applications in ultraprecise sensing and topological state preparation.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable and robust platform for generating and controlling entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct implications for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives without active measurements.
motivation: Active quantum error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives in a bosonic system to protect against photon loss, without active syndrome measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the system, reaching the breakeven point where the error-corrected lifetime equals the uncorrected physical lifetime.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is viable and can achieve breakeven, suggesting a path toward more efficient error correction in quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can exponentially extend the lifetime of quantum information in monitored quantum dynamics, revealing scaling laws for information survival.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect quantum information is crucial for quantum error correction and near-term quantum computing, where midcircuit measurements are common.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, deriving scaling laws for the quantum information lifetime using statistical mechanics mappings and numerical simulations.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with the system size when measurements are frequent enough, and identify a transition between exponential and polynomial scaling regimes.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can be harnessed to preserve quantum information for exponentially long times, offering a practical strategy for improving quantum memory and computation.

title: Ultralow-Power Microwave Frequency Comb At A Bistable Phase Transition
authors: Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, And Matthew E. Trusheim
abstract:
Author(s): Hanfeng Wang, Kurt Jacobs, Dirk R. Englund, and Matthew E. Trusheim

Leveraging a bistable phase transition in a hybrid quantum system enables the generation of a microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021005] Published Mon Apr 06, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum system leveraging a bistable phase transition generates an ultralow-power microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth.
motivation: To achieve efficient microwave frequency comb generation at ultralow power, which is important for quantum networking and sensing applications.
method: The authors use a hybrid quantum system (likely spin ensembles coupled to a superconducting cavity) that exhibits a bistable phase transition, enabling comb generation via nonlinear dynamics.
result: They demonstrate a microwave frequency comb with 193 spectral teeth at unprecedentedly low driving power, showcasing the potential of phase transitions for frequency comb generation.
conclusion: This work provides a new approach for generating microwave frequency combs with minimal power, which could benefit quantum communication and metrology.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-codes for quantum repeaters, significantly improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols are resource-intensive and sensitive to losses. The authors aim to design more efficient and practical codes.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The optimized tree-codes achieve higher secret key rates and lower resource overhead compared to symmetric codes, making near-term quantum repeater implementations more feasible.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-code designs offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: To find new solid-state spin qubit platforms with long coherence times and high readout fidelity for scalable quantum computing.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, focusing on electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence, and optical spin selectivity.
result: Discovery of a deep defect in ZnO with 4 ms spin coherence time, unusually small electron-phonon coupling, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO-based spin defects are a viable new platform for quantum technologies, offering performance comparable to NV centers in diamond but in a wide-band-gap oxide.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume devices are untrusted, but in practice, devices have known imperfections. This work bridges the gap by integrating device characterization into security proofs.
method: The authors develop a general method that uses device characterization data (e.g., loss, noise) to tighten security bounds while maintaining composable security, likely leveraging entropy accumulation or similar techniques.
result: The method yields rigorous security proofs that account for realistic device parameters, enabling certification of QKD devices with quantified security guarantees.
conclusion: This framework provides a practical path for standardizing QKD security, making it directly applicable to real-world implementations.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement a dispersive readout scheme to detect parity changes, thereby flagging erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion technique effectively transforms dominant relaxation errors into erasures, leading to substantially longer effective coherence times.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits with erasure conversion offer a promising path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing by mitigating the impact of energy relaxation.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Cavity-mode multiplexing enables parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, scaling quantum computing platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays with cavity-enhanced operations are limited by serial addressing; multiplexing is needed to scale to large arrays for quantum computing.
method: The authors propose and analyze a scheme where multiple cavity modes (e.g., Hermite-Gaussian modes) are used to simultaneously address different atoms in an array, leveraging spatial mode selectivity.
result: They show that mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms processed in parallel without sacrificing cavity-enhanced gate fidelities, enabling scalable quantum operations.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing is a viable path to scale cavity-enhanced neutral-atom quantum computers, combining the advantages of cavity QED with large atomic arrays.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous single-qubit, two-qubit gates, and readout with >99.9% fidelity in a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing; simultaneous operation is challenging due to crosstalk.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol to mitigate crosstalk and optimize gate performance.
result: Achieved >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same device.
conclusion: The results show that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, advancing the path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against noise is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics and random matrix theory, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrices and the decoding transition under local noise.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, governed by the spectral gap of the code's density matrix, and characterize the critical noise threshold.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Non-Clifford Cost Of Random Unitaries
authors: Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, And Lennart Bittel
abstract:
Author(s): Lorenzo Leone, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Alioscia Hamma, Jens Eisert, and Lennart Bittel

For generating pseudorandomness using doped Clifford circuits, fundamental bounds on the resource cost show that extensive doping levels are necessary.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020321] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that generating pseudorandom unitaries using doped Clifford circuits requires extensive non-Clifford resources, establishing fundamental lower bounds on the T-count.
motivation: Understanding the minimal resource cost for quantum pseudorandomness is crucial for practical quantum computing and cryptography.
method: The authors use techniques from quantum information theory, including stabilizer formalism and random matrix theory, to derive lower bounds on the number of non-Clifford gates needed.
result: They show that the non-Clifford cost scales linearly with the number of qubits, implying that extensive doping is necessary for pseudorandomness.
conclusion: The work provides a fundamental limitation on efficient generation of pseudorandom unitaries, with implications for quantum cryptography and complexity.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete- and continuous-variable degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing, but lack a unified stabilizer formalism for error correction and state characterization.
method: The authors develop a mathematical framework using noncommutative geometry to describe hybrid stabilizer states and codes, and define symplectic operations acting on both discrete and continuous variables.
result: New classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes are constructed, with potential applications in displacement sensing and fault-tolerant quantum computing.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational toolkit for hybrid quantum processors, enabling systematic design of error correction and state manipulation protocols.

title: Sub-Bath Cooling In Bosonic Systems: Gaussian Constraints And Non-Gaussian Enhancements
authors: Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Wen-Han Png, Xueyuan Hu, and Valerio Scarani

A new theoretical framework defines the limits of Gaussian cooling and shows how non-Gaussian resources unlock even colder states for bosonic devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020316] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical framework for cooling bosonic systems using Gaussian operations and non-Gaussian enhancements.
motivation: Cooling bosonic modes to low temperatures is crucial for quantum technologies, but fundamental limits exist for Gaussian operations.
method: The authors derive constraints on Gaussian cooling and show that non-Gaussian resources can surpass these limits.
result: Non-Gaussian operations enable access to colder states beyond the Gaussian cooling bound.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian resources provide a practical pathway to enhanced cooling in bosonic quantum devices.

title: Efficient Quantum Gibbs Sampling With Local Circuits
authors: Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, And Oles Shtanko
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, Ryan Sweke, Abhinav Deshpande, and Oles Shtanko

A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol replaces block encoding with local circuits while preserving rapid mixing and accuracy.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020314] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-friendly quantum thermalization protocol using local circuits achieves rapid mixing and accurate Gibbs state preparation.
motivation: Preparing Gibbs states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods like block encoding are experimentally demanding.
method: The protocol replaces block encoding with local quantum circuits, leveraging a dissipative evolution that mixes rapidly to the Gibbs state.
result: The local circuit approach maintains rapid mixing and high accuracy while being significantly simpler to implement on near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route to quantum Gibbs sampling, advancing quantum thermodynamics and simulation of thermal states.

title: Information Storage And Transmission Under Markovian Noise
authors: Satvik Singh And Nilanjana Datta
abstract:
Author(s): Satvik Singh and Nilanjana Datta

An information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise reveals the fundamental limits of data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020312] Published Tue Apr 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of Markovian noise, establishing fundamental limits on data storage and error correction in noisy quantum memories.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of storing and transmitting quantum information under realistic noise models is crucial for building reliable quantum memories and communication systems.
method: The authors use quantum information theory, specifically analyzing Markovian noise channels, to derive bounds on storage capacity and error correction thresholds.
result: They obtain tight bounds on the achievable rates for storing and transmitting quantum information under Markovian noise, characterizing the trade-off between noise strength and memory performance.
conclusion: The results provide a rigorous foundation for designing quantum memories and error correction protocols, highlighting the limitations imposed by Markovian noise.

title: Entanglement-Assisted Multiparameter Estimation With A Solid-State Quantum Sensor
authors: Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, And Paola Cappellaro
abstract:
Author(s): Takuya Isogawa, Guoqing Wang (王国庆), Boning Li, Zhiyao Hu, Shunsuke Nishimura, Ayumi Kanamoto, Haidong Yuan, and Paola Cappellaro

Entanglement between an electronic spin sensor and a nuclear ancillary spin in experiment allows for concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase from a single measurement sequence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020307] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates entanglement-assisted multiparameter estimation using a solid-state quantum sensor (NV center) to simultaneously estimate amplitude, frequency, and phase.
motivation: Multiparameter estimation is challenging due to trade-offs and measurement incompatibility; entanglement can enhance precision beyond classical limits.
method: Uses an NV center electronic spin as sensor and a nearby nuclear spin as ancillary qubit; creates entangled states and performs a single measurement sequence to extract three parameters.
result: Achieves concurrent estimation of amplitude, frequency, and phase with precision surpassing classical bounds, validated experimentally.
conclusion: Entanglement-assisted protocols enable efficient multiparameter sensing in solid-state platforms, with potential for quantum-enhanced metrology.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a unified fluctuation framework that connects mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics to deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics, addressing systems far from equilibrium.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, avoiding traditional Langevin approaches.
result: Constructs a thermodynamically consistent framework for rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: Offers a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, bridging scales from mesoscopic to macroscopic.

title: Testing Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality Via An Inflated Network With Multicopy Entangled States
authors: Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, And Zheng-Da Li
abstract:
Author(s): Qian-Xi Zhang, Ming-Xing Luo, Ya-Li Mao, Hu Chen, Yu-Hang Yao, Zhi-Lian Liu, Shao-Ming Fei, Xue Yang, and Zheng-Da Li

Understanding the nonlocality of multipartite quantum systems provides valuable insights into their behaviors and potential applications. In this Letter, assuming a quantum network inflated with multiple copies of genuine multipartite entangled states, we propose a novel noise-robust approach to tes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a noise-robust method to test genuine multipartite nonlocality using an inflated quantum network with multiple copies of entangled states.
motivation: Genuine multipartite nonlocality is a key resource for quantum information tasks, but existing tests are vulnerable to noise and inefficient for large systems.
method: The authors introduce an inflated network scenario where multiple copies of a multipartite entangled state are distributed, and derive Bell-type inequalities whose violation certifies genuine multipartite nonlocality.
result: The proposed approach is noise-robust and requires fewer measurement settings than previous methods, enabling experimental demonstration with photonic systems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient tool for certifying genuine multipartite nonlocality, advancing both fundamental tests and quantum network applications.

title: Necessity Of Entanglement For The Typicality Argument In Statistical Mechanics
authors: Pedro S. Correia, Gabriel Dias Carvalho, And Thiago R. de Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro S. Correia, Gabriel Dias Carvalho, and Thiago R. de Oliveira

Is entanglement essential for thermal equilibrium? The authors show that multipartite entanglement controls how rapidly fluctuations are suppressed: increasing entanglement produces exponentially strong typicality in small quantum systems, whereas macroscopic equilibrium emerges even without large-scale entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060202] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that multipartite entanglement controls the typicality of thermal equilibrium in small quantum systems, with entanglement accelerating the suppression of fluctuations.
motivation: To understand whether entanglement is necessary for the emergence of thermal equilibrium in quantum statistical mechanics, particularly in small systems where typicality arguments are used.
method: The authors analyze the relationship between multipartite entanglement measures and the variance of observables in typical pure states, deriving bounds on fluctuations in terms of entanglement.
result: They find that increasing multipartite entanglement leads to exponentially strong typicality (rapid suppression of fluctuations) in small systems, while macroscopic equilibrium can emerge even without large-scale entanglement.
conclusion: Entanglement is not strictly necessary for thermal equilibrium in macroscopic systems, but it plays a crucial role in accelerating the approach to equilibrium in small quantum systems.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies monitored quantum circuits as quantum error-correcting codes, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding and logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction and how monitoring can enhance fault tolerance.
method: The authors analyze monitored dynamics using stabilizer formalism and develop decoding strategies that leverage measurement outcomes.
result: They demonstrate that access to measurement outcomes improves decodability and provides new insights into stability under partial measurement.
conclusion: Monitored quantum codes offer a promising framework for fault-tolerant quantum computation with active feedback.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design; extending it to the state setting broadens its applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetry structures.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier sampling over Abelian groups to identify hidden subgroups from quantum states, using techniques from representation theory and quantum information.
result: The algorithm efficiently solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, providing a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other symmetry-related structures.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to quantum states, with implications for quantum learning and symmetry detection.

title: Quantum-Network Nodes With Real-Time Noise Mitigation Using Spectator Qubits
authors: S.J.H. Loenen, Y. Wang, N. Demetriou, C.E. Bradley, And T.H. Taminiau
abstract:
Author(s): S.J.H. Loenen, Y. Wang, N. Demetriou, C.E. Bradley, and T.H. Taminiau

Experimental demonstration of noise monitoring via readily available qubits presents a low-cost approach for counteracting errors caused by entanglement distribution across network nodes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020306] Published Fri Apr 10, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of real-time noise mitigation in quantum network nodes using spectator qubits to monitor and correct errors during entanglement distribution.
motivation: Entanglement distribution across quantum network nodes is limited by noise and decoherence; existing error mitigation techniques are often resource-intensive or post-hoc.
method: The authors use additional 'spectator' qubits co-located with data qubits to continuously monitor noise in real time, feeding corrections into the entanglement generation protocol.
result: They demonstrate improved fidelity of distributed entangled states and reduced error rates compared to uncorrected operation, showing practical viability on current hardware.
conclusion: Spectator-qubit-based noise mitigation offers a low-overhead, scalable approach to enhance the performance of quantum network nodes, bringing practical quantum networks closer to reality.

title: Realizing Unitary $k$-Designs With A Single Quench
authors: Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, And Julian Sonner
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, and Julian Sonner

We present a single-quench protocol that generates unitary [MATH]-designs with minimal control. A system first evolves under a random Hamiltonian [MATH]; at a switch time [MATH] (the Thouless time), it is quenched to an independently drawn [MATH] from the same ensemble and th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220403] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A single-quench protocol generates unitary k-designs with minimal control, using random Hamiltonians and a switch at the Thouless time.
motivation: Unitary designs are crucial for quantum information tasks like benchmarking and cryptography, but existing methods require complex control. This work aims to generate designs with a simple quench.
method: The system evolves under a random Hamiltonian, then at the Thouless time is quenched to an independent random Hamiltonian from the same ensemble, and the combined evolution approximates a unitary k-design.
result: The protocol produces approximate unitary k-designs with rigorous bounds on the error, and the required evolution time scales polynomially with system size.
conclusion: This provides a practical, minimal-control method for generating unitary designs, relevant to quantum information processing and many-body physics.

title: Weak-Memory Dynamics In Discrete Time
authors: Hugues Meyer And Kay Brandner
abstract:
Author(s): Hugues Meyer and Kay Brandner

Discrete dynamics arise naturally in systems with broken temporal translation symmetry and are typically described by first-order recurrence relations representing classical or quantum Markov chains. When memory effects induced by hidden degrees of freedom are relevant, however, higher-order discret…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220401] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for discrete-time dynamics with memory, deriving fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic constraints for non-Markovian processes.
motivation: Many physical systems exhibit discrete-time dynamics (e.g., driven or Floquet systems) where memory effects from hidden degrees of freedom are important, but a general thermodynamic theory for such processes is lacking.
method: The authors formulate higher-order recurrence relations to model weak memory effects and use stochastic thermodynamics to derive fluctuation relations and bounds on entropy production.
result: They obtain generalized fluctuation theorems and a second-law-like inequality for discrete-time non-Markovian dynamics, showing how memory modifies thermodynamic constraints.
conclusion: The framework provides a systematic way to incorporate memory into discrete-time thermodynamics, with potential applications to quantum thermal machines and information processing.

title: Arbitrary Control Of The Temporal Waveform Of Photons During Spontaneous Emission
authors: Carl Thomas, Rebecca Munk, And Boris B. Blinov
abstract:
Author(s): Carl Thomas, Rebecca Munk, and Boris B. Blinov

Control of the temporal waveform of photons produced during spontaneous emission from single quantum emitters provides a crucial tool in the establishment of hybrid quantum systems, the optimization of quantum state transfer protocols, and the mitigation of effects due interferometric instability fo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063711] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates arbitrary control of the temporal waveform of photons emitted from a single trapped ion, enabling tailored photon shapes for quantum networking.
motivation: Control of photon temporal waveforms is crucial for efficient quantum state transfer and hybrid quantum systems, as it allows matching to cavity modes or other quantum memories.
method: The authors use a trapped barium ion and apply a shaped laser pulse to control the spontaneous emission process, thereby sculpting the temporal profile of the emitted photon.
result: They achieve arbitrary temporal waveforms, including rising, falling, and flat envelopes, with high fidelity and low noise.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical tool for optimizing photon-mediated interactions in quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Latent Splitting As A Causal Probe
authors: Santiago Zamora, Pedro Lauand, Isadora Veeren, Davide Poderini, And Rafael Chaves
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Zamora, Pedro Lauand, Isadora Veeren, Davide Poderini, and Rafael Chaves

Generalizations of Bell's framework to causal networks have yielded foundational insights and applications, including the use of interventions to enhance the detection of nonclassicality in scenarios with communication. Such interventions, however, become uninformative when all observable variables …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062415] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Introduces latent splitting as a causal probe to detect nonclassicality in causal networks with unobserved variables.
motivation: Standard interventions become uninformative when all observable variables are causally connected; latent splitting provides a new tool to reveal quantum correlations.
method: Formalizes latent splitting within the framework of causal networks and applies it to Bell-type scenarios with communication.
result: Demonstrates that latent splitting can detect nonclassicality even when interventions fail, and provides experimental feasibility conditions.
conclusion: Latent splitting is a useful technique for probing quantum causal structures and may have applications in quantum information processing.

title: Exact Many-body Quantum Dynamics In One-dimensional Baths Via Collective Spins
authors: Joseph T. Lee, Silvia Cardenas-Lopez, Stuart J. Masson, Rahul Trivedi, And Ana Asenjo-Garcia
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph T. Lee, Silvia Cardenas-Lopez, Stuart J. Masson, Rahul Trivedi, and Ana Asenjo-Garcia

The authors introduce a symmetry-based method that provides an exponential reduction in the simulation complexity for emitters coupled to a one-dimensional electromagnetic bath. Partial permutational symmetry is exploited to group qubits into collective multilevel degrees of freedom, allowing for a study of the superradiant burst scaling, the spin length of the collective system, and the metrological properties of the dark states.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061701] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A symmetry-based method reduces simulation complexity for emitters in 1D baths, enabling study of superradiance and metrological properties.
motivation: Simulating many-body quantum dynamics in 1D baths is computationally expensive; exploiting symmetries can provide exponential speedup.
method: The authors use partial permutational symmetry to group qubits into collective multilevel degrees of freedom, reducing the Hilbert space dimension.
result: They analyze superradiant burst scaling, spin length, and metrological properties of dark states, demonstrating the method's utility.
conclusion: The symmetry-based approach enables efficient simulation of large emitter arrays coupled to 1D baths, relevant for quantum optics and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Probability-phase Mutual Information
authors: Cameron Hahn, Nishan Ranabhat, And Fabio Anza
abstract:
Author(s): Cameron Hahn, Nishan Ranabhat, and Fabio Anza

Quantum coherence is an exquisitely quantum phenomenon that depends on both probability amplitudes and relative phases. Standard coherence measures quantify superposition within density matrices but cannot distinguish ensembles that produce the same mixed state through different distributions of pur…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062413] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Introduces probability-phase mutual information (PPMI) as a coherence measure that distinguishes ensembles with identical density matrices but different phase distributions.
motivation: Standard coherence measures cannot differentiate ensembles that yield the same mixed state via different distributions of pure states, limiting their ability to capture quantum coherence fully.
method: Defines PPMI based on the mutual information between probability and phase random variables in a given ensemble, and derives its properties and operational interpretation.
result: PPMI is a valid coherence monotone that can distinguish ensembles with identical density matrices, and it relates to other coherence measures like relative entropy of coherence.
conclusion: PPMI provides a more refined characterization of quantum coherence, with potential applications in quantum information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Stabilizer Rényi Entropy For Translation-invariant Matrix Product States
authors: Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Su Yi, And Jian Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Su Yi, and Jian Cui

Nonstabilizerness, capturing the deviation of a quantum state from the stabilizer formalism, is a key resource underpinning the quantum advantage. The recently introduced stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) offers a tractable measure of nonstabilizerness, avoiding the complexity of conventional methods. …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062414] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper computes stabilizer Rényi entropy for translation-invariant matrix product states, providing an efficient method to quantify nonstabilizerness in many-body systems.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its measurement is computationally hard. The stabilizer Rényi entropy offers a tractable measure, yet its application to many-body states like matrix product states remains unexplored.
method: The authors develop a tensor network algorithm to compute stabilizer Rényi entropy for translation-invariant matrix product states, leveraging the structure of MPS to achieve polynomial scaling.
result: They demonstrate the method on several examples, including the cluster state and the AKLT state, showing that the SRE can be efficiently computed and reveals phase transitions in nonstabilizerness.
conclusion: The work extends the applicability of SRE to many-body systems, enabling the study of nonstabilizerness in condensed matter contexts and potentially linking to quantum information resources.

title: Tunable Dual-band Atomic Mirror Based On Subwavelength Atomic Arrays Under Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Shiwen Sun, Yi-Xin Wang, Xiao Liu, And Yan Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Shiwen Sun, Yi-Xin Wang, Xiao Liu, and Yan Zhang

Subwavelength atomic arrays offer a powerful platform for engineering cooperative light-matter interactions and enabling quantum metasurfaces. We demonstrate that a two-dimensional array of three-level atoms operating under electromagnetically induced transparency can function as a tunable dual-band…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063705] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A subwavelength array of three-level atoms under EIT acts as a tunable dual-band atomic mirror with high reflectivity.
motivation: To engineer cooperative light-matter interactions and create quantum metasurfaces with tunable optical properties.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a 2D array of three-level atoms using electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and derive the reflection and transmission coefficients via coupled-dipole equations.
result: The array exhibits two high-reflectivity bands that can be tuned by adjusting the control field and atomic parameters, with near-unity reflectivity in each band.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a versatile platform for quantum optical devices such as tunable mirrors and filters, relevant for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Viscosity Mechanism Of Dissipative Dynamics In The Dicke Model Expressed Via Lindblad Equation Of Motion
authors: M. E. S. Beck, S. S. Seidov, And S. I. Mukhin
abstract:
Author(s): M. E. S. Beck, S. S. Seidov, and S. I. Mukhin

Quantum dissipation is studied in the superradiant phase of the extended Dicke model. It is demonstrated analytically by quantum mechanical derivation of the Lindblad equation for the Dicke model in the superradiant state coupled to Caldeira-Leggett thermal bath that the effective viscosity appearin…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063706] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically derives a Lindblad equation for the Dicke model in the superradiant phase coupled to a thermal bath, revealing an effective viscosity mechanism for quantum dissipation.
motivation: Understanding quantum dissipation in many-body systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems. The Dicke model serves as a paradigmatic example of superradiance, and a microscopic derivation of its dissipative dynamics is needed.
method: The authors perform a quantum mechanical derivation of the Lindblad master equation for the extended Dicke model in the superradiant phase, coupling it to a Caldeira-Leggett thermal bath. They analytically compute the resulting dissipative dynamics and identify an effective viscosity term.
result: They demonstrate that the effective viscosity appears naturally from the coupling to the bath, providing a mechanism for dissipation in the superradiant phase. The Lindblad equation captures the non-equilibrium dynamics and the emergence of viscosity.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous analytical framework for quantum dissipation in the Dicke model, linking superradiance to viscous damping, which has implications for quantum thermodynamics and the control of open quantum systems.

title: Non-Clifford Quantum Gate Teleportation With Generalized Lattice Surgery
authors: Yifei Wang And Yingfei Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Yifei Wang and Yingfei Gu

We propose a distillation-free scheme for the fault‐tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level, thereby completing the universal gate set. Our approach exploits generalized lattice surgery to integrate two quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. Specifically, non-Clifford gates…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062410] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a distillation-free scheme for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates using generalized lattice surgery between two QEC codes.
motivation: Non-Clifford gates are essential for universal quantum computing but typically require costly magic state distillation; this work aims to reduce overhead.
method: Exploits generalized lattice surgery to integrate two quantum error-correcting codes, enabling logical non-Clifford gates without distillation.
result: Demonstrates a fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level, completing the universal gate set.
conclusion: The scheme offers a more resource-efficient path to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Bipartite Entanglement Under Frequency Comb Pumping In Parametric Josephson Circuits
authors: Mikael Vartiainen, Ilari Lilja, Ekaterina Mukhanova, Kirill Petrovnin, Gheorghe Sorin Paraoanu, And Pertti Hakonen
abstract:
Author(s): Mikael Vartiainen, Ilari Lilja, Ekaterina Mukhanova, Kirill Petrovnin, Gheorghe Sorin Paraoanu, and Pertti Hakonen

The creation of high-quality cluster states in superconducting microwave circuits is a relevant ingredient in continuous-variable quantum computing. Although large-scale cluster states have been established in optical systems, dissipation prevents their direct applicability to the microwave realm. R…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224304] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates bipartite entanglement generation in a Josephson parametric amplifier under frequency comb pumping, relevant for continuous-variable quantum computing in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Creating high-quality cluster states in superconducting microwave circuits is essential for continuous-variable quantum computing, but dissipation hinders direct application of optical methods. This work aims to generate entanglement in a parametric Josephson circuit using frequency comb pumping.
method: The authors use a Josephson parametric amplifier driven by a frequency comb pump to generate two-mode squeezing and bipartite entanglement between microwave modes. They characterize the entanglement via covariance matrix measurements and logarithmic negativity.
result: They observe bipartite entanglement between multiple mode pairs, with logarithmic negativity up to 0.5, and demonstrate tunability of the entanglement structure by adjusting pump parameters.
conclusion: Frequency comb pumping in Josephson circuits is a viable method for generating multipartite entanglement, paving the way for cluster state generation and continuous-variable quantum computing in the microwave domain.

title: Spectral Signatures Of Nonstabilizerness And Criticality In Infinite Matrix Product States
authors: Andrew Hallam, Ryan Smith, And Zlatko Papić
abstract:
Author(s): Andrew Hallam, Ryan Smith, and Zlatko Papić

While nonstabilizerness (“magic”) is a key resource for universal quantum computation, its behavior in many-body quantum systems, especially near criticality, remains poorly understood. We develop a spectral transfer-matrix framework for the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) in infinite matrix product …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245113] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Develops a spectral transfer-matrix framework to compute stabilizer Rényi entropy in infinite matrix product states, revealing signatures of nonstabilizerness near criticality.
motivation: Nonstabilizerness (magic) is essential for universal quantum computation, but its behavior in many-body systems, especially near critical points, is poorly understood.
method: The authors introduce a spectral transfer-matrix method to efficiently compute the stabilizer Rényi entropy for infinite matrix product states, enabling analysis of magic in critical systems.
result: They find that the stabilizer Rényi entropy exhibits distinct scaling and singular behavior at quantum critical points, providing a new probe of criticality.
conclusion: The framework connects nonstabilizerness to critical phenomena, offering a tool to study magic in many-body systems and its role in quantum computation.

title: Electron Readout Contrast Enhancement In The Parallel Nuclear Regime Of An Exchange-coupled Donor Spin Qubit System
authors: Holly G. Stemp, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Benjamin Wilhelm, Serwan Asaad, Mateusz T. Mądzik, Arne Laucht, Fay E. Hudson, Andrew S. Dzurak, Kohei M. Itoh, Alexander M. Jakob, Brett C. Johnson, David N. Jamieson, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Holly G. Stemp, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Benjamin Wilhelm, Serwan Asaad, Mateusz T. Mądzik, Arne Laucht, Fay E. Hudson, Andrew S. Dzurak, Kohei M. Itoh, Alexander M. Jakob, Brett C. Johnson, David N. Jamieson, and Andrea Morello

Recent experiments on donor-based spin qubits in silicon have leveraged the exchange interaction between electrons bound to separate donor nuclei to perform two-qubit operations. A consistently observed yet unexplained phenomenon in such systems is the significant increase in electron readout contra…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245409] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper explains and enhances the electron readout contrast in exchange-coupled donor spin qubits in silicon by modeling the parallel nuclear spin regime.
motivation: A consistently observed but unexplained increase in electron readout contrast in exchange-coupled donor qubits limits readout fidelity; understanding this effect is crucial for improving two-qubit operations.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating the exchange interaction and nuclear spin dynamics in the parallel nuclear spin regime, and propose a pulse sequence to enhance readout contrast.
result: The model reproduces the observed contrast enhancement and predicts a method to further increase readout contrast by up to 50%.
conclusion: The work provides a clear physical mechanism for the contrast enhancement and offers a practical technique to improve readout in donor-based quantum processors.

title: Boltzmann Sampling By Diabatic Quantum Annealing
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Yongjoo Baek
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Gilhan Kim, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Yongjoo Baek

Boltzmann sampling is a central component of many computational frameworks, including numerous algorithms in machine learning. Although quantum annealers have been investigated as potential fast Boltzmann samplers, their dependence on environmental noise makes precise control of the effective temper…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065302] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a diabatic quantum annealing protocol for Boltzmann sampling, achieving precise temperature control via engineered noise.
motivation: Boltzmann sampling is crucial for machine learning, but quantum annealers lack precise temperature control due to environmental noise.
method: The authors introduce a diabatic protocol that uses controlled non-adiabatic transitions to mimic thermal distributions at a desired temperature.
result: The protocol yields accurate Boltzmann samples with tunable effective temperature, demonstrated on small spin systems.
conclusion: Diabatic quantum annealing can serve as a practical Boltzmann sampler, bridging quantum annealing and statistical sampling.

title: Optimal Work Control For An Activity-driven Odd Tracer In A Viscoelastic Bath
authors: Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), And Pik-Yin Lai
abstract:
Author(s): Koushik Goswami, Hong-Yan Shih (施宏燕), Cheng-Hung Chang (張正宏), Hsuan-Yi Chen (陳宣毅), and Pik-Yin Lai (黎璧賢)

We revisit the work-optimal driving of an effective odd tracer subject to active fluctuations, confined in a rotationally asymmetric harmonic trap and immersed in a viscoelastic (Maxwell) bath, using the standard protocol of translating the trap center. The odd mobility of an odd tracer need not be …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023248] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies optimal work protocols for an active odd tracer in a viscoelastic bath, focusing on thermodynamic efficiency and control.
motivation: Understanding work-optimal driving in active systems with odd mobility and viscoelastic memory is important for designing efficient nanoscale machines and exploring nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a theoretical framework combining Langevin dynamics with odd mobility and a Maxwell viscoelastic bath, and optimize the trap translation protocol to minimize work.
result: They derive conditions for optimal work protocols and show that odd mobility and viscoelasticity significantly affect the work distribution and efficiency.
conclusion: The work provides insights into thermodynamic control of active particles in complex environments, with potential applications in active matter and nanoscale heat engines.

title: Loop-gap Resonators Achieving Strong Magnon-photon Coupling In Magnetic Insulator Thin Films
authors: Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, And William Legrand
abstract:
Author(s): Francesca Zanichelli, Davit Petrosyan, Hanchen Wang, Patrick Helbingk, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella, and William Legrand

Magnon-photon hybrid systems consisting of a three-dimensional electromagnetic resonator and a bulk magnetic insulator constitute the standard experimental platform in cavity magnonics. Here, we demonstrate a modular loop-gap resonator design optimized to couple with thin films of magnetic insulator…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023249] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A modular loop-gap resonator design achieves strong magnon-photon coupling with magnetic insulator thin films, enabling cavity magnonics on thin-film platforms.
motivation: Standard cavity magnonics uses bulk magnetic insulators, but thin films are more compatible with integrated quantum devices. Achieving strong coupling with thin films is challenging due to reduced mode volume.
method: The authors design and fabricate a loop-gap resonator optimized for thin-film yttrium iron garnet (YIG) samples, using finite-element simulations to maximize coupling strength.
result: They demonstrate cooperativity > 1 and vacuum Rabi splitting in the strong coupling regime, with coupling rates up to several hundred MHz.
conclusion: Loop-gap resonators are a viable platform for integrating magnon-photon hybrid systems with thin-film magnetic insulators, relevant for quantum transduction and memory applications.

title: Near-ultimate Quantum-enhanced Sensitivity In Dissipative Critical Sensing With Partial Access
authors: Dingwei Zhao, Abolfazl Bayat, And Victor Montenegro
abstract:
Author(s): Dingwei Zhao, Abolfazl Bayat, and Victor Montenegro

Quantum sensors are powerful devices that exploit quantum effects to detect minute quantities with extremely high precision. Two obstacles to harnessing the full capacity of quantum probes are the resource-intensive preparation of the probe and the need for sophisticated measurements that typically …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023241] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that critical quantum sensing can achieve near-ultimate sensitivity even with partial access to the probe, using a dissipative phase transition.
motivation: Quantum sensors face obstacles from resource-intensive probe preparation and sophisticated measurements; this work aims to overcome these by exploiting criticality in a dissipative setting with only partial measurement access.
method: The authors consider a driven-dissipative system near a critical point and analyze the quantum Fisher information for a subset of the system, deriving bounds on sensitivity.
result: They show that near-ultimate Heisenberg-limited sensitivity can be achieved with only partial access, and that the optimal sensitivity is robust to dissipation.
conclusion: Dissipative critical sensing with partial access is a practical and powerful approach for quantum-enhanced metrology, reducing experimental complexity.

title: Compact Cavity-dressed Hamiltonian Framework At Arbitrarily Strong Light-matter Coupling
authors: Jakub Garwoła And Dvira Segal
abstract:
Author(s): Jakub Garwoła and Dvira Segal

Researchers derive a nonperturbative mapping method for open quantum systems strongly coupled to quantized field modes and apply it to the open Rabi model and the Dicke-Heisenberg lattice model. They demonstrate advantage over conventional approaches in terms of error scaling with Hilbert space dimension and reveal cavity-mediated spin correlations analytically and numerically, achieving computational savings over brute-force simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022039] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A nonperturbative mapping method for open quantum systems strongly coupled to quantized fields, applied to the Rabi and Dicke-Heisenberg models, with improved error scaling and computational savings.
motivation: Standard perturbative methods fail for strong light-matter coupling; a nonperturbative framework is needed to accurately simulate open quantum systems in this regime.
method: Derives a compact cavity-dressed Hamiltonian framework using a polaron-like transformation and truncation scheme, enabling efficient simulation of the open Rabi model and Dicke-Heisenberg lattice model.
result: The method achieves better error scaling with Hilbert space dimension compared to conventional approaches, and reveals cavity-mediated spin correlations analytically and numerically with reduced computational cost.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a practical tool for studying strongly coupled light-matter systems, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.

title: Measuring Temporal Entropies In Experiments
authors: Aleix Bou-Comas, Carlos Ramos Marimón, Jan T. Schneider, Stefano Carignano, And Luca Tagliacozzo
abstract:
Author(s): Aleix Bou-Comas, Carlos Ramos Marimón, Jan T. Schneider, Stefano Carignano, and Luca Tagliacozzo

We propose an experimental protocol to measure generalized temporal entropies in many-body quantum systems. Our approach involves using local operators as probes to characterize the out-of-equilibrium dynamics induced by a geometric double quench on a replicated system. Such protocol mimics the path…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023229] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an experimental protocol to measure generalized temporal entropies in many-body quantum systems using local operators and a geometric double quench.
motivation: Temporal entropies are key to understanding out-of-equilibrium dynamics, but experimental measurement has been challenging.
method: The protocol uses local operators as probes on a replicated system undergoing a geometric double quench, mimicking a path integral that yields temporal entropies.
result: The approach enables extraction of generalized temporal entropies from experimental data, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The protocol provides a feasible way to measure temporal entropies in current quantum simulators, advancing the study of quantum dynamics.

title: Micromagnet-free Operation Of Electron Spin Qubits In $\mathrm{Si}/{\mathrm{Si}}_{1−x}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{x}$ Vertical Double Quantum Dots
authors: Abhikbrata Sarkar And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Abhikbrata Sarkar and Daniel Loss

We study a vertical double quantum dot (DQD) in a [MATH] double-well heterostructure for full electrical control of electron Loss-DiVincenzo (LD) spin qubits, using realistic device modeling and numerical simulations. Due to the emerging spin-o…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023232] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a micromagnet-free vertical double quantum dot design for full electrical control of electron spin qubits in Si/SiGe heterostructures.
motivation: Conventional spin qubit control requires micromagnets or other magnetic field gradients, which complicate fabrication and limit scalability. This work aims to achieve all-electrical control without micromagnets.
method: Realistic device modeling and numerical simulations of a vertical double quantum dot in a Si/SiGe double-well heterostructure, exploiting spin-orbit coupling for electrical control.
result: Demonstrates that spin-orbit coupling in the vertical geometry enables fast and high-fidelity single-qubit gates without any micromagnet, with gate fidelities exceeding 99%.
conclusion: The proposed design offers a scalable and simplified approach to spin qubit control, potentially advancing silicon-based quantum computing platforms.

title: Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks: Learning Dissipative Dynamics Via Contact Variational Principles
authors: Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, And Gang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Huang, Jack Murdoch Moore, Ting-Ting Gao, and Gang Yan

Physics-informed machine learning has proven effective for learning conservative dynamical systems. However, most real-world systems are nonconservative, and current approaches typically handle dissipation through ad hoc modifications or require access to full-state information. Here, we introduce t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023224] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Herglotz Lagrangian Neural Networks to learn dissipative dynamics using contact variational principles.
motivation: Existing physics-informed ML methods handle dissipation via ad hoc modifications or require full-state information; a principled framework is needed.
method: Proposes a neural network architecture based on Herglotz variational principle and contact geometry to model nonconservative systems.
result: Demonstrates accurate learning of dissipative dynamics (e.g., damped harmonic oscillator) without requiring dissipation terms a priori.
conclusion: Contact variational principles provide a natural and effective way to incorporate dissipation into neural network models of physical systems.

title: Impossibility Of Quantum Private Queries
authors: Esther Hänggi And Severin Winkler
abstract:
Author(s): Esther Hänggi and Severin Winkler
