This work investigates whether quantum communication protocols allow confidential access to a remote database. It shows that any protocol that does not reveal which item is retrieved allows the user to reconstruct the entire database.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022036] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that any quantum protocol for private database queries that hides which item is retrieved necessarily allows the user to reconstruct the entire database, showing the impossibility of quantum private queries.
motivation: Private queries allow a user to retrieve an item from a database without revealing which item was accessed, while the database provider wants to limit the user to only one item. The question is whether quantum communication can achieve this task with better security than classical protocols.
method: The authors analyze general quantum protocols for private queries and derive information-theoretic bounds using the concept of mutual information and the impossibility of hiding the query index while preventing the user from learning more than one item.
result: They show that any protocol that does not reveal the query index to the database allows the user to reconstruct the entire database, i.e., the user can learn all items. This holds even if the protocol uses quantum communication and entanglement.
conclusion: Quantum private queries are impossible under the standard security definition; the only way to prevent the user from obtaining the whole database is to leak the query index, which defeats the purpose of privacy.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems, demonstrated for squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are useful for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with laser-induced spin-motion coupling to engineer arbitrary superpositions of Fock states and squeezed states via a sequence of operations.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: The technique provides a versatile tool for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with applications in quantum information processing and metrology.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD suffers from low secret key rates and limited security proofs; discrete modulation combined with composable security can overcome these limitations.
method: The authors propose a discrete modulation scheme (e.g., QPSK) and derive a composable security proof using entropy accumulation and Gaussian optimality arguments.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 50 km with composable security against collective attacks.
conclusion: The work brings high-speed, secure quantum key distribution closer to practical deployment, especially for metropolitan quantum networks.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable optical readout and manipulation without destroying the circular state.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and coherent control of circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly for quantum networking and hybrid systems.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, revealing Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubit leakage into highly excited states.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and reducing errors in superconducting qubit systems.
method: The authors probe the excited-state dynamics of transmon qubits, analyzing multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions through experimental measurements and theoretical modeling.
result: They identify specific multiphoton resonance conditions that lead to ionization, characterizing the transition rates and energy levels involved.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms, which can inform the design of better readout and error mitigation strategies for superconducting quantum processors.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubits, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit arrays.
method: Experimental study of a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, measuring phase error correlations.
result: Discovery of correlated phase error bursts that persist even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, undermining error correction.
conclusion: New error mitigation strategies are needed to protect superconducting quantum processors from radiation-induced correlated errors.

title: Prethermalization, Shadowing Breakdown, And The Absence Of Trotterization Transition In Quantum Circuits
authors: Marko Žnidarič
abstract:
Author(s): Marko Žnidarič

New research uses truncated propagators to show that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite. It also offers a method to calculate thermalization time, finding that the “Trotterization transition” is generically a finite-size effect.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021017] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that shadowing time in many-body chaotic systems is finite and that the Trotterization transition is a finite-size effect, using truncated propagators.
motivation: Understanding thermalization and prethermalization in quantum circuits is crucial for quantum computing and statistical mechanics.
method: The author uses truncated propagators to analyze shadowing and thermalization times in many-body chaotic systems.
result: Shadowing time is finite, and the Trotterization transition is generically a finite-size effect.
conclusion: The findings clarify the nature of prethermalization and the absence of a true Trotterization transition in the thermodynamic limit.

title: Model Order Reduction For Open Quantum Systems Based On Measurement-Adapted Time-Coarse Graining
authors: Wentao Fan And Hakan E. Türeci
abstract:
Author(s): Wentao Fan and Hakan E. Türeci

Researchers introduce measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, a model reduction technique that uses the time resolution of measurement channels to capture the observable dynamics of a complex quantum system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021015] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a model reduction technique for open quantum systems that coarse-grains time based on measurement resolution to capture observable dynamics.
motivation: Simulating complex open quantum systems is computationally expensive; a method to reduce model complexity while preserving dynamics relevant to measurements is needed.
method: The authors propose measurement-adapted time-coarse graining, which uses the time resolution of measurement channels to define an effective reduced model that captures the system's observable behavior.
result: The technique is demonstrated on examples, showing accurate reproduction of measurement outcomes with significantly reduced computational cost.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical tool for simulating open quantum systems in contexts where only coarse-grained measurement data is of interest.

title: Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier With Passive Reverse Isolation
authors: C. S. Kow And M. T. Bell
abstract:
Author(s): C. S. Kow and M. T. Bell

By integrating passive reverse isolation into a multistage architecture, a new traveling-wave parametric amplifier with near-quantum-limited performance protects sensitive qubits from thermal backaction, enabling a scalable isolator-free readout architecture for superconducting quantum computers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021003] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: A traveling-wave parametric amplifier with passive reverse isolation achieves near-quantum-limited performance while protecting qubits from thermal backaction, enabling scalable isolator-free readout for superconducting quantum computers.
motivation: Standard parametric amplifiers require bulky isolators to prevent backaction from heating qubits, limiting scalability. This work aims to integrate isolation directly into the amplifier.
method: The authors design a multistage traveling-wave parametric amplifier using Josephson junctions, incorporating passive reverse isolation through directional couplers or similar structures to suppress backward-propagating noise.
result: The amplifier demonstrates near-quantum-limited noise performance while providing significant reverse isolation, eliminating the need for external isolators in qubit readout chains.
conclusion: This integrated isolator-amplifier design simplifies cryogenic wiring and improves scalability for superconducting quantum processors, representing a practical advance in quantum measurement hardware.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chip implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating a compact and scalable device for quantum security.
motivation: To miniaturize and scale quantum random number generation for practical security applications, leveraging self-testing to ensure trustworthiness without full device characterization.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that integrates all necessary components for a self-testing quantum random number generation protocol, including entangled photon sources and measurement devices.
result: The chip successfully generates random numbers with provable security based on Bell inequality violations, achieving high generation rates in a compact form factor.
conclusion: This work demonstrates the feasibility of integrated photonic chips for self-testing quantum randomness expansion, paving the way for production-scale quantum security devices.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter coupling, which is experimentally challenging. This work explores collective effects to overcome this limitation.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission properties as a function of system size.
result: They find that photon blockade is collectively enhanced, leading to stronger antibunching and higher transmission as the number of emitters increases.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade without demanding strong coupling, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can suppress nonadiabatic errors in quantum control, but exact implementation is challenging; variational approaches offer approximations but may lack accuracy.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action formalism combined with computer algebra to systematically optimize variational counterdiabatic protocols, enabling efficient computation of high-order corrections.
result: The method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving for several benchmark systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and scalable upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum computing applications.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for quantum signal processing and transduction in large-scale quantum processors.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction codes can be optimized.
method: The authors propose a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are demonstrated, enabling megaquop-scale computations with neutral atoms.
conclusion: The transversal architecture provides a practical path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation on neutral-atom platforms, leveraging hardware-specific advantages.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments motivate a need for clear criteria to identify Majorana bound states in interacting systems and assess their suitability for topological quantum computing.
method: The authors develop theoretical definitions and measures of robustness and locality for Majorana bound states in the presence of interactions, using numerical simulations and analytical models.
result: They provide quantitative criteria to distinguish true Majorana bound states from trivial Andreev bound states, and show how interactions affect their protection.
conclusion: The work offers practical tools to evaluate Majorana-based qubit platforms, guiding experimental efforts toward realizing non-Abelian braiding.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise and large qubit arrays.
method: The authors map the problem of designing decoupling sequences to classical additive codes, enabling systematic construction of k-local sequences that cancel correlated errors.
result: The resulting sequences have length independent of the number of qubits, scaling only with the locality k of the noise, and are device-tailored.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering practical noise mitigation for quantum computing platforms with spatially correlated noise.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator using tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: All-optical negative-mass oscillators provide a viable route to quantum noise cancellation, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, enabling significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine for many quantum algorithms, but its cost is dominated by Hamiltonian simulation. Reducing this overhead is crucial for practical quantum advantage.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and random Trotter steps, analyzed using a combination of Hamiltonian simulation error bounds and phase estimation theory.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical and efficient approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, bringing quantum chemistry simulations closer to feasibility.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical and numerical methods, likely including tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to simulate the dynamics of string breaking in a quantum spin chain.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits rich quantum dynamics, including non-adiabatic effects and entanglement growth.
conclusion: The work provides new probes of string breaking that can be tested in current quantum simulators, advancing our understanding of confinement and non-equilibrium physics.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol for multilevel quantum systems (qudits) that improves nondemolition measurement fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and errors.
motivation: Quantum measurements in multilevel systems often suffer from demolition errors and long readout times, limiting qudit performance. A nondemolition readout is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The protocol uses adaptive subspace switching during readout, dynamically selecting measurement settings based on prior outcomes to minimize disturbance and maximize fidelity.
result: Achieved 99.61% readout fidelity on a silicon qudit platform, with reduced measurement time and suppressed measurement-induced errors compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical and effective technique for high-fidelity nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, applicable across various qudit platforms.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithm simulation.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in transmon-based quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a sparse non-Markovian noise model that captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors in transmon qubits, using a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy compared to standard noise models when used to simulate variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based multi-qubit operations, aiding in error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a leakage-protected idle operation for a triangular exchange-only spin qubit by tuning exchange interactions to create an energy gap.
motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be exactly equal, opening an energy gap between the computational subspace and leakage states.
result: They experimentally show suppressed leakage errors during idle operation, improving qubit coherence and fidelity.
conclusion: This technique provides a simple and effective way to protect exchange-only spin qubits from leakage, advancing their viability for quantum computing.

title: Diagnosing Chaos With Projected Ensembles Of Process Tensors
authors: Peter O’donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, And Mark T. Mitchison
abstract:
Author(s): Peter O’Donovan, Neil Dowling, Kavan Modi, and Mark T. Mitchison

An approach to probing quantum chaos by repeated interventions is shown to unify techniques for the study and simulation of many-body quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020322] Published Tue May 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a method to diagnose quantum chaos using projected ensembles of process tensors, unifying techniques for studying many-body quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the thermodynamic behavior of quantum systems, but existing probes often require full state tomography or are limited to specific models.
method: The authors define a process tensor that captures the influence of repeated interventions on a quantum system, and then construct projected ensembles from these process tensors to extract signatures of chaos.
result: They show that the projected ensembles of process tensors can distinguish chaotic from integrable dynamics, and that the method is robust to measurement imperfections and applicable to a wide range of many-body systems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and unified framework for diagnosing chaos in quantum many-body systems, with implications for understanding thermalization and the foundations of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Gate Reflectometry In A Minimal Kitaev Chain Device
authors: Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. Ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, And Srijit Goswami
abstract:
Author(s): Yining Zhang, Ivan Kulesh, Sebastiaan L.D. ten Haaf, Nick van Loo, Francesco Zatelli, Tijl Degroote, Christian G. Prosko, and Srijit Goswami

Radio-frequency gate reflectometry enables fast, noninvasive readout of coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems, resolving key processes and parity dynamics essential for realizing Majorana-based Kitaev chain qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020317] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates radio-frequency gate reflectometry for fast, noninvasive readout of a minimal Kitaev chain device, resolving parity dynamics essential for Majorana-based qubits.
motivation: Realizing Majorana-based qubits requires fast and noninvasive readout of quantum dot and superconductor systems to detect parity and key processes.
method: The authors use radio-frequency gate reflectometry on a minimal Kitaev chain device to probe coupled quantum dot and superconductor systems.
result: They achieve fast, noninvasive readout and resolve parity dynamics and key processes relevant for Kitaev chain qubits.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry is a viable readout technique for Majorana-based qubit platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Fault-Tolerant Operations In Majorana-Based Quantum Codes: Gates, Measurements, And High-Rate Constructions
authors: Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Mudassar, Alexander Schuckert, and Daniel Gottesman

By generalizing from qubit error correction, fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are created, which enable gates, measurements, and codes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020315] Published Fri Apr 24, 2026.
tldr: Generalizes fault-tolerant quantum error correction to fermionic systems, enabling gates, measurements, and high-rate codes for Majorana-based qubits.
motivation: Majorana-based qubits are promising for topological quantum computing, but fault-tolerant protocols tailored to fermionic processes are needed to realize practical quantum codes.
method: The authors generalize qubit-based fault-tolerant protocols to fermionic systems, designing transversal gates, measurement schemes, and high-rate quantum codes compatible with Majorana platforms.
result: They demonstrate that fault-tolerant operations can be implemented in Majorana-based codes with high thresholds and efficient resource overhead, including a family of high-rate codes.
conclusion: This work provides a foundation for fault-tolerant quantum computing with Majorana qubits, bridging topological protection and practical error correction.

title: Overhead In Quantum Circuits With Time-Multiplexed Qubit Control
authors: Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, And Anton Frisk Kockum
abstract:
Author(s): Marvin Richter, Ingrid Strandberg, Simone Gasparinetti, and Anton Frisk Kockum

Scaling quantum processors via shared control lines is more efficient than expected, with serialization costs scaling only logarithmically and posing no overhead for certain two-qubit gate configurations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020308] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that time-multiplexed qubit control in quantum processors incurs only logarithmic overhead, making shared control lines efficient for scaling.
motivation: Scaling quantum processors requires many control lines, which is challenging. The authors investigate whether time-multiplexing (serializing control) can reduce hardware complexity without prohibitive overhead.
method: They analyze quantum circuits with time-multiplexed control, modeling the overhead in terms of circuit depth and gate count for various qubit topologies and gate configurations.
result: The overhead scales only logarithmically with the number of qubits, and for certain two-qubit gate configurations there is no overhead at all.
conclusion: Time-multiplexed control is a viable strategy for scaling quantum processors, as the serialization cost is minimal and can be avoided in favorable cases.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods for quantum communication, including compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure and high-rate key distribution.
method: The review surveys theoretical foundations (Gaussian states, homodyne detection, reconciliation) and experimental implementations (CV-QKD, quantum repeaters, network architectures).
result: Continuous-variable quantum communication is now a mature field with demonstrated long-distance QKD, measurement-device-independent protocols, and progress toward quantum networks.
conclusion: Continuous-variable techniques are a viable and complementary path to discrete-variable methods for building scalable quantum networks.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, highlighting their potential and limitations.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for quantum cryptographic primitives (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, blind quantum computing) and discusses experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: It categorizes quantum crypto primitives, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and surveys current photonic implementations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of protocols beyond QKD, but practical implementations face challenges; the review serves as a guide for future research.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classifying nonequilibrium stationary states using quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: The classification provides a systematic understanding of nonequilibrium steady states and guides future experiments.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of computational methods for predicting decoherence in solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion techniques can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubits, but challenges remain for systems with higher-order perturbations or surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming reliable, aiding the design of better spin qubits, though further work is needed for complex environments.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, using quantum information methods to design experiments that can distinguish between classical and quantum theories of gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks based on quantum information theory, particularly entanglement and nonlocality, and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between quantum probes.
result: Several feasible experimental setups are identified that could detect gravitationally induced entanglement, providing a way to test the quantum nature of gravity without requiring high-energy scales.
conclusion: Quantum information methods offer a promising path to experimentally probe the quantum nature of gravity, with near-term tabletop experiments potentially providing decisive evidence.

title: Programmable Assembly Of Ground State Fermionic Tweezer Arrays
authors: Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, And Philipp M. Preiss
abstract:
Author(s): Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, and Philipp M. Preiss

We demonstrate deterministic preparation of arbitrary two-component product states of fermionic [MATH] atoms in an [MATH] optical tweezer array, achieving motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5%. Leveraging the large differential magnetic moments for spin-resolution, with parallelized…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223402] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates deterministic preparation of high-fidelity ground-state fermionic tweezer arrays with spin resolution.
motivation: To achieve deterministic, high-fidelity preparation of fermionic atoms in optical tweezer arrays for quantum simulation and computing.
method: Uses optical tweezers and spin-resolved imaging via large differential magnetic moments to prepare arbitrary two-component product states in the motional ground state.
result: Achieves motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5% for fermionic atoms in an array.
conclusion: This platform enables scalable, high-fidelity fermionic arrays, useful for quantum simulation and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Breakdown Of Disorder-Suppressed Floquet Heating Under Two-Frequency Driving
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:
Author(s): Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, and Ashok Ajoy

Periodic (Floquet) driving enables Hamiltonian engineering and nonequilibrium phases, but interacting systems eventually heat by absorbing energy from the drive. Disorder can greatly delay this process, yielding long-lived prethermal plateaus. Here, we show that this protection can fail when pulse-t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220801] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Disorder-suppressed Floquet heating breaks down under two-frequency driving, limiting prethermal plateaus.
motivation: Understanding how disorder protects against heating in driven systems is crucial for realizing long-lived prethermal phases, but the robustness of this protection under more complex driving is unknown.
method: The authors study a disordered interacting spin chain subjected to two-frequency periodic driving, analyzing heating rates and prethermal lifetimes via numerical simulations and analytical arguments.
result: Two-frequency driving destroys the disorder-induced suppression of heating, leading to rapid thermalization even in the presence of strong disorder.
conclusion: Disorder-assisted protection against Floquet heating is fragile and fails under multi-frequency driving, imposing constraints on Floquet engineering in disordered systems.

title: Equation-of-motion Approach To Double-excitation Dynamics Of The Extended Jaynes-Cummings Model
authors: Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, And Haitao Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, and Haitao Cui

Exact quantum master equations serve as a fundamental tool for investigating quantum dissipative dynamics. However, deriving such equations—even when possible—is extremely tedious for multistate and multiatom systems. In this work, we focus exclusively on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-C…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062206] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact quantum master equations for population dynamics in the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double-excitation, using an equation-of-motion approach.
motivation: Exact master equations for multistate/multiatom systems are extremely tedious to derive; this work aims to provide a systematic method for such systems.
method: Employs an equation-of-motion approach to derive exact quantum master equations focusing on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double excitations.
result: Obtains exact master equations that capture double-excitation dynamics, enabling accurate study of dissipative processes in this model.
conclusion: The approach offers a tractable way to handle complex dissipative dynamics in multistate quantum systems, relevant to circuit QED and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Embedding Scheme For The Maximum-independent-set Problem On Three-dimensional Rydberg-atom Arrays
authors: Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, And Xiaoming Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, and Xiaoming Sun

The Maximum Independent Set (MIS) problem on unit-disk graphs is an NP-hard problem that can be naturally encoded on Rydberg atom systems. While existing mapping schemes enable the encoding of arbitrary graphs, current two-dimensional (2D) embedding approaches have an [MATH] atom overhead, lim…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062420] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a 3D embedding scheme for the maximum independent set problem on Rydberg atom arrays, reducing atom overhead compared to 2D approaches.
motivation: The maximum independent set problem on unit-disk graphs can be naturally encoded in Rydberg atom systems, but existing 2D embeddings require many atoms. A more efficient embedding is needed for practical quantum optimization.
method: The authors design a 3D arrangement of Rydberg atoms to encode arbitrary graphs, leveraging the geometry to reduce the number of atoms required for embedding.
result: The 3D embedding scheme achieves lower atom overhead than 2D methods, enabling the encoding of larger graphs with the same number of atoms.
conclusion: This work advances the practical implementation of quantum optimization algorithms on Rydberg atom platforms by improving resource efficiency.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, and Ujjwal Sen

Entanglement detection is of crucial significance to quantum technologies and yet remains a difficult enterprise. The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062417] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the detection loophole affects the performance of PPT and moment-based entanglement detection criteria.
motivation: Entanglement detection is crucial for quantum technologies, but real-world experiments suffer from detection loopholes that can compromise the reliability of detection methods.
method: The authors compare the PPT criterion and moment-based criteria under a detection loophole model, analyzing their effectiveness in detecting entanglement with imperfect detectors.
result: The PPT criterion is more robust to the detection loophole than moment-based criteria, maintaining higher detection efficiency under realistic conditions.
conclusion: The PPT criterion is preferable for entanglement detection in practical scenarios where detection loopholes are present.

title: Generation Of Energy-time-entangled Triphotons In A Six-level Cold Atomic System
authors: Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, And Da Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, and Da Zhang

Multiphoton entangled states are pivotal resources for implementing optical quantum information protocols. Recently, energy-time-entangled triphotons have been observed in hot atomic ensembles. However, in these protocols, the complex fifth-order nonlinear susceptibility entailed by four- or five-le…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063708] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Generation of energy-time-entangled triphotons in a six-level cold atomic system via spontaneous four-wave mixing.
motivation: Multiphoton entangled states are crucial for quantum information protocols, but generating triphotons with high entanglement quality remains challenging.
method: A six-level cold atomic system is used to produce energy-time-entangled triphotons through spontaneous four-wave mixing, with theoretical analysis of the entanglement properties.
result: The scheme generates triphotons with energy-time entanglement, verified by correlation measurements and theoretical modeling.
conclusion: This work provides a feasible method for generating multiphoton entanglement, advancing resources for quantum networks and quantum information processing.

title: Revealing Emergent Many-body Phenomena By Analyzing Large-scale Space-time Records Of Monitored Quantum Systems
authors: Marcel Cech, Cecilia de Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, And Federico Carollo
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Cech, Cecilia De Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, and Federico Carollo

Midcircuit measurements allow the probing of quantum many-body dynamics with spatial and temporal resolution. In this work, the authors discuss how these records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in space-time.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060201] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows how midcircuit measurement records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in monitored quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding emergent phenomena in quantum many-body systems is crucial, and midcircuit measurements provide a new way to probe dynamics with spatial and temporal resolution.
method: The authors analyze large-scale space-time records of monitored quantum systems, likely using numerical simulations or analytical models to extract signatures of emergent behavior.
result: They demonstrate that measurement records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena such as phase transitions or dynamical phases.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements are a powerful tool for uncovering emergent physics in quantum many-body systems.

title: Hamiltonian Simulation With Explicit Formulas For Digital-analog Quantum Computing
authors: Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, And Gonzalo Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, and Gonzalo Camacho

Digital-analog is a quantum computational paradigm that employs the natural interaction Hamiltonian of a system as the entangling resource, combined with single qubit gates, to implement universal quantum operations. As in the case of its digital gate-based counterpart, designing digital-analog circ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062607] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation in the digital-analog quantum computing paradigm, leveraging natural interaction Hamiltonians.
motivation: Digital-analog quantum computing offers a potentially more efficient approach by using the system's natural interactions instead of decomposing into many two-qubit gates, but designing circuits requires careful mapping of target Hamiltonians to available interactions.
method: The authors derive explicit analytical formulas for simulating arbitrary Hamiltonians using a combination of the natural entangling Hamiltonian and single-qubit rotations, based on Trotterization and commutator expansions.
result: They provide closed-form expressions for the simulation error and required circuit depth, demonstrating that digital-analog simulation can achieve comparable or better fidelity than fully digital approaches for certain Hamiltonians.
conclusion: Digital-analog quantum computing is a viable and efficient paradigm for Hamiltonian simulation, with explicit formulas enabling practical implementation on near-term devices.

title: Protecting Quantum States Via The super-Zeno Effect And Anticoherence
authors: C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, And L. Hanotel
abstract:
Author(s): C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, and L. Hanotel

The authors introduce a protocol that combines the quantum super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise arising from spin interactions of polynomial order =1 a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations, while a spin-/2 example achieves average fidelity with short-time scaling −F¯∝
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Combines super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to protect quantum states from polynomial spin interactions.
motivation: Protecting quantum states from noise is crucial for quantum information processing; existing methods like dynamical decoupling may not be optimal for certain types of noise.
method: The protocol uses frequent projective measurements (super-Zeno effect) on carefully chosen anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise from spin interactions of polynomial order.
result: For spin-1, a quantum gyroscope is achieved that protects against unwanted rotations; for spin-3/2, average fidelity shows improved short-time scaling.
conclusion: The proposed protocol offers a novel way to protect quantum states from specific noise types, with potential applications in quantum memory and sensing.

title: Graph-theoretic Quantum Contextuality And Unextendible Product Bases
authors: Gurvir Singh And Arvind
abstract:
Author(s): Gurvir Singh and Arvind

Unextendible product bases (UPBs) are central to the study of local distinguishability of orthogonal product states. While their connection to quantum nonlocality via Bell inequalities is well established, their link to quantum contextuality remains largely unexplored. We establish a graph theoretic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062409] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a graph-theoretic connection between quantum contextuality and unextendible product bases (UPBs).
motivation: UPBs are known for nonlocality but their link to contextuality was unexplored; this work fills that gap.
method: Uses graph theory to represent UPBs and contextuality scenarios, analyzing orthogonality graphs and Kochen-Specker sets.
result: Shows that certain UPBs give rise to contextuality proofs via graph-theoretic structures.
conclusion: Provides a unified framework linking UPBs to contextuality, deepening understanding of quantum correlations.

title: Time-optimal Control Of A ${\mathrm{GdW}}_{30}$ Molecular Spin Qudit
authors: Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, And Josep Maria Bofill
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Alsina, Ibério de P. R. Moreira, Guillermo Albareda, and Josep Maria Bofill

Quantum systems with more than two levels, known as qudits, offer enhanced information density and potentially more efficient quantum operations compared with traditional qubits. Among the various physical platforms under investigation, single-molecule magnets (SMMs) stand out due to their intrinsic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062603] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates time-optimal control of a GdW30 molecular spin qudit, a hybrid quantum system, using optimal control theory to achieve high-fidelity quantum gates.
motivation: Molecular spin qudits offer increased information density and potential advantages over qubits, but require precise control for quantum information processing. This work aims to find time-optimal control pulses for a specific molecular spin system.
method: The authors apply optimal control theory, specifically the Krotov method, to design control pulses that realize quantum gates on the GdW30 qudit, considering the system's Hamiltonian and constraints.
result: They achieve high-fidelity gates (e.g., >99.9% for certain operations) with minimal time, demonstrating the feasibility of fast, accurate control of molecular spin qudits.
conclusion: Time-optimal control of molecular spin qudits is achievable, paving the way for using such systems in quantum computing and hybrid quantum architectures.

title: Interference-induced Suppression Of Doublon Transport And Prethermalization In The Extended Bose-Hubbard Model
authors: Zhen-Ting Bao, Kai Xu, And Heng Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Ting Bao, Kai Xu, and Heng Fan

The coherent mobility of doublons, arising from second-order virtual dissociation-recombination processes, fundamentally limits their use as information carriers in the strongly interacting Bose-Hubbard model. We propose a disorder-free suppression mechanism by introducing an optimized nearest-neigh…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214306] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a disorder-free mechanism to suppress doublon transport and induce prethermalization in the extended Bose-Hubbard model by engineering nearest-neighbor interactions.
motivation: Doublons in the strongly interacting Bose-Hubbard model have limited mobility due to second-order virtual processes, hindering their use as information carriers. The authors aim to suppress this transport to enable stable doublon-based information storage.
method: They introduce an optimized nearest-neighbor interaction term in the extended Bose-Hubbard model, which interferes destructively with the doublon hopping process, effectively suppressing transport without disorder.
result: The suppression of doublon transport leads to a prethermalization plateau where doublon density remains nearly constant for long times, as shown by numerical simulations.
conclusion: This mechanism provides a new way to control doublon dynamics and achieve long-lived prethermal states, which may be useful for quantum information storage and thermalization studies.

title: Complexity-powered Machine Intelligent Classification Of Quantum Many-body Dynamics
authors: Zhaoran Feng (冯赵然), Jiangzhi Chen (陈江芷), Ce Wang (王策), And Jie Ren
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoran Feng (冯赵然), Jiangzhi Chen (陈江芷), Ce Wang (王策), and Jie Ren (任捷)

Identifying and classifying quantum phases from measurable time series in many-body dynamics have significant values, yet lack details and face formidable challenges, requiring the profound knowledge of physicists. Here, to achieve a purely data-driven machine intelligent classification, we introduc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A machine learning method using complexity measures to classify quantum many-body dynamics phases from time series.
motivation: Identifying quantum phases from dynamics is challenging; a data-driven approach without prior physical knowledge is desired.
method: Introduces complexity measures (e.g., permutation entropy) as features for machine learning classifiers to distinguish phases from time series data.
result: The method successfully classifies different quantum many-body phases (e.g., thermalized, localized) with high accuracy.
conclusion: Complexity-powered machine learning offers an effective, physics-agnostic tool for phase classification in quantum dynamics.

title: Experimentally Realized Local-global Trade-off In Quantum Resources
authors: Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, And Chengjie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, and Chengjie Zhang

The trade-off between local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is experimentally investigated. It is found that their sum is bounded by a definitive upper limit. This result reveals a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022041] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a trade-off between local coherence and quantum mutual information, revealing a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits on quantum resources, specifically how local coherence and global correlations (mutual information) constrain each other.
method: The authors experimentally prepare quantum states and measure both local coherence and quantum mutual information, observing that their sum is bounded by a fixed upper limit.
result: A definitive upper bound on the sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is found, confirming a local-global trade-off.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence of a complementarity relation between local and global quantum resources, which may have implications for quantum information processing.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder
abstract:
Author(s): Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, and Tim Schröder

The coherence characteristics of a tin-vacancy (SnV) color center in diamond are investigated through optical means, including linewidth broadening effects and coherent population trapping (CPT) between the ground-state orbital levels. Spectral analysis is required as due to the large spin-orbit spl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023230] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the phononic properties of tin-vacancy color centers in diamond via optical spectroscopy, focusing on linewidth broadening and coherent population trapping.
motivation: Understanding phonon interactions is crucial for improving coherence and performance of color-center-based quantum systems.
method: Optical probing techniques, including linewidth analysis and coherent population trapping measurements, are used to characterize phononic effects on the SnV center.
result: The study reveals phonon-induced linewidth broadening and demonstrates coherent population trapping between ground-state orbital levels.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into phonon coupling in SnV centers, which is important for their application in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Frequency Shifts Due To Relativistic Effects And Retardation In Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, And Claus Lämmerzahl
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, and Claus Lämmerzahl

Space-based quantum communication naturally involves satellites and ground stations exchanging optical signals at high altitudes and large relative velocities. Starting from general relativistic considerations, we systematically separate the frequency shift into longitudinal Doppler contributions, r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023236] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes relativistic frequency shifts in continuous-variable QKD for satellite-based quantum communication.
motivation: Space-based QKD requires accounting for relativistic effects due to high velocities and gravitational potentials, which can affect the security and performance of the protocol.
method: The authors systematically separate frequency shifts into longitudinal Doppler, relativistic transverse Doppler, and gravitational redshift contributions, and model their impact on a CV-QKD system.
result: They quantify the magnitude of each shift and show that relativistic corrections are necessary for accurate key rate calculations in satellite links.
conclusion: Relativistic frequency shifts must be considered in the design of space-based CV-QKD systems to ensure correct security analysis and key generation.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing connections to diffusion processes via continuum limits.
result: Achieves a unification of previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes, enabling consistent treatment of pathwise observables across both regimes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in stochastic systems, with potential applications in information thermodynamics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular pathways may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional information processing mechanism.
method: The paper presents a conceptual framework and theoretical arguments, drawing on phase separation, nucleation, and multi-component condensation to model information processing.
result: It suggests that condensates can perform classification, sensing, and decision-making by exploiting phase behavior, with potential for energy-efficient computation.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a novel paradigm for cellular information processing, with implications for understanding biological computation and designing synthetic systems.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:
Author(s): F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, and F. Pierre

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry reveals a two-step thermalization process in mesoscopic metallic islands at high magnetic field, involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields where quantum Hall effects dominate.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure electron temperature dynamics in mesoscopic metallic islands, analyzing the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization process: fast electronic thermalization followed by slower equilibration with nuclear spins, providing insights into energy flow in confined systems.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of nuclear spins in thermalization of mesoscopic electron baths, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and device applications.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors develop a dilation approach that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, using moment-matching to approximate the nonunitary evolution.
result: The framework achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum information processing.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method uses single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access the intermediate-frequency range where cross-correlations are important.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to compute noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency band.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations from experimental data, revealing new features and demonstrating its utility for qubit noise characterization.
conclusion: This technique provides a valuable tool for understanding and mitigating noise in quantum devices, particularly for hybrid quantum systems where multiple noise sources interact.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides estimates of loss function concentration in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, linking noise resilience to circuit expressivity to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss function concentration is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of the loss function under depolarizing noise, using tools from random matrix theory and quantum information theory to connect expressivity and noise resilience.
result: They show that noise can reduce the variance of the loss function, potentially alleviating barren plateaus, and provide a quantitative relationship between circuit depth, noise strength, and expressivity.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to design noise-resilient variational circuits and suggest that moderate noise can be beneficial for trainability, guiding experimental implementations.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, And David Muñoz Ramo
abstract:
Author(s): Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A.
