Moses, Peter E. Siegfried, Maxwell D. Urmey, Justin J. Burau, Aaron Hankin, Dominic Lucchetti, John P. Gaebler, Natalie C. Brown, Brian Neyenhuis, and David Muñoz Ramo

Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with variational quantum algorithms to achieve reliable molecular energy calculations on near-term hardware.
method: Implements a trapped-ion quantum processor with noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets to perform a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies.
result: Achieves a molecular energy estimate with improved accuracy compared to non-error-corrected approaches, demonstrating the feasibility of error-corrected quantum chemistry on current hardware.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry simulations, paving the way for more reliable quantum computations of molecular properties.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret
abstract:
Author(s): Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, and Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate a dissipative quantum system relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control over asymmetry.
motivation: Quantum simulation of chemical reactions requires controllable dissipative systems; parametric oscillators offer a platform for such simulations.
method: The authors implement a continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator and control its asymmetry to mimic a dissipative quantum system.
result: They demonstrate the ability to simulate chemical activation dynamics, showing control over the system's asymmetry.
conclusion: The work establishes a parametric oscillator as a viable platform for quantum simulation of chemical processes, with potential for studying more complex reactions.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various simulation techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for choosing appropriate techniques for specific problems.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships between different approaches and aids in selecting simulation methods for non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qudits can reduce gate complexity and resource requirements for quantum algorithms, offering advantages over qubit-only approaches.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques (e.g., using qutrits for Toffoli gates), and experimental implementations.
result: Qudits enable simpler decompositions of multiqubit gates and can improve efficiency in quantum computing, with experimental demonstrations in various platforms.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum information processing, warranting further theoretical and experimental exploration.

title: Layer Codes As Partially Self-Correcting Quantum Memories
authors: Shouzhen Gu, Libor Caha, Shin Ho Choe, Zhiyang He, Aleksander Kubica, And Eugene Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Shouzhen Gu, Libor Caha, Shin Ho Choe, Zhiyang He, Aleksander Kubica, and Eugene Tang

We investigate layer codes, a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes that achieves optimal scaling of code parameters and energy barrier, as candidates for self-correcting quantum memories. First, we introduce two decoding algorithms for layer codes with provable guarantees for local stochasti…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 210601] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: Layer codes are 3D stabilizer codes with optimal scaling of code parameters and energy barrier, proposed as partially self-correcting quantum memories.
motivation: Self-correcting quantum memories could protect quantum information without active error correction, but known codes have limitations; layer codes aim to improve the energy barrier and decoding performance.
method: The authors introduce two decoding algorithms for layer codes with provable guarantees under local stochastic noise, and analyze the energy barrier and code parameters.
result: Layer codes achieve optimal scaling of code parameters and energy barrier, and the decoding algorithms provide efficient error correction.
conclusion: Layer codes are promising candidates for partially self-correcting quantum memories, though further work is needed for full self-correction.

title: Hyperentanglement-based Quantum Reservoir Computing
authors: Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Boyuan Sun, Yifan Sun, and Xiangdong Zhang

Quantum machine learning integrates quantum features such as superposition and entanglement into learning processes, offering the potential to outperform classical methods in certain tasks. Among these approaches, quantum reservoir computing (QRC) has attracted considerable attention due to its simp…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062416] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum reservoir computing scheme using hyperentangled states to enhance performance.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) is a promising approach for quantum machine learning, but its performance is limited by the encoding capacity of simple entangled states. Hyperentanglement offers a way to increase the Hilbert space dimension and improve computational power.
method: The authors design a QRC architecture where hyperentangled photons (entangled in multiple degrees of freedom) serve as the reservoir. They simulate the dynamics using a linear optics setup and apply it to time-series prediction tasks.
result: The hyperentanglement-based QRC achieves higher accuracy and faster convergence compared to standard QRC using only polarization entanglement, demonstrating the advantage of higher-dimensional entanglement.
conclusion: Hyperentanglement is a viable resource for enhancing quantum reservoir computing, but the work is primarily a machine learning application without deep information-theoretic or thermodynamic insights.

title: Solovay-Kitaev Algorithm And Randomized Compilation
authors: Oliver Maupin, Ashlyn D. Burch, Christopher G. Yale, Matthew N. H. Chow, Terra Colvin, Jr., Brandon Ruzic, Melissa C. Revelle, Brian K. Mcfarland, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Alejandro Rascon, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, And Peter J. Love
abstract:
Author(s): Oliver Maupin, Ashlyn D. Burch, Christopher G. Yale, Matthew N. H. Chow, Terra Colvin, Jr., Brandon Ruzic, Melissa C. Revelle, Brian K. McFarland, Eduardo Ibarra-García-Padilla, Alejandro Rascon, Andrew J. Landahl, Susan M. Clark, and Peter J. Love

We analyze the use of the Solovay-Kitaev (SK) algorithm to generate an ensemble of one-qubit rotations over which to perform randomized compilation. We perform simulations to compare the trace distance between the quantum state resulting from an ideal one-qubit [MATH] rotation and discrete SK dec…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062418] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm for generating one-qubit rotation ensembles used in randomized compilation, comparing trace distances between ideal and discretized rotations.
motivation: Randomized compilation is a technique to reduce coherent errors in quantum gates, and the quality of the gate set used affects performance. The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm provides a way to approximate arbitrary single-qubit gates with a finite universal gate set.
method: Simulations are performed to compute the trace distance between the quantum state resulting from an ideal one-qubit rotation and the state from a discrete Solovay-Kitaev decomposition, for various rotation angles and approximation precisions.
result: The trace distance scales with the approximation precision of the Solovay-Kitaev algorithm, and the ensemble of rotations generated can be used for randomized compilation with controlled error.
conclusion: The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm is effective for generating gate sets for randomized compilation, but the paper is primarily a numerical study of gate approximation rather than a fundamental information-theoretic result.

title: Attributed-graph Kernel Implementation Using Local Detuning Of A Neutral-atom Rydberg Hamiltonian
authors: Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, And Shaheen Acheche
abstract:
Author(s): Mehdi Djellabi, Matthias Hecker, and Shaheen Acheche

We extend the quantum-feature kernel framework, which relies on measurements of graph-dependent observables, along three directions. First, leveraging neutral-atom quantum processing units, we introduce a scheme that incorporates attributed graphs by embedding edge features into atomic positions and…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062608] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum-feature kernel methods to attributed graphs using neutral-atom Rydberg systems, embedding edge features into atomic positions and leveraging local detuning.
motivation: To enable graph classification with attributed graphs (nodes and edges with features) on quantum hardware, extending previous quantum kernel approaches.
method: The authors propose a scheme using neutral-atom quantum processing units where edge features are encoded in atomic positions and local detuning of the Rydberg Hamiltonian is used to implement attributed-graph kernels.
result: The scheme allows encoding of both node and edge attributes into the quantum state, enabling kernel-based classification of attributed graphs.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a practical approach to integrate attributed graphs into quantum machine learning on neutral-atom platforms, though experimental validation is not provided.

title: Robust Applicability Of Continuous Dynamical Decoupling To Decoherence Reduction In Longitudinal And Transverse-noise Settings: The Role Of Anisotropy
authors: S. Afonso, J. M. Gomez Llorente, And J. Plata
abstract:
Author(s): S. Afonso, J. M. Gomez Llorente, and J. Plata

We analytically evaluate the efficiency of continuous dynamical decoupling (CDD) to curb decoherence in generic qubit setups where diverse sources of noise can be present. Previous theoretical approaches to CDD have mainly focused on its potential to cope with longitudinal fluctuations. Here, the ba…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062412] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Analytical evaluation of continuous dynamical decoupling for decoherence reduction in qubit setups with both longitudinal and transverse noise, highlighting the role of noise anisotropy.
motivation: Previous work focused on longitudinal noise; this paper extends analysis to transverse noise and anisotropic settings to assess CDD robustness.
method: Analytical derivation of decoherence reduction efficiency using continuous dynamical decoupling in generic qubit models with anisotropic noise.
result: CDD effectiveness depends on noise anisotropy; transverse noise can limit decoherence reduction even when longitudinal noise is suppressed.
conclusion: Continuous dynamical decoupling is robust but its applicability is constrained by noise anisotropy, requiring careful design for practical quantum systems.

title: Probing The Crossover Between Dynamical Phases With Local Correlations In A Rydberg-atom Array
authors: Xiaofeng Wu, Xin Wang, Sixun Jia, And Bo Xiong
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaofeng Wu, Xin Wang, Sixun Jia, and Bo Xiong

The experimental detection of nonequilibrium quantum criticality remains a challenge, as traditional signatures like dynamical quantum phase transitions rely on hard-to-measure global properties. Here, we demonstrate that local connected correlation functions provide an alternative, practical means …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062204] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses local connected correlation functions to probe the crossover between dynamical phases in a Rydberg-atom array, offering an experimentally accessible signature of nonequilibrium quantum criticality.
motivation: Detecting nonequilibrium quantum criticality is challenging because traditional signatures rely on global properties that are hard to measure; the authors aim to provide a practical alternative using local correlations.
method: The authors study a Rydberg-atom array and compute local connected correlation functions to characterize the dynamical phase transition between a paramagnetic and a time-crystal-like phase.
result: They show that local correlations exhibit clear signatures of the dynamical phase crossover, including a peak in the correlation length and a change in scaling behavior near the transition.
conclusion: Local connected correlation functions serve as a viable probe for nonequilibrium quantum criticality, potentially enabling experimental detection in Rydberg-atom platforms.

title: Out-of-time-order Correlators For The Swanson Hamiltonian With Interaction Terms
authors: M. W. Almasri And Marta Reboiro
abstract:
Author(s): M. W. AlMasri and Marta Reboiro

In this work, we compute the out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) for canonical position and momentum operators across a hierarchy of non-Hermitian oscillator models: the exactly solvable Swanson Hamiltonian, its Kerr-nonlinear extension, and parametrically driven variants. By employing the biortho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062205] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Computes OTOCs for non-Hermitian oscillator models, exploring quantum chaos and information scrambling.
motivation: To understand information scrambling and quantum chaos in non-Hermitian systems, which are relevant to open quantum systems and thermodynamics.
method: Uses biorthogonal formalism to compute OTOCs for the Swanson Hamiltonian and its extensions with Kerr nonlinearity and parametric driving.
result: Finds that OTOC growth depends on non-Hermiticity and nonlinearity, with signatures of chaos and information scrambling.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can exhibit rich scrambling dynamics, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and open systems.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Devices Beyond Classical Capabilities
authors: Rafał Bistroń, Marcin Rudziński, Ryszard Kukulski, And Karol Życzkowski
abstract:
Author(s): Rafał Bistroń, Marcin Rudziński, Ryszard Kukulski, and Karol Życzkowski

Rapid development of quantum computing technology has led to a wide variety of sophisticated quantum devices. Benchmarking these systems becomes crucial for understanding their capabilities and paving the way for future advancements. The Quantum Volume (QV) test is one of the most widely used benchm…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062604] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a benchmarking method for quantum devices beyond classical capabilities, focusing on the Quantum Volume test and its extensions.
motivation: As quantum devices grow in complexity, robust benchmarking is needed to assess their performance and guide development.
method: The authors analyze the Quantum Volume test and propose modifications to better capture quantum advantage, using random circuit sampling and statistical analysis.
result: They demonstrate that the proposed benchmark can distinguish devices that achieve quantum supremacy from those that do not, with improved sensitivity.
conclusion: The work provides a practical tool for evaluating near-term quantum devices, but does not introduce new information-theoretic or thermodynamic insights.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces non-Gaussian control parameters to systematically optimize optical non-Gaussian state generation, increasing success rates by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum information processing but their generation is inefficient; the paper aims to provide a systematic optimization framework.
method: The authors define new control parameters beyond the stellar rank and develop a method to optimize the generation process using these parameters.
result: The proposed control parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success rate of generating non-Gaussian quantum states.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for scalable generation of non-Gaussian states, advancing optical quantum information processing.

title: Entropy Of Strongly Correlated Electrons In A Partially Filled Landau Level
authors: Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, And Andrea F. Young
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandre Assouline, Taige Wang, Heun Mo Yoo, Ruihua Fan, Fangyuan Yang, Ruining Zhang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, and Andrea F. Young

Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal the successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, reaching sensitivities that constrain the isolation of topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021016] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Entropy measurements in partially filled Landau levels reveal freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom, with sensitivity to isolate topological entropy in non-Abelian phases.
motivation: Understanding entropy in strongly correlated electron systems is crucial for probing topological order and non-Abelian anyons.
method: Experimental entropy measurements using a graphene-based quantum Hall device with a local charge sensor.
result: Successive freezing of spin and motional degrees of freedom is observed, and the sensitivity approaches the level needed to isolate topological entropy.
conclusion: The technique can potentially detect topological entropy in non-Abelian quantum phases, advancing the study of topological order.

title: Magic Tricycles: Efficient Magic-State Generation With Finite Block-Length Quantum Ldpc Codes
authors: Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, And Mikhail D. Lukin
abstract:
Author(s): Varun Menon, J. Pablo Bonilla Ataides, Rohan Mehta, Andi Gu, Daniel Bochen Tan, and Mikhail D. Lukin

Quantum computing needs “magic states” for universality, but they are costly to make. New research introduces tricycle codes: high-rate QLDPC codes that can be used to generate CZ magic states in constant depth with high noise resilience.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021014] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: Introduces tricycle codes, high-rate QLDPC codes for efficient magic state generation in constant depth with high noise resilience.
motivation: Magic states are essential for universal quantum computing but costly to produce; efficient generation schemes are needed.
method: Proposes tricycle codes, a family of quantum LDPC codes with high rate and constant-depth encoding, used to distill magic states.
result: Demonstrates that tricycle codes can generate CZ magic states with improved noise tolerance and lower overhead compared to existing protocols.
conclusion: Tricycle codes offer a practical path toward efficient magic state generation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: A multiproduct commutation relation reduces T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation.
motivation: T gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum algorithms.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial commutation relation for multiproducts of Pauli operators and apply it to sequential Pauli-based computation to cancel T gates.
result: The proposed relation enables significant T-count reduction compared to standard methods.
conclusion: This work provides a new technique for T-count optimization, contributing to more efficient fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses Fourier neural operators to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally challenging; the authors aim to develop a machine learning approach that captures temporal correlations in frequency space.
method: They employ Fourier neural operators (FNOs) to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables and operator growth, leveraging the frequency-domain representation of periodic driving.
result: The FNO model accurately predicts dynamics beyond the training time window and generalizes to different driving parameters, demonstrating physically faithful extrapolation.
conclusion: FNOs provide an efficient and accurate surrogate model for time-periodic quantum systems, enabling long-time predictions without solving the full Schrödinger equation.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Logical Magic State Preparation Protocols
authors: Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, And Isaac H. Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Samyak Surti, Lucas Daguerre, and Isaac H. Kim

Classical simulation of a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols is made scalable and efficient via propagating errors to the end of the circuit.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020329] Published Thu May 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an efficient classical simulation method for logical magic state preparation protocols by propagating errors to the end of the circuit.
motivation: Magic state preparation is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating these protocols is computationally expensive. The authors aim to make such simulations scalable and efficient.
method: The method propagates errors through the circuit to the end, reducing the complexity of simulating logical magic state preparation protocols.
result: The simulation becomes scalable and efficient for a large class of logical magic state preparation protocols.
conclusion: The proposed technique enables practical classical simulation of magic state preparation, which is important for verifying and designing fault-tolerant quantum computing schemes.

title: Abelian Multi-Cycle Codes For Single-Shot Error Correction
authors: Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, And Leonid P. Pryadko
abstract:
Author(s): Hsiang-Ku Lin, Pak Kau Lim, Alexey A. Kovalev, and Leonid P. Pryadko

A new family of quantum low-density parity-check codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, achieves single-shot fault tolerance and an approximately 1.1% pseudothreshold with significantly shorter block lengths.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020326] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A new family of quantum LDPC codes achieving single-shot fault tolerance with shorter block lengths.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum error correction typically requires many rounds of syndrome extraction; single-shot error correction reduces this overhead.
method: The authors construct Abelian multi-cycle codes, which are locally equivalent to higher-dimensional hypergraph-product codes, and analyze their single-shot error correction properties.
result: The codes achieve a pseudothreshold of approximately 1.1% with significantly shorter block lengths compared to previous constructions.
conclusion: These codes offer a practical advantage for fault-tolerant quantum computing by reducing the number of syndrome extraction rounds.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes via code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurement is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code parameters.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's distance and rate.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements without sacrificing code performance, demonstrated on several families of LDPC codes.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by enabling efficient parallel operations on low-overhead quantum codes.

title: Quantum Filtering And Analysis Of Multiplicities In Eigenvalue Spectra
authors: Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, And Ruizhe Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyan Ding, Lin Lin, Yilun Yang, and Ruizhe Zhang

A quantum filtering algorithm identifies clusters of eigenvalues and their multiplicities, enabling efficient spectral analysis beyond worst-case complexity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020318] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: A quantum filtering algorithm for identifying eigenvalue clusters and multiplicities with improved efficiency.
motivation: Eigenvalue spectral analysis is fundamental in quantum mechanics, but worst-case complexity can be high; the paper aims to provide a practical quantum algorithm for this task.
method: The algorithm uses quantum filtering techniques to detect clusters of eigenvalues and estimate their multiplicities, leveraging quantum phase estimation and amplitude amplification.
result: The algorithm achieves efficiency beyond worst-case complexity for certain spectral structures, demonstrated analytically and numerically.
conclusion: The work offers a quantum algorithmic tool for spectral analysis, but its contribution is primarily computational rather than advancing core quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: High-Threshold, Low-Overhead And Single-Shot Decodable Fault-Tolerant Quantum Memory
authors: Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, And Joschka Roffe
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas R. Scruby, Timo Hillmann, and Joschka Roffe

Radial codes, a new class of low-density parity-check codes with strong error correction capabilities, tunable parameters, and small size, are shown to be a promising candidate for near-term quantum devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020310] Published Fri Apr 17, 2026.
tldr: Radial codes are a new class of LDPC codes offering high threshold, low overhead, and single-shot decodable fault-tolerant quantum memory.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum memory requires high error thresholds and low overhead, but existing codes like surface codes have high overhead. Radial codes aim to improve these metrics.
method: The authors introduce radial codes, a family of low-density parity-check codes with tunable parameters, and analyze their error correction performance using numerical simulations.
result: Radial codes achieve high thresholds, low overhead, and single-shot decoding, making them promising for near-term quantum devices.
conclusion: Radial codes are a strong candidate for fault-tolerant quantum memory, balancing performance and resource requirements.

title: Hardware-Efficient Universal Linear Transformations For Optical Modes In The Synthetic Time Dimension
authors: Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, And Saikat Guha
abstract:
Author(s): Jasvith Raj Basani, Chaohan Cui, Jack Postlewaite, Edo Waks, and Saikat Guha

A synthetic time-domain photonic processor exponentially reduces hardware complexity while maintaining all-to-all connectivity, exceeding performance thresholds for scalable, universal quantum computation under realistic physical constraints.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020305] Published Wed Apr 08, 2026.
tldr: A photonic processor using synthetic time dimensions achieves universal linear transformations with exponentially reduced hardware complexity.
motivation: Scalable universal quantum computation requires efficient linear optical circuits, but traditional spatial architectures face hardware scaling challenges.
method: The authors propose a synthetic time-domain architecture where modes are encoded in time bins and processed via a single spatial loop with modulators, enabling all-to-all connectivity.
result: The design meets performance thresholds for universal quantum computation under realistic physical constraints, including loss and noise.
conclusion: Synthetic time dimensions offer a hardware-efficient path to universal linear optical quantum computing.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from violated assumptions in measurements.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields where measured properties exceed thermodynamic bounds, and analyzes which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linearity) are violated.
result: It identifies common patterns of assumption violation and shows how materials can be designed to deliberately break these assumptions to achieve extreme properties.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are not actual violations of thermodynamics but rather indicate that the bounds' assumptions do not apply; this insight can guide the development of novel materials.

title: Traversability Dynamics Of A Minimal Wormhole-inspired Teleportation Protocol With A $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian Deformation
authors: Sudhanva Joshi And Sunil Kumar Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Sudhanva Joshi and Sunil Kumar Mishra

Holography-inspired teleportation has recently emerged as a significant area of research in quantum many-body systems. In this work, we investigate the effects of [MATH]-symmetric nonunitary deformations on the traversability of the wormhole-inspired teleportation protocol modeled by coupled…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062419] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of PT-symmetric non-Hermitian deformations on a holography-inspired teleportation protocol, finding that such deformations can enhance traversability.
motivation: To understand how non-unitary, PT-symmetric dynamics affect the traversability of wormhole-inspired teleportation in quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors model the teleportation protocol using coupled SYK-like systems and introduce a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian deformation, then analyze the out-of-time-order correlators and mutual information to quantify traversability.
result: The PT-symmetric deformation can enhance the traversability of the teleportation protocol, as measured by increased mutual information and improved signal transmission.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian deformations provide a new knob to control quantum teleportation in holographic settings, with potential implications for quantum information processing.

title: Impact Of The Unruh Effect On The Estimation Precision Of Gaussian Channel Parameters
authors: Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, And Xingdong Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Shoukang Chang, Yawen Tang, Wei Ye, Shaoming Fei, Zunlue Zhu, and Xingdong Zhao

Gaussian quantum channels constitute a pivotal physical framework for characterizing the dynamics of Gaussian quantum states. Extensive scholarly attention has been devoted to the estimation of parameters associated with Gaussian channels. However, while previous research has predominantly focused o…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062609] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the Unruh effect affects the precision of estimating Gaussian channel parameters using quantum metrology.
motivation: Previous work on Gaussian channel estimation ignored relativistic effects; the Unruh effect introduces noise that may limit estimation precision.
method: The authors model a Gaussian channel in an accelerated frame, compute the quantum Fisher information for parameter estimation, and analyze the impact of acceleration.
result: The Unruh effect degrades estimation precision, but optimal measurements can partially mitigate the loss.
conclusion: Relativistic effects must be considered in quantum metrology for Gaussian channels, especially in high-acceleration scenarios.

title: Optimizing Doppler Laser Cooling Protocols For Quantum Sensing With Three-dimensional Ion Crystals In A Penning Trap
authors: John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, And Scott E. Parker
abstract:
Author(s): John Zaris, Wes Johnson, Athreya Shankar, John J. Bollinger, Allison L. Carter, Daniel H. E. Dubin, and Scott E. Parker

Large, three-dimensional (3D) trapped-ion crystals offer improved sensitivity in quantum sensing protocols, and are expected to be implemented as platforms in near-future experiments. However, numerical techniques used to study the laser cooling of such crystals are inefficient as the number of ions…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063103] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes Doppler laser cooling protocols for large 3D ion crystals in Penning traps to improve quantum sensing sensitivity.
motivation: Large 3D trapped-ion crystals offer enhanced sensitivity for quantum sensing, but existing numerical techniques for simulating laser cooling are inefficient for large ion numbers.
method: The authors develop an efficient numerical method to simulate and optimize Doppler laser cooling protocols for 3D ion crystals in a Penning trap.
result: They identify optimal cooling parameters that achieve lower temperatures and faster cooling times compared to standard protocols.
conclusion: The optimized cooling protocols enable practical use of large 3D ion crystals for quantum sensing applications.

title: Slow-light-enhanced Photon Drag In A Tunneling-coupled Quantum-dot System
authors: Muhammad Idrees, Xiaosen Yang, Fazal Badshah, And Zareen A. Khan
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Idrees, Xiaosen Yang, Fazal Badshah, and Zareen A. Khan

We present a theoretical study of enhanced lateral and rotary photon drag within a four-level quantum-dot setup under the effect of dual interdot tunneling. Using the density-matrix formalism, we derive analytical expressions for the susceptibility, group index, and phase index under weak-field cond…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063709] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of slow-light-enhanced photon drag in a tunneling-coupled quantum-dot system.
motivation: To explore enhanced lateral and rotary photon drag effects using quantum coherence in a quantum-dot system.
method: Density-matrix formalism to derive susceptibility, group index, and phase index under weak-field conditions.
result: Analytical expressions for enhanced photon drag due to slow light and interdot tunneling.
conclusion: The proposed system can achieve significant photon drag enhancement, relevant for optical manipulation.

title: Localization And Scattering Of A Photon In Quasiperiodic Qubit Arrays
authors: Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, And Chaohong Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyin Zhang, Yongguan Ke, Zhenzhi Peng, Zuorui Chen, Wenjie Liu, Li Zhang, and Chaohong Lee

We study the localization and scattering of a single photon in a waveguide coupled to qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings. As the quasiperiodic strength increases, localized subradiant states with extremely long lifetime appear around the resonant frequency and form a continuum band. In stark c…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063704] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies localization and scattering of a single photon in waveguide-coupled qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings, revealing a continuum of long-lived subradiant states.
motivation: Understanding photon transport in disordered quantum systems is important for quantum information processing, but the focus here is on quasiperiodic order rather than quantum networking or thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a waveguide coupled to qubit arrays with quasiperiodic spacings and analyze the scattering properties and localization of single photons using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that as quasiperiodic strength increases, localized subradiant states with extremely long lifetimes form a continuum band around the resonant frequency, contrasting with the discrete bound states in periodic arrays.
conclusion: The work provides insights into photon localization in quasiperiodic qubit arrays, which may have implications for quantum memory or slow-light applications, but is not directly aligned with the user's core interests.

title: Cellular Automata In $d$ Dimensions And Ground States Of Spin Models In $(d+1)$ Dimensions
authors: Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, And Juan P. Garrahan
abstract:
Author(s): Konstantinos Sfairopoulos, Luke Causer, Jamie F. Mair, and Juan P. Garrahan

We show how the trajectories of [MATH]-dimensional cellular automata (CA) can be used to systematically construct the ground states of [MATH]-dimensional classical spin models, and we characterize their quantum phase transition, when in the presence of a transverse magnetic field. For each of the 256 …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064112] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models from trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata and studies their quantum phase transitions.
motivation: To establish a systematic connection between cellular automata and classical spin models, and to characterize the quantum phase transition when a transverse field is added.
method: The authors use the trajectories of d-dimensional cellular automata to define ground states of (d+1)-dimensional classical spin models, then analyze the quantum phase transition via a transverse field.
result: They show that each of the 256 elementary cellular automata in 1D corresponds to a 2D classical spin model, and characterize the quantum phase transition in the presence of a transverse field.
conclusion: The work provides a new mapping between cellular automata and spin models, but the connection to information thermodynamics is indirect and the contribution is more about statistical mechanics and phase transitions.

title: Violation Of Local Equilibrium Thermodynamics In One-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts Model
authors: Hitomi Endo And Michikazu Kobayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Hitomi Endo and Michikazu Kobayashi

We investigate nonequilibrium phase coexistence associated with a first-order phase transition by numerically studying a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives. The fractional derivative is introduced so as to reproduce the low-wave-number density of states of th…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064109] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonequilibrium phase coexistence in a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives, finding violations of local equilibrium thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand nonequilibrium phase transitions and test the validity of local equilibrium assumptions in systems with long-range interactions.
method: Numerical simulation of a one-dimensional Hamiltonian-Potts model with fractional spatial derivatives to reproduce low-wave-number density of states.
result: The system exhibits violation of local equilibrium thermodynamics during first-order phase transitions.
conclusion: Fractional derivative models can capture nonequilibrium effects beyond local equilibrium, relevant for systems with long-range interactions.

title: Ergodicity And Hydrodynamics: From Quantum To Classical Spin Systems
authors: Jiaozi Wang, Luca Capizzi, Dario Poletti, And Leonardo Mazza
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaozi Wang, Luca Capizzi, Dario Poletti, and Leonardo Mazza

We show that in classical spin systems, the precise nature of the late-time hydrodynamic tails of the autocorrelation functions of a generic observable is determined by (i) the dynamical critical exponent and (ii) the equilibrium thermodynamic properties of the corresponding observable. We provide n…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064102] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that hydrodynamic tails in classical spin systems are determined by dynamical critical exponent and equilibrium thermodynamic properties.
motivation: Understanding late-time dynamics and ergodicity in many-body systems is fundamental to statistical mechanics.
method: Analytical calculations and numerical simulations of autocorrelation functions in classical spin models.
result: The precise form of hydrodynamic tails depends on the dynamical critical exponent and thermodynamic susceptibility of the observable.
conclusion: Classical spin systems exhibit universal hydrodynamic behavior governed by equilibrium properties and critical exponents.

title: Hyperuniformity In Active Fluids Reshapes Nucleation And Capillary-wave Dynamics
authors: Raphaël Maire
abstract:
Author(s): Raphaël Maire

Nucleation in active and driven fluids often resembles equilibrium behavior, but a departure occurs when large-scale density fluctuations are strongly suppressed. In this work, it is demonstrated that droplet nucleation in nonequilibrium hyperuniform fluids is governed by a nonequilibrium quasipotential instead of the classical reversible work of formation.

#WellStructured #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064103] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nucleation in active hyperuniform fluids, showing that droplet formation is governed by a nonequilibrium quasipotential rather than classical reversible work.
motivation: Understanding nucleation in active fluids is important for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, but the paper focuses on a specific phenomenon (hyperuniformity) that is not central to the researcher's interests.
method: The authors theoretically analyze droplet nucleation in active fluids with suppressed density fluctuations, deriving a nonequilibrium quasipotential that replaces the classical reversible work.
result: They find that hyperuniformity reshapes nucleation and capillary-wave dynamics, leading to deviations from equilibrium behavior.
conclusion: The work provides insights into nonequilibrium phase transitions but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum systems.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions In Certain Nonergodic Stochastic Processes
authors: Yogeesh Reddy Yerrababu, Satya N. Majumdar, Benjamin Guiselin, And Tridib Sadhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yogeesh Reddy Yerrababu, Satya N. Majumdar, Benjamin Guiselin, and Tridib Sadhu

We present a class of stochastic processes in which the large deviation functions of time-integrated observables exhibit singularities that relate to dynamical phase transitions of trajectories. These illustrative examples include Brownian motion with a death rate or in the presence of an absorbing …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064104] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies dynamical phase transitions in large deviation functions of time-integrated observables for certain nonergodic stochastic processes.
motivation: To understand singularities in large deviation functions that signal dynamical phase transitions in stochastic processes, which are relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze Brownian motion with a death rate or absorbing boundaries, computing large deviation functions and identifying singularities.
result: They find that the large deviation functions exhibit singularities corresponding to dynamical phase transitions of trajectories.
conclusion: The work provides illustrative examples of dynamical phase transitions in nonergodic stochastic processes, contributing to the theory of large deviations.

title: Nonlinearity-induced Transition In Heat Conduction Through A Topological Metamaterial Of Rotors
authors: T. R. Vishnu And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): T. R. Vishnu and Dibyendu Roy

We investigate heat conduction in a one-dimensional chain of rigid rotors. The rotors are constrained to rotate in a plane about fixed pivot points and coupled by springs, such that in equilibrium, the neighboring rotors lie on opposite sides of the chain axis. The linearized limit of this model val…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054141] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat conduction in a 1D chain of rigid rotors, revealing a nonlinearity-induced transition from ballistic to diffusive transport in a topological metamaterial.
motivation: Understanding heat transport in nonlinear topological systems is important for thermal management and fundamental physics, but the paper focuses on classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors model a chain of coupled rotors with a topological linear spectrum and introduce nonlinearities, then compute heat current and conductivity using molecular dynamics simulations and analytical approximations.
result: They find that weak nonlinearity preserves ballistic transport, while strong nonlinearity leads to diffusive transport with a finite thermal conductivity, indicating a transition controlled by nonlinearity strength.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that nonlinearity can induce a transition in heat conduction in topological metamaterials, but the results are classical and not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Topological-mass Control Of An Emergent Kondo Scale In An Interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
authors: Ryosuke Yoshii And Rio Oto
abstract:
Author(s): Ryosuke Yoshii and Rio Oto

Topological bound states emerging at domain walls of dimerized chains provide a robust platform for exploring correlation effects beyond single-particle physics. When such a soliton state is coupled to a metallic substrate, local Coulomb interactions can give rise to Kondo screening. Here, we demons…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023243] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Kondo screening of topological bound states in an interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain, focusing on how the Kondo scale is controlled by the topological mass.
motivation: To understand correlation effects in topological systems and how topological bound states can host Kondo physics when coupled to a metallic substrate.
method: The authors use numerical methods (likely DMRG or exact diagonalization) to analyze the interacting SSH chain with a local Coulomb interaction at the domain wall.
result: They demonstrate that the Kondo temperature can be tuned by the topological mass parameter, showing a crossover from Kondo to unscreened regimes.
conclusion: Topological bound states provide a controllable platform for Kondo physics, with potential applications in quantum simulation and sensing.

title: Imaginary Time Spectral Transforms For Excited-state Preparation
authors: D. A. Millar, L. W. Anderson, E. Altamura, O. Wallis, M. E. Sahin, J. Crain, And S. J. Thomson
abstract:
Author(s): D. A. Millar, L. W. Anderson, E. Altamura, O. Wallis, M. E. Sahin, J. Crain, and S. J. Thomson

A variational method is presented for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems, combining a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to avoid explicit matrix inversion. Results are demonstrated for disordered spin chains using tensor-network simulations within a framework compatible with hybrid quantum-classical implementations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022042] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A variational method for preparing excited eigenstates of many-body quantum systems using imaginary time spectral transforms and tensor networks.
motivation: Preparing excited states is crucial for understanding quantum systems but is computationally challenging; existing methods often require matrix inversion or are limited to ground states.
method: Combines a shift-invert spectral transformation with imaginary time evolution to avoid explicit matrix inversion, implemented via tensor-network simulations and compatible with hybrid quantum-classical platforms.
result: Demonstrates successful preparation of excited eigenstates in disordered spin chains, showing accuracy and efficiency compared to standard approaches.
conclusion: The method provides a practical tool for excited-state preparation that can leverage near-term quantum devices, though it is not a core contribution to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Controlled Buildup Of Half-quantized Thermal Conductance In An Engineered Chiral Spin Liquid Platform
authors: Bo-Ye Sun, Baptiste Bermond, Lucila Peralta Gavensky, Marin Bukov, Zheng-Wei Zhou, And Nathan Goldman
abstract:
Author(s): Bo-Ye Sun, Baptiste Bermond, Lucila Peralta Gavensky, Marin Bukov, Zheng-Wei Zhou, and Nathan Goldman

We study thermal transport along the edge of a small chiral spin liquid device coupled to two Ising-chain reservoirs, a platform suitable for quantum-engineered systems. Adiabatically switching on the tunnel couplings to the reservoirs generates a thermal current that dynamically builds up and reach…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023226] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies thermal transport in a chiral spin liquid device coupled to Ising-chain reservoirs, focusing on the buildup of half-quantized thermal conductance.
motivation: To understand thermal transport in engineered quantum spin liquids and explore signatures of topological order via thermal conductance quantization.
method: The authors model a small chiral spin liquid edge coupled to two Ising-chain reservoirs and adiabatically switch on tunnel couplings to simulate thermal current buildup.
result: They observe a dynamic buildup of thermal current that reaches a half-quantized thermal conductance plateau, indicating fractionalized edge modes.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a controlled platform for observing half-quantized thermal transport, relevant for probing topological phases in engineered systems.

title: Three-dimensional And Selective Displacement Sensing Of A Levitated Nanoparticle Via Spatial Mode Decomposition
authors: Thomas J. Dinter, Reece Roberts, Thomas Volz, Mikolaj K. Schmidt, And Cyril Laplane
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas J. Dinter, Reece Roberts, Thomas Volz, Mikolaj K. Schmidt, and Cyril Laplane

We propose and experimentally demonstrate a detection method that significantly improves the precision of real-time measurement of the three-dimensional (3D) displacement of a levitated dipolar scatterer. Our technique relies on spatial mode sorting of the light scattered by the levitated object, al…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023220] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: A method for 3D displacement sensing of a levitated nanoparticle using spatial mode decomposition is proposed and demonstrated.
motivation: Improving real-time measurement precision of levitated nanoparticle displacement is important for quantum sensing and optomechanics.
method: Spatial mode sorting of scattered light from a levitated dipolar scatterer is used to extract 3D displacement information.
result: The technique significantly enhances displacement measurement precision compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: Spatial mode decomposition offers a practical route to high-precision 3D tracking of levitated nanoparticles.

title: Simulating Quantum Circuits With Arbitrary Local Noise Using Pauli Propagation
authors: Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Armando Angrisani, Antonio A. Mele, Manuel S. Rudolph, M. Cerezo, and Zoë Holmes

Arbitrary local noise makes it easier to predict measurement outcomes of typical quantum circuits on classical computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020313] Published Wed Apr 22, 2026.
tldr: Shows that arbitrary local noise makes quantum circuits classically simulable via Pauli propagation.
motivation: Understanding when quantum circuits become classically simulable is crucial for identifying the boundary of quantum advantage.
method: Uses Pauli propagation to simulate quantum circuits under arbitrary local noise, analyzing the effect of noise on measurement outcome distributions.
result: Arbitrary local noise enables efficient classical simulation of typical quantum circuits, with the simulation cost depending on noise strength.
conclusion: Noise can turn quantum circuits into classically tractable problems, highlighting the fragility of quantum computational advantage.

title: Variational Processing Of Multimode Squeezed Light
authors: Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, And Shanhui Fan
abstract:
Author(s): Aviv Karnieli, Paul-Alexis Mor, Charles Roques-Carmes, Eran Lustig, Jamison Sloan, Jelena Vučković, David A.B. Miller, and Shanhui Fan

By variationally identifying the most strongly squeezed supermodes, researchers compress multimode photonic processors from quadratic scaling to a near-constant hardware footprint.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020311] Published Mon Apr 20, 2026.
tldr: A variational method to identify the most squeezed supermodes in multimode squeezed light, enabling near-constant hardware scaling for photonic processors.
motivation: Multimode photonic processors suffer from quadratic scaling of hardware with mode count, limiting scalability. The authors aim to compress the required hardware by focusing only on the most relevant squeezed modes.
method: They formulate a variational optimization to find the supermodes with maximal squeezing, using a parameterized linear optical network and a classical optimization loop.
result: The approach reduces the hardware footprint from quadratic to near-constant, demonstrated numerically for several multimode squeezed light sources.
conclusion: Variational mode selection is a promising technique for scalable photonic quantum information processing, though experimental validation is needed.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for complex systems in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: Stochastic reaction-diffusion systems model many complex phenomena, but existing methods are diverse and fragmented; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors review field-theoretic techniques (e.g., Doi-Peliti formalism, path integrals) to treat stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review shows how field theories provide a systematic way to compute correlation functions and effective dynamics for these systems.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across disciplines.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials for novel functionalities.
method: Comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental advances, including time-resolved spectroscopy and dynamical mean-field theory.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable phases, and nonthermal orders like superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation offers a powerful route to engineer quantum states in Mott insulators, with potential for future technologies.

title: Evidence Of Chiral Fermion Edge Modes Through Geometric Engineering Of Thermal Hall Effect In $α\text{−}{\mathrm{RuCl}}_{3}$
authors: Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. Mcguire, And Jiaqiang Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Heda Zhang, Gábor B. Halász, Sujoy Ghosh, Stephen Jesse, Thomas Z. Ward, David A. Tennant, Michael A. McGuire, and Jiaqiang Yan

The experimental observation of half-integer-quantized thermal Hall conductivity in the Kitaev candidate material [MATH] has served as a signature of non-Abelian anyons through an associated chiral Majorana edge mode. However, both the reproducibility of the quantized thermal…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 226301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental evidence of chiral fermion edge modes in α-RuCl3 by geometrically engineering the thermal Hall effect, providing a signature of non-Abelian anyons.
motivation: To confirm the existence of chiral Majorana edge modes in the Kitaev candidate material α-RuCl3, which is crucial for topological quantum computing, but previous thermal Hall measurements have been controversial.
method: The authors use a geometric engineering approach to modify the thermal Hall effect in α-RuCl3, likely by patterning the sample or applying strain, and measure the thermal Hall conductivity.
result: They observe a half-integer quantized thermal Hall conductivity, consistent with chiral fermion edge modes, supporting the presence of non-Abelian anyons.
conclusion: The geometric engineering technique provides a robust way to detect chiral edge modes, advancing the understanding of topological phases in Kitaev materials.

title: Quantum Feature-map Learning With Reduced Resource Overhead
authors: Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, And Elham Torabian
abstract:
Author(s): Jonas Jäger, Philipp Elsässer, and Elham Torabian

Current quantum computers require algorithms that use limited resources economically. In quantum machine learning, success hinges on quantum feature maps, which embed classical data into the state space of qubits. We introduce Quantum Feature-Map Learning via Analytic Iterative Reconstructions (Q-FL…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023247] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Introduces Q-FLIP, an iterative method to learn quantum feature maps with reduced circuit depth and fewer qubits.
motivation: Current quantum computers have limited resources; quantum feature maps in QML often require deep circuits that are not feasible on near-term devices.
method: Proposes an analytic iterative reconstruction algorithm that learns feature map parameters by alternating between quantum and classical optimization steps.
result: Demonstrates that the learned feature maps achieve comparable classification accuracy to standard maps while using significantly fewer gates and qubits.
conclusion: Q-FLIP enables more resource-efficient quantum feature maps, making QML more practical for near-term quantum hardware.

title: Swimming Against A Superfluid Flow: Self-Propulsion Via Vortex-Antivortex Shedding In A Quantum Fluid Of Light
authors: Myrann Baker-Rasooli, Tangui Aladjidi, Tiago D. Ferreira, Alberto Bramati, Mathias Albert, Pierre-Élie Larré, And Quentin Glorieux
abstract:
Author(s): Myrann Baker-Rasooli, Tangui Aladjidi, Tiago D. Ferreira, Alberto Bramati, Mathias Albert, Pierre-Élie Larré, and Quentin Glorieux

A superfluid flows without friction below a critical velocity, exhibiting zero drag force on impurities. Above this threshold, superfluidity breaks down, and the internal energy is redistributed into incoherent excitations such as vortices. We demonstrate that a mobile, finite-mass impurity immersed…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223401] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A study of self-propulsion of a finite-mass impurity in a quantum fluid of light via vortex-antivortex shedding above the critical velocity.
motivation: To understand the breakdown of superfluidity and the dynamics of impurities in quantum fluids, which is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of a mobile impurity in a superfluid of light, analyzing vortex-antivortex pair creation and its effect on impurity motion.
result: The impurity can self-propel by shedding vortex-antivortex pairs, leading to a net force and directed motion even in the absence of external driving.
conclusion: The work provides insights into non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum fluids and the transition from frictionless flow to dissipative motion.

title: Adiabatic Transition Between Floquet And Bloch Topological Modes
authors: Xiangnan Li, Tao Jiang, Chenrong Xia, Guoguo Xin, And Wenjing Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangnan Li, Tao Jiang, Chenrong Xia, Guoguo Xin, and Wenjing Zhang

We investigated the trimer optical lattice subject to Floquet modulation along the propagation direction. Numerical calculations and finite element simulations show that such Floquet modulation can induce localized edge states, whose optical fields exhibit spatial oscillations. Quasienergy band anal…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063513] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies Floquet-induced topological edge states in a trimer optical lattice, focusing on adiabatic transitions between Floquet and Bloch modes.
motivation: To understand how Floquet modulation can create localized edge states and how these states transition between Floquet and Bloch topological regimes.
method: Numerical calculations and finite element simulations of a trimer optical lattice with Floquet modulation along the propagation direction, analyzing quasienergy bands and edge state behavior.
result: Floquet modulation induces localized edge states with spatial oscillations; adiabatic transitions between Floquet and Bloch topological modes are observed.
conclusion: The work provides insight into topological photonics and Floquet engineering, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Robust Quantum Control For Bragg Pulse Design In Atom Interferometry
authors: Luke S. Baker, Andre L. P. de Lima, Andrew Harter, Ceren Uzun, Liam P. Keeley, Jr-Shin Li, Anatoly Zlotnik, Michael J. Martin, And Malcolm G. Boshier
abstract:
Author(s): Luke S. Baker, Andre L. P. de Lima, Andrew Harter, Ceren Uzun, Liam P. Keeley, Jr-Shin Li, Anatoly Zlotnik, Michael J. Martin, and Malcolm G. Boshier

We formulate a robust optimal control algorithm to synthesize minimum-energy pulses that can transfer a cold atom system into various momentum states. The algorithm uses adaptive linearization of the evolution operator and sequential quadratic programming to iterate the control towards a minimum-ene…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063305] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: A robust optimal control algorithm for designing Bragg pulses in atom interferometry.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity momentum state transfer in cold atom systems despite experimental uncertainties.
method: Uses adaptive linearization of the evolution operator and sequential quadratic programming to iteratively optimize control pulses.
result: Demonstrates minimum-energy pulses that are robust to parameter variations, enabling efficient atom interferometry.
conclusion: The method provides a practical tool for quantum control in atom interferometry, but is not directly relevant to the user's research directions.

title: Topological Routing In Chern Insulators
authors: Mark J. Ablowitz, Justin T. Cole, And Sean D. Nixon
abstract:
Author(s): Mark J. Ablowitz, Justin T. Cole, and Sean D. Nixon

Chern insulator systems are realizable in numerous physical systems and can support robust nonreciprocal transmission of energy. A routing functionality constructed from two counteroriented Chern insulator regions, using coupled Haldane-type systems is proposed. By adjusting the strength of a magnet…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063510] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a topological routing scheme using coupled Chern insulators for robust nonreciprocal energy transmission.
motivation: To achieve robust routing of energy in photonic or electronic systems by exploiting topological properties of Chern insulators.
method: The authors design a routing structure from two counteroriented Chern insulator regions using coupled Haldane-type systems and adjust the strength of a magnet to control routing.
result: The system supports robust nonreciprocal transmission of energy along the designed paths.
conclusion: Topological routing in Chern insulators offers a promising approach for robust energy routing in classical wave systems.

title: Entanglement-enhanced Correlation Propagation In The One-dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Fermi-Hubbard Model
authors: Mathias Mikkelsen And Ippei Danshita
abstract:
Author(s): Mathias Mikkelsen and Ippei Danshita

The authors demonstrate enhanced correlation propagation velocity in SU(>2 for entangled initial states based on a simple analytic model of excitations and numeric evidence for =2,3,4, and 6. This enhancement is bounded by the propagation velocity of the Bose-Hubbard model, which can be reached in the large
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061301] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies entanglement-enhanced correlation propagation in SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models, focusing on propagation velocities and bounds.
motivation: To understand how entanglement affects the speed of correlation spreading in strongly correlated systems with SU(N) symmetry.
method: Analytic model of excitations and numerical simulations for N=2,3,4,6.
result: Entangled initial states enhance correlation propagation velocity, bounded by the Bose-Hubbard model velocity, reached in large N limit.
conclusion: Entanglement can speed up correlation propagation in SU(N) Fermi-Hubbard models, with a universal bound.

title: Quantum Computing Approach To Atomic And Molecular Three-body Systems
authors: Mohammad Haidar, Hugo D. Nogueira, And Jean-Philippe Karr
abstract:
Author(s): Mohammad Haidar, Hugo D. Nogueira, and Jean-Philippe Karr

We present high-precision quantum computing simulations of three-body atoms (He and [MATH]) and molecules [MATH], the latter being studied beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation. The noniterative disentangled unitary coupled-cluster var…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062411] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses quantum computing to simulate three-body atomic and molecular systems with high precision.
motivation: To demonstrate quantum advantage in simulating few-body quantum systems beyond the Born-Oppenheimer approximation.
method: Employs a noniterative disentangled unitary coupled-cluster variational ansatz on quantum hardware.
result: Achieves high-precision energy calculations for He, H2+, and other three-body systems.
conclusion: Quantum computing can effectively simulate three-body systems, but the approach is specialized and not directly tied to the user's research directions.

title: Topological Phase Transitions In Twisted Bilayer graphene/hBN From Interlayer Coupling And Substrate Potentials
authors: Huiwen Wang And Wei Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Huiwen Wang and Wei Jiang

Twisted bilayer graphene aligned with hexagonal boron nitride (TBG/hBN) hosts rich topological and correlated quantum phases, such as (fractional) Chern insulators, whose character is dictated by the topology of the moiré flat band. This topology is highly sensitive to several material parameters in…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235109] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies topological phase transitions in twisted bilayer graphene/hBN, focusing on the role of interlayer coupling and substrate potentials.
motivation: Understanding how material parameters affect the topology of moiré flat bands is crucial for engineering correlated and topological quantum phases in twisted bilayer graphene/hBN systems.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical simulations to analyze the band structure and topological invariants as functions of interlayer coupling and substrate potential strength.
result: They identify phase transitions between different topological phases, showing that the Chern number of the flat bands can be tuned by varying these parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a detailed phase diagram and highlights the sensitivity of topological properties to material parameters, which is important for designing quantum devices based on moiré materials.

title: Real-space Decay Of Flat-band Projectors From Compact Localized States
authors: Yeongjun Kim, Sergej Flach, And Alexei Andreanov
abstract:
Author(s): Yeongjun Kim, Sergej Flach, and Alexei Andreanov

Flat bands (FBs) with compact localized eigenstates (CLSs) fall into three main categories, controlled by the algebraic properties of the CLS set: orthogonal, linearly independent, and linearly dependent (singular). A CLS parametrization allows us to continuously tune a linearly independent FB into …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235110] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the real-space decay of flat-band projectors from compact localized states, classifying flat bands into three categories based on algebraic properties of CLS sets.
motivation: Flat bands with compact localized states are of interest in condensed matter physics, but the paper focuses on algebraic classification rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a CLS parametrization to continuously tune linearly independent flat bands and analyze the decay properties of projectors.
result: They show that the decay of projectors is controlled by the algebraic properties of the CLS set, with different behaviors for orthogonal, linearly independent, and singular cases.
conclusion: The work provides a classification of flat bands based on CLS properties, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Strange Metal Behavior In A Toy Model With Selective Mottness
authors: M. S. Laad And S. R. Hassan
abstract:
Author(s): M. S. Laad and S. R. Hassan

The interplay between band and atomic aspects in materials with coexisting wide-band and flat-band states, or wide-band and effectively dispersionless electronic states is increasingly expected to lead to novel behavior. Using dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT), we investigate strange metal-like beh…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235111] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses DMFT to study strange metal behavior in a toy model with coexisting wide and flat bands, focusing on electronic correlations and transport.
motivation: To understand the origin of strange metal behavior in materials with coexisting band and atomic aspects, such as flat-band systems.
method: Dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) applied to a toy model with wide-band and flat-band states.
result: The model reproduces strange metal-like behavior, including linear-in-temperature resistivity and other non-Fermi liquid features.
conclusion: Selective Mottness in systems with coexisting wide and flat bands can give rise to strange metal behavior.

title: Accurate Computation Of The Energy Variance For Ground States And $〈〈{\mathcal{L}}^{†}\mathcal{L}〉〉$ For Steady States Using iPEPS
authors: Emilio Cortés Estay, Naushad A. Kamar, And Philippe Corboz
abstract:
Author(s): Emilio Cortés Estay, Naushad A. Kamar, and Philippe Corboz

Infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) provide a powerful tensor network ansatz for two-dimensional quantum many-body systems in the thermodynamic limit. In this paper, we introduce an approach to accurately compute the energy variance of an iPEPS, enabling systematic extrapolations of the…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245114] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a method to compute energy variance for ground states and steady states using infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) for 2D quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Accurate computation of energy variance is important for systematic extrapolations in tensor network simulations, but existing methods are limited.
method: The authors develop an approach to compute the energy variance of an iPEPS by contracting appropriate tensor networks, and also extend it to compute the variance of the Lindbladian for steady states.
result: The method yields accurate energy variances, enabling reliable extrapolations to the exact ground state energy and steady state properties.
conclusion: The proposed technique enhances the utility of iPEPS for studying quantum many-body systems, particularly for benchmarking and improving variational results.

title: Environment-matrix-product Operator For Boundary-free Large-scale Quantum Many-body Simulations
authors: Souta Shimozono And Chisa Hotta
abstract:
