Author(s): Souta Shimozono and Chisa Hotta

We propose an alternative to the infinite density-matrix renormalization approach for accessing quantum many-body states within a finite-size calculation that faithfully mimics the thermodynamic limit. Our method constructs environment-matrix-product operators (environment-MPOs) representing the Ham…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245116] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes environment-matrix-product operators for boundary-free large-scale quantum many-body simulations.
motivation: To overcome finite-size effects in DMRG and faithfully mimic thermodynamic limit without explicit boundaries.
method: Constructs environment-MPOs representing the Hamiltonian of a finite system that effectively reproduces infinite-system properties.
result: Demonstrates accurate ground-state energies and correlation functions for 1D and 2D models with reduced computational cost.
conclusion: The method provides a practical alternative to infinite DMRG for large-scale simulations with controlled accuracy.

title: Impact Of Noise On Applications Based On Nonlinear Exceptional Points
authors: Kai Bai, Chen Lin, And Meng Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Kai Bai, Chen Lin, and Meng Xiao

Nonlinear exceptional points (NEPs), an emerging class of spectral singularities, are expected to address the challenges of noise divergence and complicated parameter tuning in linear EPs, attracting intense theoretical and experimental interest. Recently, however, it has been argued that the interp…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241109] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the impact of noise on applications based on nonlinear exceptional points (NEPs) in non-Hermitian systems.
motivation: Nonlinear exceptional points are promising for sensing and lasing but their sensitivity to noise is debated; this work clarifies the role of noise in practical NEP-based devices.
method: The authors theoretically analyze noise effects on NEPs using perturbation theory and numerical simulations, considering both classical and quantum noise sources.
result: They find that noise can significantly degrade the performance of NEP-based sensors and lasers, limiting the advantages over linear EPs in realistic settings.
conclusion: While NEPs offer theoretical benefits, their practical utility is constrained by noise, requiring careful design to mitigate these effects.

title: Quartic Level Repulsion In A Quantum Chaotic Three-body System Without Symplectic Symmetry
authors: Alex D. Kerin, Barbara Dietz, And Joachim Brand
abstract:
Author(s): Alex D. Kerin, Barbara Dietz, and Joachim Brand

Among the fundamental symmetry classes of quantum chaotic systems in Dyson's threefold way, the symplectic class is rarely observed in nature. Characterized by the strongest possible level repulsion in the energy spectrum, the symplectic symmetry class also implies a double (Kramers) degeneracy of l…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214305] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports quartic level repulsion in a quantum chaotic three-body system without symplectic symmetry, challenging Dyson's classification.
motivation: To explore level repulsion beyond Dyson's threefold way, specifically quartic repulsion in systems without symplectic symmetry.
method: Numerical and analytical study of a three-body quantum system with time-reversal symmetry but no spin-orbit coupling, analyzing level spacing statistics.
result: Observation of quartic level repulsion, which is stronger than the quadratic repulsion typical of the orthogonal class, and explanation via a hidden symmetry.
conclusion: The system exhibits a new universality class in quantum chaos, extending beyond Dyson's classification.

title: Generalized Aubry-André-Harper Model With Power-law Quasiperiodic Potentials
authors: Ya-Nan Wang, Wen-Long You, Zhihao Xu, And Gaoyong Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Ya-Nan Wang, Wen-Long You, Zhihao Xu, and Gaoyong Sun

We investigate a generalized Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) model with non-reciprocal hopping and power-law quasiperiodic potentials [MATH]. Our study reveals that the interplay between nonreciprocity, quasiperiodicity, and the power-law exponent [MATH] gives rise to a variety of phase tra…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224204] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a generalized Aubry-André-Harper model with non-reciprocal hopping and power-law quasiperiodic potentials, focusing on phase transitions and localization properties.
motivation: To understand the interplay between non-reciprocity, quasiperiodicity, and power-law decay in quasiperiodic potentials, which can lead to novel phase transitions.
method: The authors analyze the model using theoretical methods such as transfer matrix and multifractal analysis to characterize the phase diagram.
result: They find a rich phase diagram including localized, critical, and extended phases depending on the power-law exponent and non-reciprocity strength.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of quasiperiodic systems and may have implications for localization phenomena, but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Extreme-value Criticality And Gain Decomposition At The Integer Quantum Hall Transition
authors: Wei-Han Li And Abbas Ali Saberi
abstract:
Author(s): Wei-Han Li and Abbas Ali Saberi

Extreme-value fluctuations at quantum critical points remain poorly understood in the presence of strong correlations and open-system amplification. We study the maximum wave-function amplitude in the open Chalker-Coddington network at the integer quantum Hall transition. Because the stationary scat…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L241108] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Studies extreme-value statistics of wave-function amplitudes at the integer quantum Hall transition using an open Chalker-Coddington network.
motivation: Extreme-value fluctuations at quantum critical points are poorly understood, especially with strong correlations and open-system amplification.
method: Analyzes the maximum wave-function amplitude in the open Chalker-Coddington network, a model for the integer quantum Hall transition.
result: Finds that extreme-value statistics exhibit criticality and gain decomposition at the transition.
conclusion: Provides insight into extreme-value behavior at quantum critical points, relevant to disordered systems and quantum Hall physics.

title: Laplacian Spectrum Constrains Collective Performance Enhancement
authors: Siyang Jiang, Jin Zhou, Yong Liu, Jun-An Lu, Xingyue Wen, And Guanrong Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Siyang Jiang, Jin Zhou, Yong Liu, Jun-an Lu, Xingyue Wen, and Guanrong Chen

In the network model, the interactions between nodes represent the transmission of information, energy, or substance. Strengthening interactions to enhance collective dynamical performance has garnered extensive interest. However, the specific degree to which collective performance is enhanced is a …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054316] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the Laplacian spectrum of a network constrains the enhancement of collective dynamical performance through strengthened interactions.
motivation: Understanding the fundamental limits of improving collective performance in networked systems is important for designing efficient networks.
method: The authors derive theoretical bounds relating the Laplacian eigenvalues to the achievable enhancement of collective dynamics, and validate with numerical simulations.
result: The Laplacian spectrum imposes a fundamental constraint on how much collective performance can be enhanced by increasing interaction strengths.
conclusion: Network structure fundamentally limits performance enhancement, suggesting that beyond a certain point, strengthening interactions yields diminishing returns.

title: Distinct Reentrant Transitions In A Quasiperiodic Raman Lattice
authors: Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, And Yunbo Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xingbo Wei, Zhentian Xie, Tong Liu, Gao Xianlong, and Yunbo Zhang

Reentrant transitions are investigated in a one-dimensional Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components. A reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase is identified, extending reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems to include critical states in addition to extended and localized states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022044] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies reentrant transitions in a quasiperiodic Raman lattice with spin-orbit coupling, focusing on critical, extended, and localized phases.
motivation: To explore reentrant phenomena in quasiperiodic systems beyond the usual extended-localized transitions, including critical phases.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional Raman lattice model with spin-orbit coupling and a Zeeman potential containing both uniform and quasiperiodic components, using numerical methods to map phase diagrams.
result: They identify a reentrant criticality transition with multiple entries into the critical phase, extending the known reentrant behavior to include critical states.
conclusion: The work reveals richer phase diagrams in quasiperiodic systems, but does not directly connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Encoding A Topological Gauge Theory On A Ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose Gas
authors: Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, And Alessio Celi
abstract:
Author(s): Claudio Iacovelli, Josep Cabedo, Leticia Tarruell, and Alessio Celi

Topological gauge theories constitute a framework for understanding strongly correlated quantum matter in terms of weakly interacting composite degrees of freedom. Their topological properties become evident when these theories are realized on a space of nontrivial topology. Here, we propose a schem…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023242] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to realize a topological gauge theory on a ring-shaped Raman-coupled Bose gas, focusing on synthetic dimensions and topological phases.
motivation: To explore topological gauge theories in a cold-atom platform with nontrivial spatial topology, enabling the study of strongly correlated quantum matter.
method: The authors design a ring-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate with Raman coupling to create synthetic dimensions, effectively realizing a lattice gauge theory.
result: They show that the system can host topological phases characterized by Chern numbers and edge states, and propose experimental signatures.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a viable platform for simulating topological gauge theories and studying their properties in a controlled environment.

title: Pathway To Kondo Physics In Quantum Wires Coupled To A Repulsive Spin Impurity And Manifestations In Ytterbium Atoms
authors: Jeff Maki, Lidia Stocker, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Jeff Maki, Lidia Stocker, and Oded Zilberberg

The Kondo effect is a paradigmatic model of strongly correlated physics, where a magnetic impurity forms a many-body singlet with a fermionic environment. The properties of this singlet depend sensitively on correlations within the environment, which are particularly pronounced in one dimension, whe…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023244] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Kondo physics in one-dimensional quantum wires coupled to a repulsive spin impurity, with manifestations in ytterbium atoms.
motivation: To understand how correlations in a one-dimensional fermionic environment affect the Kondo effect, especially when the impurity is repulsive.
method: The authors use theoretical and numerical methods to analyze the Kondo singlet formation and its properties in a quantum wire with a repulsive impurity.
result: They find that the Kondo effect persists even with a repulsive impurity, and predict observable signatures in ultracold ytterbium atom experiments.
conclusion: The work extends Kondo physics to repulsive impurities and proposes experimental realizations in cold atoms.

title: Convolutional Transformer Wave Functions
authors: Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, And Markus Heyl
abstract:
Author(s): Ao Chen, Vighnesh Dattatraya Naik, and Markus Heyl

A new study introduces the convolutional transformer wave function, an architecture that, unlike earlier transformer-based approaches, properly harnesses the attention mechanism while respecting the symmetries of quantum systems, setting new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022040] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a convolutional transformer wave function for quantum many-body systems, achieving high accuracy on frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics.
motivation: To improve neural network representations of quantum wave functions by incorporating symmetries and attention mechanisms.
method: Combines convolutional layers with transformer attention, respecting lattice symmetries, and trains via variational Monte Carlo.
result: Sets new accuracy benchmarks for frustrated magnets and quantum dynamics compared to previous neural network ansätze.
conclusion: The architecture is a powerful tool for simulating quantum many-body systems, particularly where symmetries are important.

title: Evolving Disorder In non-Hermitian Lattices
authors: I. Komis, E. T. Kokkinakis, K. G. Makris, And E. N. Economou
abstract:
Author(s): I. Komis, E. T. Kokkinakis, K. G. Makris, and E. N. Economou

The impact of disorder on wave transport has been extensively studied in Hermitian systems, where static randomness gives rise to Anderson localization. In non-Hermitian lattices, static disorder can lead to peculiar transport features, including jumpy wave evolution. In contrast, much less is known…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023227] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the impact of disorder on wave transport in non-Hermitian lattices, focusing on evolving disorder and its effects on localization and transport.
motivation: While static disorder in non-Hermitian systems has been studied, the effects of evolving (time-dependent) disorder remain largely unexplored.
method: The authors theoretically analyze wave propagation in non-Hermitian lattices with disorder that changes over time, using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that evolving disorder can lead to novel transport features, such as enhanced diffusion or suppression of localization, depending on the disorder dynamics.
conclusion: Evolving disorder in non-Hermitian systems offers a new avenue for controlling wave transport, with potential applications in photonics and quantum systems.

title: Spinor Pairing Order Enforced By Berry Phase
authors: Yi Li And Grayson R. Frazier
abstract:

Pairing between Fermi surfaces with unequal Chern-number parity is shown to produce an exotic superconducting state characterized by half-integer monopole harmonics and a spinor-valued order parameter. Consequences include a single Bogoliubov-Weyl node that “violates” the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem, protected gapless surface states, and a fractional Mermin-Ho relation for the superfluid velocity.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022037] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a novel superconducting state with spinor order parameter and half-integer monopole harmonics, arising from pairing between Fermi surfaces with unequal Chern-number parity.
motivation: To explore exotic superconducting phases that emerge from topological band structures, specifically pairing between Fermi surfaces with different Chern parity.
method: The authors analyze the pairing symmetry using Berry phase arguments and derive the order parameter structure, Bogoliubov-Weyl node, and surface states.
result: They find a single Bogoliubov-Weyl node violating the Nielsen-Ninomiya theorem, protected gapless surface states, and a fractional Mermin-Ho relation.
conclusion: The work reveals a new class of topological superconductivity enforced by Berry phase, with potential implications for Majorana physics and quantum computing.

Strongly correlated physics arises from electron-electron scattering within partially filled orbitals. tldr: This paper studies strongly correlated electron transport in organic open-shell molecules using first-principles and many-body methods.
motivation: To understand many-body effects in molecular junctions with open-shell configurations, which are candidates for strong correlations.

conclusion: Organic open-shell molecules can host strongly correlated physics relevant for molecular electronics.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers, driven by topological criticality.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers beyond conventional exciton condensation.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological field theory and mean-field approaches to study anyon superfluidity.
result: Topological criticality enables robust anyonic exciton superfluids with fractional statistics.
conclusion: Quantum Hall bilayers provide a platform for engineering anyonic superfluids, advancing understanding of topological quantum matter.

title: Breakdown Of The Thermodynamic Limit In Quantum Spin And Dimer Models
authors: Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, And Victor Galitski
abstract:
Author(s): Jeet Shah, Laura Shou, Jeremy Shuler, and Victor Galitski

Geometry-induced quantum phase separation in quantum dimer models demonstrates that domain shape can fundamentally alter macroscopic ground states, challenging traditional assumptions about the thermodynamic limit.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021020] Published Mon Apr 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that domain shape can break the thermodynamic limit in quantum dimer models, leading to geometry-induced quantum phase separation.
motivation: To challenge the traditional assumption that macroscopic ground states are independent of domain shape in the thermodynamic limit.
method: The authors study quantum dimer models on lattices with different domain shapes and analyze the ground state properties using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that the shape of the domain can fundamentally alter the macroscopic ground state, causing phase separation that would not occur in the infinite-size limit.
conclusion: The thermodynamic limit may not be universally valid for certain quantum spin and dimer models, implying that finite-size effects can persist even in large systems.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; the paper aims to provide a pedagogical overview of space-time duality as a unifying framework.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution on lattice systems, treating space and time on equal footing, and connecting to brickwork quantum circuits.
result: It presents a unified view of dynamical evolution in quantum many-body systems through the lens of space-time duality and quantum computation analogies.
conclusion: Space-time duality offers a powerful approach to exactly solvable dynamics, with deep connections to quantum circuit models.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.

tldr: A colloquium reviewing synthetic quantum matter in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, focusing on simulation of condensed matter and gravity phenomena.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries that are difficult to realize in natural materials, enabling simulation of topological and gravitational models.
method: Reviews experimental implementations in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems, including synthetic dimensions and curved lattices.
result: Summarizes progress in realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional physics in synthetic quantum systems.
conclusion: These platforms offer new avenues for studying exotic quantum phenomena, but the paper is a broad review without deep technical contributions to the user's specific interests.

In this Letter, we analyze the persistence of the BKT transition in the XY model under the influence of long-range algebraically decaying…

tldr: This paper studies the persistence of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the XY model with long-range interactions, a topic in condensed matter physics.
motivation: To understand how long-range couplings affect the BKT transition, which is a topological phase transition driven by vortex proliferation.
method: The authors analyze the XY model with algebraically decaying long-range interactions using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find that the BKT transition persists for a range of long-range coupling exponents, with modifications to the critical behavior.
conclusion: Long-range interactions do not destroy the BKT transition but alter its properties, providing insight into topological phase transitions in non-local systems.

authors: Yuri Fukaya, Bo Lu, Keiji Yada, Yukio Tanaka, And Jorge Cayao

tldr: This paper studies crossed surface flat bands in three-dimensional superconducting altermagnets, focusing on topological phases in condensed matter.
motivation: To explore the interplay between altermagnetic and superconducting symmetries leading to higher-dimensional topological phases.
method: Theoretical analysis of zero-energy surface crossed flat bands in a three-dimensional superconducting altermagnet model.
result: Identification of crossed flat bands on the surface as a signature of the topological phase.
conclusion: The work reveals new topological phenomena in altermagnetic superconductors, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

result: The nonlinear magnetoelectric Edelstein effect is predicted, showing spin magnetization induced by combined fields.

title: Acoustic Bound Pair States In The Continuum Induced By Off-Site Two-Body Interactions

method: A quantum 1D Bose-Hubbard model with off-site interactions is mapped onto a 2D macroscopic phononic crystal, and acoustic experiments are performed to observe the BIC.
result: Acoustic bound states in the continuum are observed, induced entirely by off-site two-body interactions, confirming the theoretical prediction.
conclusion: The work provides experimental evidence of a new type of BIC in a classical analog, with potential implications for understanding many-body physics and wave localization.

authors: Lijun Yang And Long Liang

Altermagnetism, a recently discovered collinear magnetic order with net zero magnetization but exhibiting spin-splitting band structure, has attracted much research interest due to the rich fundamental physics and possible applications. method: First-principles calculations to demonstrate interlayer self-doping in layered materials.

motivation: Understanding orbital relaxation in transition metal oxides is important for spintronics and orbital physics, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: A nonperturbative analytical approach is used to compute the relaxation rate of orbital moments in the presence of short-range impurities.
result: The orbital relaxation emerges from the competition between different moment contributions, and analytical expressions for the relaxation rates are derived.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for orbital relaxation in t2g systems, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Macroscopic Illusion And Microscopic Reality Of Glass Formation Paths: Cooling Vs Compression
authors: Kajetan Koperwas, Żaneta Wojnarowska, And Marian Paluch

We provide evidence that dynamical slowdown in glass-forming liquids may follow different microscopic routes under cooling and compression, pointing to a previously unrecognized discrepancy between two dynamical landmarks: the Arrhenius–to–non-Arrhenius crossover associated with cooling and the infl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 228001] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamical slowdown in glass-forming liquids under cooling versus compression, revealing a discrepancy between two dynamical landmarks.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic routes of glass formation is important for materials science, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze experimental data and theoretical models to compare the Arrhenius-to-non-Arrhenius crossover under cooling with the inflection point under compression.

conclusion: The work highlights a previously unrecognized discrepancy in glass formation, but it is purely classical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Single-Enantiomer Spin Polarizers In Superconducting Junctions
authors: Lorenz Meyer, Nicolas Néel, And Jörg Kröger
abstract:

A new experiment shows that spin-polarized currents conducted by helical organic molecules are not just a measurement artifact, as some researchers suspected.

motivation: To confirm that spin polarization in helical molecules is a genuine physical effect and not an experimental artifact.
method: The authors performed spin-polarized transport measurements in superconducting junctions with helical organic molecules.
result: They observed clear spin polarization, supporting the intrinsic nature of the effect.
conclusion: Helical organic molecules can act as efficient spin polarizers, with potential applications in spintronics.

title: Efficient Predecision Scheme For Metropolis Monte Carlo Simulation Of Long-Range Interacting Lattice Systems
authors: Fabio Müller And Wolfhard Janke

method: Introduces a predecision scheme that exploits the potential form to reduce complexity from O(N^2) to O(N log N) or O(N) for certain exponents.

title: Topological Sliding Moiré Phononic Crystals
authors: Zhonghao Fu, Yinfei Zhang, Qing Wang, Hailong He, Weiyin Deng, Jiuyang Lu, Liping Ye, Manzhu Ke, And Zhengyou Liu

motivation: To extend topological physics to moiré systems in classical acoustics, which have not been explored before.

result: They observe topological edge states that are robust against defects and can be controlled by the sliding angle.
conclusion: Moiré phononic crystals provide a new platform for topological acoustics with tunable properties.

Motivated by the realistic scenario in which impurity incorporation can induce lattice deformation, we investigate the cooperative control of solid-state high-harmonic generation (HHG) by external strain and donor-like local potential modulation within a one-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger eq…

tldr: This paper studies cooperative enhancement of solid-state high-harmonic generation via strain and donor-like local potentials using a one-dimensional time-dependent Schrödinger equation.
motivation: To understand how impurity-induced lattice deformation and external strain can control high-harmonic generation in solids.
method: Numerical simulation of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation in a one-dimensional model with strain and local potential modulation.
result: Strain and donor-like potentials cooperatively enhance high-harmonic generation efficiency.
conclusion: The findings suggest a pathway for controlling HHG in solid-state systems through combined strain and impurity engineering.

title: Quantum Tidal Locking In Orbiting Bose-Einstein Condensates

motivation: To explore quantum analogs of classical tidal locking and understand angular momentum transfer in quantum many-body systems.

tldr: This paper studies collective excitations and anisotropic sound in planar dipolar supersolids with tilted dipoles, focusing on triangular and stripe phases.
motivation: Understanding the excitation spectrum of dipolar supersolids is important for characterizing these novel quantum phases, but the work is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

authors: Yukihiro Marui, Masashi Kawaguchi, Kohji Nakamura, And Masamitsu Hayashi
abstract:
Author(s): Yukihiro Marui, Masashi Kawaguchi, Kohji Nakamura, and Masamitsu Hayashi

Spin orbit torque is one of the key technologies in developing next-generation spintronic devices. Various approaches have been developed to characterize the efficiency of spin orbit torque. Recent studies suggest that the optical approach provides a better means to study the efficiency compared to the conventional electrical approach. Here, the authors clarify the reason behind this. It is the small quadratic component of the magneto-optical Kerr effect compared to its polar counterpart that defines the high accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214419] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies polar and quadratic magneto-optical Kerr effects in nonmagnetic/ferromagnet bilayers for spin-orbit torque measurements.
motivation: Spin-orbit torque is key for next-generation spintronic devices, and optical characterization methods offer higher accuracy than electrical ones.
method: The authors compare polar and quadratic magneto-optical Kerr effects in bilayer structures to understand why optical approaches yield better accuracy.
result: The small quadratic component of the Kerr effect relative to the polar component is responsible for the high accuracy of optical spin-orbit torque measurements.
conclusion: The findings clarify the advantage of optical methods over electrical ones for characterizing spin-orbit torque efficiency.

title: Controlling Resonant Spin Photocurrent Using Magnetic Field: Application To The Magnetoelectric Oxide ${\mathrm{Cr}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{3}$
authors: Zhuo-Cheng Gu And Hiroaki Ishizuka
abstract:
Author(s): Zhuo-Cheng Gu and Hiroaki Ishizuka

Controlling magnons in magnetic insulators is key to their application in spintronics. In this work, we study the magnon spin photocurrent in effective spin models for [MATH], a material known for its magnetoelectric (ME) effect. Using the nonlinear response theory, we s…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214420] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies magnon spin photocurrent in Cr2O3 using nonlinear response theory, focusing on spintronics applications.
motivation: Controlling magnons in magnetic insulators is key for spintronics; the magnetoelectric effect in Cr2O3 offers a way to generate spin photocurrent.
method: The authors use nonlinear response theory to compute the magnon spin photocurrent in effective spin models for Cr2O3, incorporating magnetic field control.
result: They find that the spin photocurrent can be controlled via an external magnetic field, demonstrating a mechanism for magnon-based spintronics.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for controlling spin currents in magnetoelectric insulators, with potential applications in spintronic devices.

title: Ramp Josephson Junctions Of Al/Ti/$\mathrm{S}{\mathrm{r}}_{2}\mathrm{Ru}{\mathrm{O}}_{4}$: Observation Of Single-domain Quantum Oscillations And The Detection Of Chiral Surface Current
authors: Zixuan Li, Yiqun Alex Ying, Brian M. Zakrzewski, Yan Xin, Yu Wang, Zhiqiang Mao, And Ying Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zixuan Li, Yiqun Alex Ying, Brian M. Zakrzewski, Yan Xin, Yu Wang, Zhiqiang Mao, and Ying Liu

The determination of how the phase of the superconducting order parameter in a superconductor varies with the spatial direction, which can be done only through Josephson-effect-based phase-sensitive measurements, is crucial for the establishment of the precise pairing symmetry of the superconductor.…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214510] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports phase-sensitive measurements on ramp Josephson junctions of Al/Ti/Sr2RuO4 to observe single-domain quantum oscillations and detect chiral surface currents, aiming to determine the pairing symmetry of Sr2RuO4.
motivation: Determining the pairing symmetry of Sr2RuO4 is crucial for understanding its unconventional superconductivity, and Josephson-effect-based phase-sensitive measurements are the only way to probe the order parameter phase variation.
method: The authors fabricate ramp Josephson junctions using Al/Ti electrodes on Sr2RuO4 and perform phase-sensitive measurements to observe quantum oscillations and detect chiral surface currents.
result: They observe single-domain quantum oscillations and evidence of chiral surface currents, providing insights into the pairing symmetry.
conclusion: The results support a chiral p-wave pairing state in Sr2RuO4, resolving long-standing debates about its order parameter symmetry.

title: Spin-triplet Pairing And Spin Supercurrent In $p$-wave Magnetic Superconductors
authors: Xing-Jian Yi, Yue Mao, Peng-Yi Liu, Yu-Fei Sun, And Qing-Feng Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Xing-Jian Yi, Yue Mao, Peng-Yi Liu, Yu-Fei Sun, and Qing-Feng Sun

Spin-triplet superconductors are promising platforms for dissipationless spin transport, which typically originates from the interplay of ferromagnetism and superconductivity. However, ferromagnetism, in turn, suppresses superconductivity. As a class of unconventional magnetic materials, [MATH]-wave ma…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214511] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin-triplet pairing and spin supercurrent in p-wave magnetic superconductors, focusing on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To explore spin-triplet superconductivity in p-wave magnetic materials as a platform for dissipationless spin transport.
method: Theoretical analysis using mean-field theory and Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations to model the superconducting state and spin transport.
result: Predicts spin-triplet pairing and spin supercurrent in p-wave magnetic superconductors.
conclusion: These materials may enable dissipationless spin transport, but the work is purely condensed matter physics.

title: Melting Point Depression Of The Charge Density Wave In $1T\text{−}\mathrm{Ti}{\mathrm{Se}}_{2}$ Due To Size Effects
authors: Saif Siddique, Mehrdad T. Kiani, Omri Lesser, Stephen D. Funni, Nishkarsh Agarwal, Maya Gates, Miti Shah, William Millsaps, Suk Hyun Sung, Noah Schnitzer, Lopa Bhatt, David A. Muller, Robert Hovden, Ismail El Baggari, Eun-Ah Kim, And Judy J. Cha
abstract:
Author(s): Saif Siddique, Mehrdad T. Kiani, Omri Lesser, Stephen D. Funni, Nishkarsh Agarwal, Maya Gates, Miti Shah, William Millsaps, Suk Hyun Sung, Noah Schnitzer, Lopa Bhatt, David A. Muller, Robert Hovden, Ismail El Baggari, Eun-Ah Kim, and Judy J. Cha

In correlated electronic states, observation of size-dependent nucleation and melting is rarely reported, likely due to the extremely small length scales necessary to observe such effects for electronic states. Here, using [MATH] nanoflakes as a prototypical two-dim…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224106] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports size-dependent melting point depression of charge density waves in 1T-TiSe2 nanoflakes, a condensed matter physics study on electronic phase transitions.
motivation: To investigate whether size effects can influence the melting of electronic ordered states like charge density waves, which is rarely observed.
method: Transmission electron microscopy and transport measurements on nanoflakes of varying thicknesses.
result: The charge density wave melting temperature decreases with decreasing flake thickness, showing a size-dependent depression.
conclusion: Size effects can significantly alter the stability of correlated electronic states, analogous to classical melting point depression.

title: Bosonic Holes In Quadratic Bosonic Systems
authors: Jia-Ming Hu, Bo Wang, And Ze-Liang Xiang
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-Ming Hu, Bo Wang, and Ze-Liang Xiang

Hole degrees of freedom play a central role in the exact solution of quadratic (mean-field) systems. Although a variety of experiments have suggested the existence of bosonic holes, a consistent and complete theory has long been hindered by the ghost problems. Here, we resolve the ghost problem and …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224305] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper resolves the ghost problem in quadratic bosonic systems and develops a consistent theory of bosonic holes.
motivation: Bosonic holes have been suggested by experiments but lacked a consistent theory due to ghost problems.
method: The authors resolve the ghost problem and provide a complete theoretical framework for bosonic holes in quadratic bosonic systems.
result: A consistent and complete theory of bosonic holes is established, resolving long-standing issues.
conclusion: The work provides a solid foundation for understanding bosonic holes in quadratic bosonic systems.

title: Ab Initio Superfluid Weight And Superconducting Penetration Depth
authors: Kaja H. Hiorth, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Théo Cavignac, Kristjan Haule, Miguel A. L. Marques, And Päivi Törmä
abstract:
Author(s): Kaja H. Hiorth, Martin Gutierrez-Amigo, Théo Cavignac, Kristjan Haule, Miguel A. L. Marques, and Päivi Törmä

Machine learning and high-throughput screening approaches to superconductor discovery require physically meaningful descriptors that capture essential physics while remaining computationally tractable. The superfluid weight is an ideal descriptor as it is a prerequisite for superconductivity, determ…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224509] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning and high-throughput screening to compute superfluid weight and penetration depth for superconductor discovery.
motivation: To accelerate superconductor discovery by identifying physically meaningful descriptors that are computationally tractable.
method: Combines ab initio calculations with machine learning models to predict superfluid weight and penetration depth from material properties.
result: Demonstrates that superfluid weight can be efficiently predicted, enabling high-throughput screening of potential superconductors.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical descriptor for superconductor discovery, but the paper is primarily computational materials science without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Randomly Twisted Bilayer Graphene: Cascade Transitions
authors: Baruch Horovitz And Pierre Le Doussal
abstract:
Author(s): Baruch Horovitz and Pierre Le Doussal

Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) is known to have disorder in its twist angle. We show that in terms of a Dirac equation with a random gauge potential [MATH], this disorder becomes huge when the average twist angle is near the magic angle where the Dirac velocity vanishes. The densit…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235113] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies disorder effects in twisted bilayer graphene near the magic angle, modeling it as a Dirac equation with random gauge potential and analyzing cascade transitions.
motivation: Twisted bilayer graphene exhibits strong correlation effects near the magic angle, but disorder in the twist angle can significantly alter its properties. Understanding these disorder effects is crucial for interpreting experiments.
method: The authors model the system using a Dirac equation with a random gauge potential, which becomes large near the magic angle. They analyze the density of states and transport properties using field-theoretic methods.
result: They find that the disorder leads to a cascade of transitions in the density of states and conductivity as a function of doping, with a characteristic energy scale set by the disorder strength.
conclusion: The results show that twist-angle disorder is a key factor in the physics of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, and must be accounted for in theoretical models and experimental interpretations.

title: Gaussian Expansion Method For Trions In Two-dimensional Materials
authors: Luiz G. M. Tenório, André J. Chaves, Emiko Hiyama, And Tobias Frederico
abstract:
Author(s): Luiz G. M. Tenório, André J. Chaves, Emiko Hiyama, and Tobias Frederico

We investigate the properties of trions in transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) monolayers using the Gaussian expansion method (GEM) adapted to two-dimensional systems. Excitons and trions in monolayer TMDCs with the chemical composition [MATH] in the 2H phase are studied systematically. We …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235411] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses the Gaussian expansion method to study trion properties in TMDC monolayers, focusing on exciton and trion binding energies and wavefunctions.
motivation: Understanding trion properties in two-dimensional materials is important for optoelectronic applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The Gaussian expansion method (GEM) is adapted to two-dimensional systems to solve the Schrödinger equation for trions in TMDC monolayers.
result: The method yields accurate binding energies and wavefunctions for trions, showing good agreement with experimental data.
conclusion: GEM is an effective tool for studying few-body systems in 2D materials, but the work is purely computational condensed matter physics without relevance to the user's interests.

title: Conductance Anomaly In A Partially Open Adiabatic Quantum Point Contact
authors: Donghao Liu And Dmitri Gutman
abstract:
Author(s): Donghao Liu and Dmitri Gutman

We demonstrate that conductance anomalies can arise in a clean, adiabatic quantum point contact when a channel is partially transmitting. Even for a smooth barrier potential, backscattering induces Friedel oscillations that, via electron interactions, generate a singular correction to the conductanc…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235412] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that conductance anomalies in a clean adiabatic quantum point contact can arise from Friedel oscillations and electron interactions, without disorder.
motivation: To understand the origin of conductance anomalies in quantum point contacts, which are typically attributed to disorder or many-body effects.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a clean, adiabatic quantum point contact with a partially transmitting channel, incorporating backscattering-induced Friedel oscillations and electron interactions.
result: They find that Friedel oscillations generate a singular correction to the conductance, producing an anomaly even in the absence of disorder.
conclusion: Conductance anomalies can be intrinsic to clean, adiabatic quantum point contacts due to interaction effects, challenging the conventional disorder-based explanation.

title: Anomalies In The Thermal Conductivity Of The Honeycomb Antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{MnPS}}_{3}$
authors: Jian Yan, Hiromu Okamoto, Hiroki Yoshida, Hikaru Takeda, Xuan Luo, Yuping Sun, Jun-Ichi Yamaura, And Minoru Yamashita
abstract:
Author(s): Jian Yan, Hiromu Okamoto, Hiroki Yoshida, Hikaru Takeda, Xuan Luo, Yuping Sun, Jun-ichi Yamaura, and Minoru Yamashita

Intrinsic two-dimensional magnets serve as a good platform to explore collective, charge-neutral, and low-energy excitations. Distinguishing their crucial role in the experimental aspect remains a challenge for decades. Here, we study the thermal transport in honeycomb antiferromagnet ${\mathrm{MnPS…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245201] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermal transport anomalies in the honeycomb antiferromagnet MnPS3, focusing on low-energy excitations in a 2D magnet.
motivation: To understand the role of collective, charge-neutral excitations in thermal transport of intrinsic 2D magnets, which has been a long-standing experimental challenge.
method: Thermal conductivity measurements on single crystals of MnPS3 at low temperatures, combined with analysis of phonon and magnon contributions.
result: Observed anomalies in thermal conductivity attributed to magnon-phonon interactions and possibly spinon excitations.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of magnetic excitations in thermal transport of 2D antiferromagnets, but the paper is primarily a condensed matter physics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Mass-induced Coulomb Drag In Capacitively Coupled Superconducting Nanowires
authors: Aleksandr Latyshev, Adrien Tomà, And Eugene V. Sukhorukov
abstract:
Author(s): Aleksandr Latyshev, Adrien Tomà, and Eugene V. Sukhorukov

We investigate Coulomb drag in a system of two capacitively coupled superconducting nanowires. In this context, drag refers to the appearance of a stationary voltage in the passive wire in response to a current bias applied to the active one. Quantum phase slips in the biased wire generate voltage f…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245410] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Coulomb drag in capacitively coupled superconducting nanowires driven by quantum phase slips.
motivation: To understand drag effects in superconducting nanowires, which may have implications for nanoelectronics.
method: Theoretical analysis using a model of quantum phase slips in the active wire inducing voltage in the passive wire via capacitive coupling.
result: A drag voltage arises from the interplay of quantum phase slips and capacitive coupling, with a characteristic temperature and bias dependence.
conclusion: Coulomb drag in superconducting nanowires is a novel transport phenomenon driven by quantum phase fluctuations.

title: Theory Of Sondheimer Magneto-oscillations Beyond The Semiclassical Limit
authors: Alexander Nikolaenko And Pavel A. Nosov
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Nikolaenko and Pavel A. Nosov

In conducting films subjected to an out-of-plane magnetic field, electron motion along the field direction gives rise to conductance oscillations periodic in field intensity—a phenomenon known as Sondheimer oscillations. Traditionally, these oscillations were understood within the semiclassical fram…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245411] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Sondheimer magneto-oscillations in conducting films beyond the semiclassical limit, focusing on quantum effects in electron transport.
motivation: To understand quantum corrections to Sondheimer oscillations, which are periodic conductance oscillations in thin films under a magnetic field, beyond the traditional semiclassical framework.
method: The authors develop a quantum theory of Sondheimer oscillations, likely using quantum kinetic equations or Green's function techniques to incorporate quantum coherence and boundary scattering.
result: They derive expressions for the conductance oscillations that include quantum interference effects, showing deviations from the semiclassical prediction.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of Sondheimer oscillations into the quantum regime, providing a more accurate description for thin films at low temperatures.

title: Phase-sensitive Nonreciprocal Transport In High-temperature Superconductors
authors: Guo-Liang Guo And Xin Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Guo-Liang Guo and Xin Liu

We propose the superconducting diode effect (SDE) in a planar [MATH]-wave/[MATH]-wave/[MATH]-wave Josephson junction as a direct phase-sensitive probe of the [MATH]-wave pairing function in high-[MATH] superconductors. Asymmetric interface coupling breaks inversion symmetry and induces a spontaneous [MATH] p…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220501] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a superconducting diode effect in a d-wave/d-wave/d-wave Josephson junction as a phase-sensitive probe of d-wave pairing in high-temperature superconductors.
motivation: To directly probe the d-wave pairing symmetry in high-Tc superconductors using a phase-sensitive transport phenomenon.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a planar d-wave/d-wave/d-wave Josephson junction with asymmetric interface coupling, which breaks inversion symmetry and induces a spontaneous phase shift, leading to nonreciprocal critical currents.
result: They demonstrate that the superconducting diode effect can serve as a direct signature of d-wave pairing, with the diode efficiency depending on the junction geometry and interface asymmetry.
conclusion: The proposed setup provides a new phase-sensitive technique to identify d-wave pairing in high-temperature superconductors.

title: Interaction-induced Quasicrystalline Order: Emergence Of Quasisolid And Quasisupersolid Phases
authors: Chao Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Zhang

Deterministic quasiperiodicity in quantum systems has long been associated with localization, criticality, or glassy behavior, and has therefore been believed to suppress long-range order rather than stabilize it. Here, we demonstrate the opposite: quasiperiodicity in interactions—without any quasip…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220502] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quasiperiodicity in interactions can stabilize quasicrystalline order, leading to quasisolid and quasisupersolid phases.
motivation: To challenge the conventional belief that quasiperiodicity suppresses long-range order and to explore emergent quasicrystalline phases in quantum systems.
method: The authors study a Bose-Hubbard model with quasiperiodic interactions using numerical methods such as DMRG and mean-field theory.
result: They find that interaction-induced quasiperiodicity can stabilize quasicrystalline order, resulting in novel phases with both solid and supersolid characteristics.
conclusion: Quasiperiodicity in interactions can be a mechanism for stabilizing quasicrystalline order, expanding the understanding of quantum phases.

title: Flat Bands In The ${J}_{1}\text{−}{J}_{2}\text{−}{J}_{3}$ Xxz Sawtooth Chain
authors: Vadim Ohanyan, Johannes Richter, Michael Sekania, Lucas Giambattista, Alexei Andreanov, And Marcus Kollar
abstract:
Author(s): Vadim Ohanyan, Johannes Richter, Michael Sekania, Lucas Giambattista, Alexei Andreanov, and Marcus Kollar

We consider a generalization of the XXZ model on the sawtooth spin chain with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions in which all exchange constants (symmetric, antisymmetric, and axial anisotropy) are different for the three different bonds of each triangle. We derive and resolve algebraic constraints …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214418] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies flat bands in a generalized XXZ sawtooth chain with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions.
motivation: Flat bands in frustrated spin systems can lead to exotic magnetic phases, but the paper focuses on algebraic constraints and band structure rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive and resolve algebraic constraints for the XXZ model on a sawtooth chain with three different bond types, including symmetric, antisymmetric, and axial anisotropy.
result: They find conditions for flat bands and analyze the resulting magnetic properties.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of frustrated magnetism but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Layer-dependent Control Of Spin Hall Effect In Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator
authors: Sheng Pan, Xin Chen, Hong-Fei Huang, And Jie-Xiang Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Pan, Xin Chen, Hong-Fei Huang, and Jie-Xiang Yu

The spin Hall effect (SHE), a key mechanism for generating spin currents, is typically uniform in bulk materials. In topological materials, however, the layer degree of freedom offers a novel avenue to control spin transport. Here, we demonstrate a layer-resolved SHE in the intrinsic antiferromagnet…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224416] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies layer-resolved spin Hall effect in an antiferromagnetic topological insulator, focusing on spin transport control via layer degree of freedom.
motivation: To explore how the layer degree of freedom in topological materials can be used to control spin currents, which is important for spintronics.
method: First-principles calculations and symmetry analysis to compute layer-resolved spin Hall conductivity in an intrinsic antiferromagnetic topological insulator.
result: The spin Hall effect is layer-dependent and can be tuned by the antiferromagnetic order and layer index.
conclusion: Layer degree of freedom provides a new knob for controlling spin transport in topological antiferromagnets.

title: Effect Of Charge-imbalance Potential Relaxation On The High-frequency Vortex Dynamics And Kinetic Inductance Of Superconducting Circuits
authors: R. I. Kinzibaev, V. S. Stolyarov, And A. S. Mel'nikov
abstract:
Author(s): R. I. Kinzibaev, V. S. Stolyarov, and A. S. Mel'nikov

We show that relaxation of the charge-imbalance potential plays a key role in the retarded dynamics of Abrikosov vortices in a type-II superconducting sample carrying a microwave current. Starting from the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations we derive the vortex equation of motion accounting fo…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224507] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the effect of charge-imbalance potential relaxation on high-frequency vortex dynamics and kinetic inductance in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Understanding vortex dynamics in type-II superconductors under microwave currents is important for applications in superconducting circuits, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors derive the vortex equation of motion from time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau equations, incorporating charge-imbalance potential relaxation.
result: They show that charge-imbalance relaxation plays a key role in the retarded dynamics of Abrikosov vortices.
conclusion: The findings are relevant for understanding kinetic inductance and high-frequency behavior in superconducting circuits, but do not advance the user's research directions.

title: Quantum Tunneling Driven Giant Electric Field Gradients In Plasmonic Cavities
authors: Chao Meng, Zhonglin Xie, Yueweiying Wang, Fanfan Lu, Ting Mei, And Wending Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Meng, Zhonglin Xie, Yueweiying Wang, Fanfan Lu, Ting Mei, and Wending Zhang

Quantum tunneling suppresses extreme nanofocusing in plasmonic cavities while significantly enhancing the electric field gradient. This study employs a plasmonic cavity to drive multipolar Raman scattering of asymmetric thiobenzonitrile, directly observing this phenomenon via the quadrupole-to-dipol…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235108] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum tunneling in plasmonic cavities and its effect on electric field gradients, using multipolar Raman scattering to observe the phenomenon.
motivation: To understand how quantum tunneling affects extreme nanofocusing in plasmonic cavities and to demonstrate enhanced electric field gradients.
method: A plasmonic cavity is used to drive multipolar Raman scattering of asymmetric thiobenzonitrile, and the quadrupole-to-dipole ratio is analyzed.
result: Quantum tunneling suppresses extreme nanofocusing but significantly enhances the electric field gradient.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into quantum effects in plasmonic systems and their potential for sensing or spectroscopy.

title: Impact Of Multiband Effects On non-Fermi-liquid Transport Phenomena In Bilayer Nickelates
authors: Seiichiro Onari, Daisuke Inoue, Rina Tazai, Youichi Yamakawa, And Hiroshi Kontani
abstract:
