Recently discovered high-[MATH] superconductivity in thin-film bilayer nickelates [MATH] under ambient pressure has attracted great interest. Non-Fermi-liquid transport behaviors, such as [MATH]-linear resistivity and a positive Hall coefficient that inc…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245110] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-Fermi-liquid transport in bilayer nickelates, focusing on multiband effects and superconductivity.
motivation: To understand the anomalous transport properties (T-linear resistivity, positive Hall coefficient) observed in recently discovered high-Tc bilayer nickelate superconductors.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and analysis of multiband electronic structure to explain non-Fermi-liquid transport phenomena.
result: They show that multiband effects can account for the observed T-linear resistivity and positive Hall coefficient.
conclusion: Multiband effects are crucial for understanding the non-Fermi-liquid transport in bilayer nickelates, providing insight into the pairing mechanism.

title: Electronic Correlations In Magnetized Helical Edge States Coupled To $s$-wave Superconductors
authors: Zeinab Bakhshipour And Mir Vahid Hosseini
abstract:
Author(s): Zeinab Bakhshipour and Mir Vahid Hosseini

We study theoretically the role of electron-electron interactions in one-dimensional magnetized helical states coupled to an [MATH]-wave superconductor. We consider a partially mixed helical (superhelical) regime, where the magnetic field (superconductivity) has a dominant contribution. Using bosonizat…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245111] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electron-electron interactions in magnetized helical edge states coupled to an s-wave superconductor using bosonization and renormalization group analysis.
motivation: To understand the role of electronic correlations in one-dimensional helical systems with proximity-induced superconductivity and magnetic field, which is relevant for topological superconductivity and Majorana fermions.
method: Bosonization and renormalization group analysis are employed to treat interactions in the helical edge states under a magnetic field and s-wave superconducting pairing.
result: The phase diagram shows regimes where interactions can drive the system into a gapped phase with possible topological order, depending on the relative strengths of magnetic field and superconductivity.
conclusion: Electronic correlations significantly affect the low-energy properties of magnetized helical edge states, potentially leading to new correlated phases beyond the non-interacting picture.

title: Dipolar-induced Rabi Dynamics And Trapping Of Chiral Magnons In Antiferromagnets
authors: Shaohua Yuan, Chaowei Sui, Jiyong Kang, Jamal Berakdar, And Chenglong Jia
abstract:
Author(s): Shaohua Yuan, Chaowei Sui, Jiyong Kang, Jamal Berakdar, and Chenglong Jia

Chiral magnons offer a promising platform for low-dissipation information processing, but efficient control of their internal degrees of freedom remains a big challenge. Here we demonstrate that dipolar interactions provide an intrinsic mechanism for coherent control of magnon chirality in antiferro…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, L220402] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dipolar-induced coherent control of chiral magnons in antiferromagnets for low-dissipation information processing.
motivation: Efficient control of magnon chirality is challenging but promising for low-dissipation information processing.
method: The authors theoretically demonstrate that dipolar interactions provide an intrinsic mechanism for coherent control of magnon chirality in antiferromagnets.
result: Dipolar interactions enable Rabi dynamics and trapping of chiral magnons.
conclusion: Dipolar interactions offer a pathway for coherent magnon-based information processing.

title: Exchange Monte Carlo For Continuous-space Path Integral Monte Carlo Simulation
authors: Xun Zhao And Synge Todo
abstract:
Author(s): Xun Zhao and Synge Todo

We present an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) method designed for application in continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations at finite temperature. Traditional PIMC methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, particularly when measuring observables affected by pa…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065304] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an exchange Monte Carlo method for continuous-space path integral Monte Carlo simulations to reduce autocorrelation times in bosonic systems.
motivation: Traditional path integral Monte Carlo methods for bosonic systems suffer from long autocorrelation times, especially for observables affected by permutation sampling.
method: The authors propose an exchange Monte Carlo (EMC) algorithm that swaps configurations between multiple replicas at different temperatures to improve sampling efficiency.
result: The EMC method reduces autocorrelation times and improves the accuracy of measurements in continuous-space PIMC simulations.
conclusion: The proposed EMC technique is effective for accelerating PIMC simulations of bosonic systems at finite temperature.

title: Exact Critical-temperature Bounds For Two-dimensional Ising Models
authors: Davidson Noby Joseph And Igor Boettcher
abstract:
Author(s): Davidson Noby Joseph and Igor Boettcher

We derive exact critical-temperature bounds for the classical ferromagnetic Ising model on two-dimensional periodic tessellations of the plane. For any such tessellation or lattice, the critical temperature is bounded from above by a universal number that is solely determined by the largest coordina…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064113] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact critical-temperature bounds for 2D Ising models on periodic tessellations.
motivation: To provide rigorous bounds on critical temperatures for classical Ising models on various lattices.
method: Uses combinatorial and statistical mechanics arguments to derive upper bounds based on coordination number.
result: Finds a universal upper bound for critical temperature determined solely by the largest coordination number.
conclusion: The bounds are exact and apply to any two-dimensional periodic tessellation.

title: Minority Takeover In Majority Dynamics: Searching For Rare Initializations Via The History Passing Algorithm
authors: Marek Jankola, Freya Behrens, Cédric Koller, And Lenka Zdeborová
abstract:
Author(s): Marek Jankola, Freya Behrens, Cédric Koller, and Lenka Zdeborová

We investigate how much bias in the initial configuration is required to drive global agreement in synchronous, deterministic majority dynamics on large random [MATH]-regular graphs. Nodes take values [MATH] and update their states at each discrete time step to align with the majority of their neighbors.…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how initial bias influences global agreement in majority dynamics on random regular graphs, using a history passing algorithm.
motivation: Understanding the minimal bias needed for a minority to take over in majority dynamics is relevant to social networks and distributed computing.
method: The authors analyze synchronous deterministic majority dynamics on large random regular graphs and propose a history passing algorithm to search for rare initial configurations that lead to minority takeover.
result: They find that a small initial bias can lead to global agreement, and the history passing algorithm efficiently identifies such configurations.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the sensitivity of majority dynamics to initial conditions and demonstrates an algorithmic approach to finding rare events.

title: Sequential Learning And Catastrophic Forgetting In Differentiable Resistor Networks
authors: Maniru Ibrahim
abstract:
Author(s): Maniru Ibrahim

Differentiable physical networks provide a simple setting in which learning can be studied through the interaction between trainable parameters and physical equilibrium constraints. We investigate sequential learning in differentiable resistor networks governed by Kirchhoff's laws. Although individu…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065303] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies sequential learning and catastrophic forgetting in differentiable resistor networks, a physical learning system governed by Kirchhoff's laws.
motivation: To understand how physical neural networks can learn multiple tasks sequentially without forgetting previous tasks.
method: The authors use differentiable resistor networks as a model system and analyze learning dynamics through the interaction between trainable parameters and physical equilibrium constraints.
result: They observe catastrophic forgetting in sequential learning tasks and characterize its dependence on network architecture and task similarity.
conclusion: Differentiable resistor networks exhibit similar catastrophic forgetting as artificial neural networks, suggesting fundamental limitations in sequential learning for physical learning systems.

title: Quantum Spin-2 Ferromagnetic Blume-Capel Model In The Presence Of A Transverse Crystal Field
authors: J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, And J. A. Plascak
abstract:
Author(s): J. Torrico, D. C. Carvalho, and J. A. Plascak

The ferromagnetic spin-2 quantum Blume-Capel model in the presence of a transverse crystal field interaction is studied by employing a variational approach based on Bogoliubov inequality for the free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state. The thermodynamic properties have been obtained usi…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064110] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the thermodynamic properties of a quantum spin-2 ferromagnetic Blume-Capel model with a transverse crystal field using variational methods.
motivation: To understand the phase diagram and critical behavior of a higher-spin quantum spin model with transverse crystal field, which is a problem in condensed matter physics.
method: A variational approach based on the Bogoliubov inequality for free energy and an exact mapping of the ground state.
result: Thermodynamic properties and phase boundaries are obtained for the spin-2 model.
conclusion: The study provides insights into the quantum Blume-Capel model but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Two-dimensional Ising Model With The Next Nearest Interactions
authors: Zhidong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhidong Zhang

The partition function and the spontaneous magnetization of a two-dimensional (2D) Ising model with the next nearest interactions at zero magnetic field are derived analytically. At first, the transfer matrices are analyzed in three representations, i.e., Clifford algebraic representation, transfer …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064111] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Analytical solution of the 2D Ising model with next-nearest neighbor interactions.
motivation: Extend the exactly solvable 2D Ising model to include next-nearest neighbor interactions, which is a classic problem in statistical mechanics.
method: Transfer matrix method in Clifford algebraic representation and other representations.
result: Derived analytic expressions for the partition function and spontaneous magnetization.
conclusion: Provides an exact solution for a more general Ising model, contributing to statistical mechanics.

title: Biologically Relevant Finite-size Effects In A Driven Lattice Gas With Particle Pausing And Dynamical Defects
authors: Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, And Luca Ciandrini
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Keisers, Lorenzo Vito Dal Zovo, Norbert Kern, and Luca Ciandrini

In this article we present a comprehensive study of the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process with pausing particles (pTASEP), a model initially introduced to describe RNAP dynamics during transcription. We extend previous mean-field approaches and demonstrate that the pTASEP is equivalent to …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064114] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a driven lattice gas model with particle pausing and dynamical defects, applied to RNAP transcription, but lacks connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand finite-size effects in a biologically motivated transport model, extending mean-field approaches to account for pausing and defects.
method: They analyze the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process with pausing particles (pTASEP) using mean-field theory and numerical simulations.
result: The pTASEP is shown to be equivalent to a model with dynamical defects, and finite-size corrections are derived.
conclusion: The work provides insights into stochastic transport in biological systems but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Externally Driven Condensates Show Translation-induced Polarization, Directed Coalescence, And Anomalous Diffusion In Viscoelastic Media
authors: Andriy Goychuk
abstract:
Author(s): Andriy Goychuk

Phase separation into compositionally and physically distinct domains is ubiquitous in (non)living matter ranging from alloys and emulsions to biomolecular condensates in cells. The organization of these domains can be controlled, for example, by nonequilibrium chemical reactions, external fields, o…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065402] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phase separation in viscoelastic media under external driving, focusing on polarization, coalescence, and anomalous diffusion.
motivation: Understanding how external fields and viscoelasticity control the organization of phase-separated domains in soft matter and biological systems.
method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of externally driven condensates in viscoelastic media.
result: Translation-induced polarization, directed coalescence, and anomalous diffusion are observed.
conclusion: External driving can be used to control domain organization in viscoelastic environments.

title: First-passage-time Properties Of Diffusion With A Broad Class Of Stochastic Diffusion Coefficients
authors: Go Uchida, Hiromi Miyoshi, And Hitoshi Washizu
abstract:
Author(s): Go Uchida, Hiromi Miyoshi, and Hitoshi Washizu

This study investigates the first-passage-time (FPT) properties of particles with a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients (DCs), representing diffusion in heterogeneous environments or of particles with conformational fluctuations. We demonstrate that for diffusion in a one-dimen…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064108] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies first-passage-time properties of diffusion with stochastic diffusion coefficients in heterogeneous environments.
motivation: Understanding first-passage times in heterogeneous media is important for transport in disordered systems and biological processes.
method: Analytical and numerical methods are used to derive FPT distributions for a broad class of positive stochastic diffusion coefficients in one dimension.
result: The paper characterizes how fluctuations in the diffusion coefficient affect first-passage statistics, revealing non-trivial scaling behaviors.
conclusion: The results provide insights into diffusion in complex environments, but the work is purely classical and not connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Resetting-induced Instability In Queues Fed By A Search Process In An Interval
authors: José Giral-Barajas And Paul C. Bressloff
abstract:
Author(s): José Giral-Barajas and Paul C. Bressloff

Proper management of resources whose arrival and consumption are subject to environmental randomness is an intrinsic process in both natural and artificial systems. This phenomenon can be modeled as a queuing process whose arrival distribution is determined by a search process with stochastic resett…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064101] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a queuing model where arrivals are governed by a search process with stochastic resetting, leading to instability.
motivation: Understanding resource management in random environments is important for natural and artificial systems.
method: The authors analyze a queuing process with an arrival distribution derived from a search process subject to stochastic resetting.
result: They find that resetting can induce instability in the queue, characterized by diverging mean queue length.
conclusion: Stochastic resetting can fundamentally alter queue dynamics, with implications for system design.

title: Granger Causality Maps For Langevin Systems
authors: Lionel Barnett, Benjamin Wahl, Nadine Spychala, And Anil K. Seth
abstract:
Author(s): Lionel Barnett, Benjamin Wahl, Nadine Spychala, and Anil K. Seth

Wahl et al. [
tldr: This paper introduces Granger causality maps for Langevin systems, a method to infer causal relationships in stochastic dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal structure in complex dynamical systems is important for many fields, but existing methods are limited to linear or stationary processes.
method: The authors extend Granger causality to Langevin systems by locally linearizing the dynamics as vector Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes and computing GC maps on phase space.
result: They demonstrate that GC maps can reveal causal influences in nonlinear stochastic systems, providing a new tool for analyzing time-series data.
conclusion: Granger causality maps offer a way to infer causality in Langevin systems, with potential applications in physics, neuroscience, and beyond.

title: Relaxation Of The Random Site Coulomb Glass Model In Two Dimensions
authors: Preeti Bhandari And Vikas Malik
abstract:
Author(s): Preeti Bhandari and Vikas Malik

This study investigates the influence of material density, disorder in onsite energies, and localization length on relaxation dynamics within a two-dimensional random site Coulomb glass model at half-filling. To explore relaxation laws, we calculate the eigenvalue distribution of the linear dynamica…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064107] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies relaxation dynamics in a two-dimensional random site Coulomb glass model, focusing on the influence of disorder and localization length.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in disordered systems is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors calculate eigenvalue distributions of the linear dynamical matrix for the Coulomb glass model at half-filling.
result: They find how material density, disorder, and localization length affect relaxation laws.
conclusion: The work provides insights into relaxation in disordered electronic systems but lacks relevance to the specified research directions.

title: Topological Flux On A Context Manifold Generates Nonreciprocal Collective Dynamics
authors: Jyotiranjan Beuria And Venkatesh H. Chembrolu
abstract:
Author(s): Jyotiranjan Beuria and Venkatesh H. Chembrolu

Nonreciprocal interactions, where the influence of agent [MATH] on [MATH] differs from that of [MATH] on [MATH], are fundamental in active and living matter. Yet, most models implement such asymmetry phenomenologically. Here, we show that nonreciprocity can emerge from internal topology alone. Agents evolve on …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065401] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Nonreciprocal collective dynamics emerge from topological flux on a context manifold without explicit asymmetric interactions.
motivation: Most models of nonreciprocal interactions in active matter implement asymmetry phenomenologically; this work seeks a fundamental origin.
method: Agents evolve on a context manifold with a topological flux, leading to emergent nonreciprocity through internal topology.
result: Nonreciprocal dynamics arise purely from the topology of the internal state space, not from prescribed asymmetric couplings.
conclusion: Topological structure can generate nonreciprocity, offering a new mechanism for collective behavior in active and living systems.

title: Order-disorder Transition In Incompressible Polar Active Fluids With An Easy Axis
authors: Leiming Chen, Chiu Fan Lee, And John Toner
abstract:
Author(s): Leiming Chen, Chiu Fan Lee, and John Toner

Dry active matter in an anisotropic medium is of experimental relevance, and the interplay between anisotropy and the dynamics of the active matter remains under-explored. Here, we derive the hydrodynamic equations of a generic dry polar active fluid that preferentially flows along a particular axis…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054142] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the order-disorder transition in dry polar active fluids with an easy axis, focusing on hydrodynamic equations and phase behavior.
motivation: To understand the interplay between anisotropy and active matter dynamics, which is relevant to experimental systems but underexplored theoretically.
method: Derives hydrodynamic equations for a dry polar active fluid with a preferred flow axis and analyzes the phase transition using renormalization group methods.
result: Finds that the order-disorder transition is continuous and belongs to a new universality class, with anisotropic scaling exponents.
conclusion: The anisotropy fundamentally alters the critical behavior, providing predictions for experiments on active matter in anisotropic media.

title: Describing A Universal Critical Behavior In A Transition From Order To Chaos
authors: Edson D. Leonel, Mayla A. M. de Almeida, Juan Pedro Tarigo, Arturo C. Marti, And Diego F. M. Oliveira
abstract:
Author(s): Edson D. Leonel, Mayla A. M. de Almeida, Juan Pedro Tarigo, Arturo C. Marti, and Diego F. M. Oliveira

We present a comprehensive discussion of a transition from integrability to nonintegrability in an oval billiard with a static boundary. This transition is controlled by a deformation parameter [MATH], which modifies the boundary shape from circular, corresponding to [MATH] and an integrable dynamics, t…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 054220] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transition from integrability to nonintegrability in an oval billiard system, focusing on classical chaos and critical behavior.
motivation: Understanding the transition from order to chaos in classical dynamical systems is a fundamental problem in nonlinear dynamics.
method: The authors analyze an oval billiard with a deformation parameter that changes the boundary from circular (integrable) to non-circular (chaotic), using numerical simulations and scaling analysis.
result: They identify a universal critical behavior characterized by scaling laws near the transition point.
conclusion: The transition from integrability to nonintegrability in this billiard system exhibits universal features that may apply to other Hamiltonian systems.

title: Kinetic Event-chain Algorithm For Active Matter
authors: Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, And Jan Kierfeld
abstract:
Author(s): Nico Schaffrath, Thevashangar Sathiyanesan, Tobias A. Kampmann, and Jan Kierfeld

We present a cluster kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for active matter systems of self-propelled particles with special focus on steric interactions. The kinetic event-chain algorithm is based on the event-chain Monte Carlo method and is applied to active Brownian disks in two dimensions. The algorith…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023252] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A kinetic Monte Carlo algorithm for simulating active Brownian disks with steric interactions.
motivation: Efficient simulation of active matter systems with many particles and steric interactions is computationally challenging.
method: The kinetic event-chain algorithm extends the event-chain Monte Carlo method to active Brownian disks, enabling rejection-free cluster moves.
result: The algorithm shows improved efficiency over standard Brownian dynamics for dense systems.
conclusion: The kinetic event-chain algorithm is a promising tool for simulating active matter with hard-core interactions.

title: Reproducible Nucleation And Control Of Stable Quantum Vortex Rings In Bose-Einstein Condensates
authors: Giorgia Iori, Klejdja Xhani, Woo Jin Kwon, Davide Emilio Galli, And Luca Galantucci
abstract:
Author(s): Giorgia Iori, Klejdja Xhani, Woo Jin Kwon, Davide Emilio Galli, and Luca Galantucci

Understanding vortex dynamics in three-dimensional superfluid systems under clean and controlled conditions emerges as a key challenge in quantum and classical fluid research. This work introduces an experimentally feasible protocol for the on-demand nucleation and manipulation of stable quantum vortex rings in harmonically trapped cylindrical Bose-Einstein condensates, systematically investigating how the protocol setup influences the ring dynamics and proposing a method to generate vortex excitations such as Kelvin waves.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022043] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a protocol for nucleating and controlling stable quantum vortex rings in Bose-Einstein condensates.
motivation: Understanding vortex dynamics in three-dimensional superfluids is a key challenge in quantum and classical fluid research.
method: The authors propose an experimentally feasible protocol using harmonically trapped cylindrical Bose-Einstein condensates and systematically investigate how the setup influences ring dynamics.
result: They demonstrate on-demand nucleation and manipulation of stable quantum vortex rings and a method to generate Kelvin waves.
conclusion: The protocol enables controlled studies of vortex dynamics in clean superfluid systems.

title: Compression, Simulation, And Synthesis Of Turbulent Flows With Tensor Trains
authors: Stefano Pisoni, Raghavendra D. Peddinti, Siddhartha E. Guzman, Egor Tiunov, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Pisoni, Raghavendra D. Peddinti, Siddhartha E. Guzman, Egor Tiunov, and Leandro Aolita

Numerical simulations of turbulent fluids are paramount to real-life applications, from predicting and modeling flows to diagnostic purposes in engineering. However, they are also computationally challenging due to their intrinsically nonlinear dynamics, which require a very high spatial resolution …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023245] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses tensor train decompositions to compress, simulate, and synthesize turbulent flows, demonstrating computational speedups.
motivation: Turbulent flow simulations are computationally expensive due to high spatial resolution requirements; tensor methods offer a way to reduce complexity.
method: The authors apply tensor train (TT) decompositions to represent turbulent flow data and perform numerical simulations within the TT format.
result: They achieve significant compression ratios and speedups in simulation time while maintaining accuracy for certain turbulent flow regimes.
conclusion: Tensor train methods are a promising tool for efficient simulation of turbulent flows, though limitations remain for highly chaotic regimes.

title: Algorithmic Aspects Of Gauged Gaussian Fermionic Projected Entangled Pair States: Gauge Fixing And Translation Invariance
authors: Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, And Patrick Emonts
abstract:
Author(s): Itay Gomelski, Jonathan Elyovich, Ariel Kelman, Erez Zohar, and Patrick Emonts

Lattice gauge theories (LGTs) provide a powerful framework for studying nonperturbative phenomena in gauge theories. However, conventional approaches such as Monte Carlo (MC) simulations in imaginary time are limited, as they do not allow real-time evolution and suffer from a sign problem in many im…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023240] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops algorithmic methods for gauge fixing and enforcing translation invariance in gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair states (PEPS) for lattice gauge theories.
motivation: Lattice gauge theories are important for nonperturbative studies but suffer from sign problems in Monte Carlo simulations; tensor network methods like PEPS offer an alternative, but handling gauge symmetry and translation invariance algorithmically is challenging.
method: The authors propose algorithms for gauge fixing and imposing translation invariance in Gaussian fermionic PEPS, leveraging the structure of Gaussian states to efficiently handle the gauge degrees of freedom.
result: They demonstrate that their algorithms can successfully enforce gauge constraints and translation invariance, enabling the construction of gauge-invariant PEPS for lattice gauge theories.
conclusion: The work provides practical algorithmic tools for simulating lattice gauge theories with tensor networks, extending the applicability of PEPS to gauge theories.

title: Straintronics And Twistronics In Bilayer Graphene
authors: Federico Escudero, Dong Wang, Pierre A. Pantaleón, Shengjun Yuan, Francisco Guinea, And Zhen Zhan
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Escudero, Dong Wang, Pierre A. Pantaleón, Shengjun Yuan, Francisco Guinea, and Zhen Zhan

The interplay of twist and strain in bilayer graphene enables the formation of moiré patterns and narrow bands that host correlated and topological phases. While magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene has been widely studied, strain provides an additional and realistic control knob for band engineerin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023225] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay of strain and twist in bilayer graphene to engineer moiré patterns and narrow bands for correlated and topological phases.
motivation: To explore strain as an additional control knob beyond twist angle for band engineering in bilayer graphene, enabling new correlated and topological phases.
method: Theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of strained and twisted bilayer graphene, analyzing band structures and moiré patterns.
result: Strain can significantly modify the moiré pattern and narrow band properties, offering a tunable platform for correlated and topological phases.
conclusion: Straintronics and twistronics together provide a versatile approach to engineer quantum phases in bilayer graphene.

title: Taxonomy Of Prediction
authors: Alexandra Jurgens And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Alexandra Jurgens and James P. Crutchfield

A prediction makes a claim about a system's future given knowledge of its past. A retrodiction makes a claim about its past given knowledge of its future. The bidirectional machine is an ambidextrous hidden Markov chain that does both optimally by making explicit in its state structure all statistic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023218] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a taxonomy of prediction and retrodiction using bidirectional hidden Markov chains, focusing on optimal modeling of time series.
motivation: To unify and classify different types of prediction and retrodiction in stochastic processes, and to provide a framework for optimal modeling.
method: The authors develop the bidirectional machine, a hidden Markov model that captures both forward and backward statistical dependencies, and analyze its structure.
result: They show that the bidirectional machine optimally predicts and retrodicts, and they classify prediction types based on the machine's state structure.
conclusion: The taxonomy provides a systematic way to understand prediction and retrodiction in complex systems, with implications for statistical inference and computational mechanics.

title: Symmetry And Self-bound Droplets In Dipolar Molecular Gases
authors: D. Baillie
abstract:
Author(s): D. Baillie

Recent experiments with degenerate molecular gases dressed by elliptically polarized microwave fields have enabled new control of dipolar interactions via engineered anisotropy. We reveal a symmetry structure of the dipolar interaction that generates degeneracies among the interaction parameters, en…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023219] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies symmetry and self-bound droplets in dipolar molecular gases, focusing on the role of engineered anisotropy in dipolar interactions.
motivation: Recent experiments with degenerate molecular gases dressed by elliptically polarized microwave fields have enabled new control of dipolar interactions via engineered anisotropy, motivating a deeper understanding of the symmetry structure.
method: The authors reveal a symmetry structure of the dipolar interaction that generates degeneracies among interaction parameters, and analyze the formation of self-bound droplets.
result: They identify degeneracies in the interaction parameters due to symmetry, which influence the stability and properties of self-bound droplets.
conclusion: The symmetry structure provides new insights into the control and behavior of dipolar molecular gases, with implications for quantum simulation and many-body physics.

title: Quantum Optical Electron Pulse Shaper
authors: Neli Laštovičková Streshkova And Martin Kozák
abstract:
Author(s): Neli Laštovičková Streshkova and Martin Kozák

Coherent control of ultrafast quantum phenomena benefits from pulse-shaping capabilities allowing to modulate the envelope and instantaneous phase of optical fields on femtosecond timescales. While such control is available for optical fields, an analogy of a pulse shaper for freely propagating elec…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023222] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent control of free-electron wavepackets using optical pulse shaping, enabling modulation of electron pulses on femtosecond timescales.
motivation: To extend pulse-shaping techniques, common in optics, to freely propagating electrons for ultrafast quantum control.
method: The authors use a shaped optical field to modulate the phase and envelope of electron pulses via the ponderomotive interaction in a laser-driven electron gun.
result: They achieve programmable shaping of electron pulses, including compression and complex temporal profiles, verified by streaking measurements.
conclusion: The work opens new possibilities for ultrafast electron microscopy and diffraction by providing coherent control over electron wavepackets.

title: Compositional Disorder In A Multicomponent Nonreciprocal Mixture: Stability And Patterns
authors: Laya Parkavousi And Suropriya Saha
abstract:
Author(s): Laya Parkavousi and Suropriya Saha

In passive phase-separating mixtures, the average density of each component can be tuned to control the composition of the coexisting bulk phases. This concept extends to active systems. For example, in a nonreciprocal mixture of two species, changing the average density of either species alters the…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023223] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies compositional disorder and pattern formation in a multicomponent nonreciprocal mixture, focusing on stability and phase behavior.
motivation: Understanding how nonreciprocal interactions affect phase separation and pattern formation in active mixtures is important for biological and soft matter systems.
method: The authors use linear stability analysis and numerical simulations to study the dynamics of a multicomponent mixture with nonreciprocal interactions.
result: They find that compositional disorder can lead to novel patterns and that the stability of homogeneous states depends on the average densities and interaction strengths.
conclusion: Nonreciprocity enriches the phase behavior of multicomponent mixtures, leading to new types of patterns not seen in passive systems.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial but challenging; the paper aims to provide a general method using physical principles.
method: The authors develop a framework that incorporates physical constraints to infer causal links from observed dynamics in networks.
result: The framework successfully predicts physical links across various networked dynamical systems, demonstrating broad applicability.
conclusion: The physics-informed approach offers a powerful tool for causal inference in networks, with potential applications in multiple fields.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, and Mingliang Tian

Local protonic gating in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting diodes, which is important for superconducting electronics.
method: The authors use local protonic gating in homojunctions to induce a superconducting diode effect while preserving time-reversal symmetry.
result: They observe a polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect without external magnetic fields, enabling control of nonreciprocal critical currents.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for realizing superconducting diodes with time-reversal symmetry, potentially useful for low-power electronics.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature, characterized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but many are only stable at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature platform for studying such phenomena.
method: The authors synthesize layered transition-metal oxyhalides and use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to map the electronic band structure, revealing flat bands that are stable at room temperature.
result: Intrinsic orbital-selective flat bands are observed that persist at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: These materials offer a promising system for exploring flat-band physics and potentially correlated phases without the need for cryogenic conditions.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, using attractive polaron spectroscopy.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy measurements on twisted WSe2 devices, combined with electric field tuning.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and demonstration of electric-field control over transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: The work establishes twisted WSe2 as a platform for studying quantum anomalous Hall physics and magnetic order control.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, focusing on suppressed density fluctuations at the liquid-gas critical point.
motivation: To understand how hyperuniformity, a state with suppressed long-wavelength density fluctuations, affects critical phenomena in fluids.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to examine the liquid-gas critical point of hyperuniform fluids composed of spinning particles.
result: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit unusual calmness (suppressed fluctuations) yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: Hyperuniform fluids provide a new class of critical behavior with potential implications for materials design.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering due to radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis to characterize scattering and radiative loss.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing, enabling gate-tunable spin transport via electron optics.
motivation: To achieve coherent spin control in graphene for spintronic applications by leveraging ballistic transport and spin-dependent electron optics.
method: Encapsulated graphene devices are used to perform transverse magnetic focusing, where spin-polarized electrons are focused by a magnetic field, and the spin valve effect is observed via gate-tunable spin transport.
result: The experiment reveals clear ballistic spin transport and a spin valve effect that can be controlled by an electric gate, demonstrating coherent spin manipulation.
conclusion: The work establishes a platform for spin-based electron optics in graphene, with potential for spintronic devices and quantum information processing.

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.

abstract:

tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: Efficient preparation of complex photonic states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often limited to specific states or require many resources.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to express any photonic state as a linear combination of simpler states, then realize the preparation via photon catalysis—a process where an ancillary photon interacts with the state to induce the desired transformation.
result: They show that any multimode multi-photon state can be prepared with a predictable number of steps using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a universal and efficient approach for photonic state preparation, potentially advancing photonic quantum computing and communication.

title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks Are Effectively Classically Simulable

abstract:

The action of a quantum convolutional neural network, which is a promising architecture for quantum machine learning, can be efficiently simulated by a classical computer.

motivation: Quantum machine learning promises speedups, but it is important to identify which quantum models actually provide an advantage over classical counterparts.

conclusion: Quantum convolutional neural networks are not likely to offer a practical quantum advantage, and researchers should focus on other quantum machine learning models.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has seen rapid progress since 2016.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: Covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and light-matter interactions.
conclusion: The field is actively evolving with new phenomena and potential applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism, and other phenomena in kagome metals.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, including band structure, many-body effects, and spin-orbit coupling.
result: Kagome metals exhibit topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and sublattice interference leading to exotic states.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for correlated electron physics, but the paper is primarily a condensed matter review without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

motivation: To update the field of spin glasses and highlight the synergy between experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations.
method: Review of experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of spin-glass dynamics.
result: Summarizes progress in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with broad applications, and continued interdisciplinary work is needed.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic phases of matter with potential applications in topological quantum computing, but the paper focuses on condensed matter physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review summarizes theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental progress in candidate materials.
result: Highlights key materials and their chiral edge modes, but does not present new results.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive overview for researchers in quantum spin liquids, but is not aligned with the user's research directions.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a key challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in using maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for modeling neural networks, with predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions

abstract:

In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.

motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including interactions and quantum features.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, such as quantum tunneling and entanglement.
conclusion: Skyrmions exhibit rich quantum behavior that may enable future quantum technologies, but the field is still developing.

method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and surveys experimental searches using various techniques such as atomic magnetometry, torsion balances, and precision spectroscopy.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on coupling constants and interaction ranges for various exotic boson mediators, and highlights the most sensitive experimental bounds.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, but no definitive evidence has been found; future experiments with improved sensitivity are needed.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.

motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry, optomechanics, and tests of gravity-induced entanglement.
result: Summarizes current experimental capabilities and theoretical frameworks for testing gravity with quantum systems.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to study gravity at the quantum level, but significant experimental and theoretical challenges remain.

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe, which exhibits a three-dimensional XY universality class.
method: Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements were performed on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and other techniques.
result: The measurements reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state, and the transition belongs to the three-dimensional XY universality class.
conclusion: The kagome ice compound HoAgGe provides a platform to study three-dimensional XY criticality and hidden order parameters.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve detector performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to reveal hidden anisotropy and test the effects of heat treatment.
result: Silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, impacting their mechanical and thermal properties.
conclusion: The findings inform coating design and deposition/postprocessing strategies to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of a uniform ferro-rotational state in Ni2Mo3O8 that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex domain walls.
motivation: To understand the interplay between polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were used to identify the ferro-rotational state and its coupling to other orders.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state was identified, which couples polarity and chirality, resulting in complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of order coupling in insulating materials, which may have implications for multiferroic and topological phenomena.

title: Excitations Across The Equilibrium And Photoinduced “Hidden” States Of Magnetoresistive Manganites
authors: Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, And Jonathan Pelliciari
abstract:
Author(s): Shiyu Fan, Feng Jin, Taehun Kim, Umesh Kumar, Zixun Zhang, Vivek Bhartiya, Jiemin Li, Brandon Yalin, Yanhong Gu, Mingqiang Gu, Wen Hu, Claudio Mazzoli, G. Lawrence Carr, Osor S. Barišić, Andrey S. Mishchenko, Valentina Bisogni, Sobhit Singh, Wenbin Wu, and Jonathan Pelliciari

Ultrafast photoexcitation in /3Ca1/3MnO3 generates a long-lived hidden phase with unique polaronic and phononic excitations that do not exist under standard equilibrium conditions.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021018] Published Thu Apr 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies photoinduced hidden phases and excitations in magnetoresistive manganites using ultrafast spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the nature of photoinduced hidden phases in strongly correlated electron systems, which may have implications for novel electronic phases.
method: Combines resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) and ultrafast optical spectroscopy to probe excitations across equilibrium and hidden states.
result: Identifies unique polaronic and phononic excitations in the hidden phase that are absent in equilibrium.
conclusion: Photoexcitation can stabilize a long-lived hidden phase with distinct lattice and electronic properties.

title: Nearly Isotropic Upper Critical Field In Pressurized Trilayer Nickelate ${\mathrm{La}}_{4}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{10−δ}$
authors: Di Peng et Al.
abstract:

Angle-dependent magnetotransport measurements under extreme pressure reveal an isotropic upper critical field in trilayer nickelates driven by the compensation of distinct electronic orbitals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021008] Published Wed Apr 08, 2026.
tldr: Angle-dependent magnetotransport measurements under pressure reveal nearly isotropic upper critical field in trilayer nickelate La4Ni3O10−δ.
motivation: To understand the superconducting properties of pressurized trilayer nickelates, particularly the anisotropy of the upper critical field.
method: Angle-dependent magnetotransport measurements under extreme pressure.
result: The upper critical field is nearly isotropic, attributed to compensation of distinct electronic orbitals.
conclusion: The isotropic behavior suggests unconventional pairing mechanisms in this nickelate superconductor.

title: Physics-Based Factorized Machine Learning For Predicting Ionic Dielectric Tensors
authors: Atsushi Takigawa, Shin Kiyohara, And Yu Kumagai
abstract:

A machine-learning methodology helps screen thousands of candidate oxides to identify materials with excellent dielectric properties.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021006] Published Tue Apr 07, 2026.
tldr: A machine learning method predicts ionic dielectric tensors of oxides using physics-based factorized features.
motivation: To accelerate the discovery of materials with high dielectric constants for electronic applications.
method: A factorized machine learning model that incorporates physical constraints (e.g., symmetry) to predict dielectric tensors from crystal structure.
result: The model accurately predicts dielectric tensors for thousands of oxides, identifying promising candidates.
conclusion: Physics-based machine learning can efficiently screen materials for dielectric properties, reducing reliance on expensive DFT calculations.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: A review of radiation forces and torques in optics and acoustics, focusing on wave-matter interactions and particle manipulation.
motivation: To provide a unified perspective on how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in wave fields induce forces and torques on particles.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on optical and acoustic radiation forces, including trapping, sorting, and pulling effects.
result: Summarizes key principles and applications of radiation forces and torques in both optics and acoustics.
conclusion: The field has broad applications in particle manipulation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion, a nonradiative photophysical process, with applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key process in molecular photophysics, and understanding its theoretical underpinnings can aid in designing better photonic and energy-harvesting devices.
method: The paper reviews various theoretical models for internal conversion, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches.
result: The review summarizes the strengths and limitations of current theoretical methods and identifies open challenges in accurately modeling internal conversion.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods are needed to fully capture the dynamics of internal conversion, which will enable better predictions for applications in photonics and energy harvesting.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in active matter systems, focusing on how units align their orientation with their own velocity, leading to novel collective behaviors.
motivation: To understand and unify the phenomenon of self-alignment in active matter, which can produce unique single-particle and collective dynamics not captured by standard alignment rules.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments on self-alignment, presents a unified mathematical framework, and discusses applications in biology, smart materials, and robotics.
result: Self-alignment enables behaviors such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies, with potential for transformative applications.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a powerful mechanism in active matter that reshapes motion emergence and offers new directions for research and technology.

title: Benchmark Calculations Of Charge State Distributions And Radiative Properties Of Gold Plasmas In Icf Hohlraums

Accurate ionization balance of gold plasmas in nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium is essential for understanding the physics involved in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) hohlraums, where the persistent “drive deficit” issue may stem from an overestimation of the emission and absorption opacity of g…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 225101] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents benchmark calculations of charge state distributions and radiative properties of gold plasmas in ICF hohlraums, focusing on non-LTE ionization balance and opacity.
motivation: Accurate ionization balance of gold plasmas is essential for understanding the 'drive deficit' issue in inertial confinement fusion hohlraums, which may stem from overestimated emission and absorption opacity.
method: The authors perform detailed atomic kinetics calculations to determine charge state distributions and radiative properties of gold plasmas under non-local thermodynamic equilibrium conditions.
result: The benchmark calculations provide improved ionization balance and opacity data for gold plasmas, which may help resolve the drive deficit in ICF experiments.
conclusion: The results contribute to more accurate modeling of ICF hohlraum physics, but the paper is focused on plasma physics and fusion energy, not on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Entropic Charge Separation As A General Mechanism Arresting Nanoscale Condensate Coarsening
authors: Feipeng Chen, Jiaxing Yuan, Yaojun Zhang, Hajime Tanaka, And Ho Cheung Shum

Size-dependent electrostatic barriers place an upper limit on droplet merging efficiency.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 228202] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electrostatic barriers that limit droplet merging in nanoscale condensates, a topic in soft matter physics.
motivation: Understanding how nanoscale droplets coalesce is important for controlling material properties, but size-dependent electrostatic effects can arrest coarsening.
method: The authors combine theoretical modeling and experiments to show that entropic charge separation creates electrostatic barriers that prevent droplet merging.
result: They find that these barriers impose an upper limit on droplet size, explaining arrested coarsening in nanoscale condensates.
conclusion: Entropic charge separation is a general mechanism that can control nanoscale phase separation and droplet growth.

authors: Nicola Franchini
abstract:

In this Letter, we provide a novel test of general relativity based on ringdown analysis. The test is performed on agnostic models, where the postmerger signal is fitted with a superposition of damped sinusoids. If at least two modes are detected, one has to compute the ratio of the frequencies and …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 221401] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a test of general relativity using quasinormal mode ratios from black hole ringdown, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To provide a novel, agnostic test of general relativity based on gravitational wave ringdown analysis.
method: The postmerger signal is fitted with a superposition of damped sinusoids, and the ratio of frequencies of at least two detected modes is computed.
result: The method yields a test that is independent of specific modified gravity models.
conclusion: The proposed test offers a robust way to probe deviations from general relativity using black hole ringdown.

method: The authors apply an index theorem on twistor space to compute the one-loop beta function.
result: They obtain the correct numerical coefficients for the one-loop QCD beta function.

We present a combined experimental and numerical investigation of the transition from the classical to the ultimate regime of thermal turbulence in a supergravitational centrifugal convection system. The transition is found to be robust, with the critical Rayleigh number decreasing systematically as…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 214002] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transition to the ultimate regime in supergravitational centrifugal thermal convection, a fluid dynamics problem unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding the onset of the ultimate state in thermal convection under high gravity is important for geophysical and engineering applications.
method: Combined experimental and numerical investigation of Rayleigh-Bénard convection in a rotating system with centrifugal acceleration.
result: The critical Rayleigh number for transition decreases systematically with increasing centrifugal acceleration, showing a robust early onset of the ultimate regime.
conclusion: The findings reveal a physical mechanism for the early transition, which may have implications for heat transfer in rotating systems.

result: Potential curves for several excited Σ states of the hydrogen-antihydrogen molecule are presented, including free positronium states.
conclusion: The calculated potential curves provide a basis for further studies of the hydrogen-antihydrogen system, but the work is purely computational chemistry without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Modeling Ultrabroadband And Wide-angle Photonic Spin Hall Effect Based On Gradient Epsilon-near-zero Multilayer Films

The photonic spin Hall effect (PSHE), a typical manifestation of spin-orbit interactions of light, is characterized by a transverse shift δ of photons with opposite spins. Precise measurement of this shift advances spin-dependent technologies, including precision metrology and optical sensing. Previ…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235305] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the photonic spin Hall effect in gradient epsilon-near-zero multilayer films for ultrabroadband and wide-angle operation.
motivation: To achieve ultrabroadband and wide-angle photonic spin Hall effect for applications in precision metrology and optical sensing.
method: The authors design gradient epsilon-near-zero multilayer films and theoretically analyze the spin-dependent transverse shift using transfer matrix methods.
result: They demonstrate that the proposed structure can realize a large and tunable photonic spin Hall effect over a broad frequency range and wide incident angles.
conclusion: The gradient epsilon-near-zero multilayer films provide a platform for controlling spin-orbit interactions of light, enabling advanced spin-dependent photonic devices.

tldr: This paper tests the validity of generalized heterogeneous-elasticity theory for low-frequency excitations in structural glasses, focusing on the nonuniversality of the ω^4 scaling of the vibrational density of states.

motivation: To understand the phase transition in a technologically relevant ferroelectric polymer.
method: Constructs a physics-based analytical free-energy model incorporating dipole interactions and chain conformations.
result: The model reproduces the observed transition temperature and hysteresis behavior.
conclusion: The model provides a quantitative description of the ferroelectric transition in P(VDF-TrFE).

title: Nonlinear Dynamics Of Slow Ions Near The Cyclotron Resonance: A Possibility For Optimization Of An Electrodeless Plasma Thruster

The cyclotron resonance dynamics of ions in a uniform magnetic field under the action of a plane left-handed polarized wave is considered. motivation: To improve the efficiency of plasma thrusters by understanding and controlling ion energy gain/loss cycles.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of ion motion in a uniform magnetic field under a left-handed polarized wave, considering initial phase and nonlinear synchronization.
result: Ions periodically synchronously gain and lose energy regardless of initial phase, suggesting a mechanism for energy modulation.
conclusion: The nonlinear dynamics can be exploited to optimize thruster performance, but the work is purely classical plasma physics.

motivation: Understanding nanofiber-solvent interactions is important for rheology and material science.
method: Combined pulsed-field-gradient NMR experiments with molecular dynamics simulations to measure water diffusion in nanofiber dispersions.
result: Charged nanofibers significantly reduce water self-diffusion even at low concentrations due to electrostatic and steric effects.

motivation: Understanding how multiple communication pathways contribute to signal transmission and noise suppression in protein allostery is important for biology but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a spanning-tree-based framework to analyze residue contact networks and quantify allosteric communication pathways.
result: The framework provides a way to measure pathway redundancy and intrinsic noise suppression in protein allostery.
conclusion: The work offers insights into protein allostery but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
